topics.name: Genesis: overview
topics.description: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
evidence: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?

topics.name: Romans: overview
topics.description: Paul's letter to the Romans, from the greeting and the gospel theme (1:1-17) to its closing greetings and doxology (16:27).
evidence: State the letter's theme from 1:16-17
Describe the movement: sin (1-3), justification (3-5), life in Christ and the Spirit (6-8), Israel (9-11), Christian living (12-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Romans is about, using 1:16-17?

topics.name: God creates the world
topics.description: God creates the heavens and the earth, and all that fills them, in six days, and rests on the seventh.
evidence: Retell what God made on each of the six days
Say that God rested on the seventh day and blessed it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what God made on each day, and what happened on the seventh?

topics.name: Made in the image of God
topics.description: Man and woman are made in God's image and given dominion; the same truth grounds the sanctity of human life after the flood.
evidence: Explain what it means to be made in God's image using Genesis 1:26-27
Connect Genesis 9:6 to the value of human life
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Genesis 1:26-27 teaches about people, and why this matters?

topics.name: The garden of Eden
topics.description: God plants a garden, places the man in it with a command, and forms the woman as a helper fit for him.
evidence: Retell the formation of the man and the woman
State God's command about the tree (2:16-17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the garden and the one thing God told the man not to do?

topics.name: The fall
topics.description: The serpent tempts the woman; she and the man eat the fruit God forbade and hide from God.
evidence: Retell the temptation and the disobedience in order
Explain what the man and woman did when God called
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how sin entered the world in Genesis 3?

topics.name: The curse and the first promise
topics.description: God pronounces judgment, yet promises that the woman's offspring will bruise the serpent's head (3:15), and clothes the man and woman before sending them from the garden.
evidence: Name the consequences God gives in 3:14-19
Read 3:15 and say why it is called the first promise of a saviour
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the promise in Genesis 3:15?

topics.name: Cain and Abel
topics.description: Cain murders his brother Abel after God accepts Abel's offering and not his own.
evidence: Retell the story, including God's question to Cain (4:9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Cain did and how God responded?

topics.name: Noah and the flood
topics.description: God sees the wickedness of man, finds favour with Noah, and saves him and his household in the ark through the flood.
evidence: Retell why God sent the flood and how Noah and his family were saved
Say how Noah left the ark and what he did (8:20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell the story of Noah and the ark?

topics.name: God's covenant with Noah
topics.description: After the flood God establishes his covenant with Noah and every living creature and sets the rainbow as its sign.
evidence: State what God promises in 9:11
Identify the sign of the covenant (9:12-13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what God promised Noah and what the sign was?

topics.name: The tower of Babel
topics.description: The people build a city and tower; God confuses their language and scatters them.
evidence: Retell why the people built the tower and what God did
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Babel?

topics.name: God calls Abram
topics.description: God calls Abram to leave his country and promises to make him a great nation and bless all the families of the earth through him.
evidence: State the promises of 12:1-3
Say that Abram went as the LORD told him
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list what God promised Abram in Genesis 12:1-3?

topics.name: God's covenant with Abram
topics.description: God confirms his promise of offspring and land to Abram and makes a covenant with him.
evidence: Describe the promises of offspring and land
Read 15:6 and say what Abram believed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what God promised Abram in Genesis 15 and how Abram responded?

topics.name: Abram believed and it was counted as righteousness
topics.description: Genesis 15:6 records that Abram believed the LORD and it was counted to him as righteousness, the verse Paul explains in Romans 4.
evidence: Quote or paraphrase 15:6 accurately
Say who or what Abram believed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Genesis 15:6 in their own words?

topics.name: The sign of circumcision
topics.description: God appears to Abram at ninety-nine, changes his name to Abraham, and gives circumcision as the sign of the covenant.
evidence: Explain the name change (17:5)
State what circumcision signified (17:10-11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what circumcision was a sign of in Genesis 17?

topics.name: Isaac is born
topics.description: God keeps his promise: Sarah bears Isaac to Abraham in his old age.
evidence: Retell how God kept his promise
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Isaac was born?

topics.name: Abraham offers Isaac
topics.description: God tests Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac; God provides a ram in his place.
evidence: Retell the story, including 22:8 and 22:13-14
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what God provided on the mountain?

topics.name: Jacob and Esau
topics.description: Esau sells his birthright to Jacob, and Jacob later receives Isaac's blessing.
evidence: Retell the birthright and blessing episodes
Note God's word to Rebekah in 25:23
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob received the birthright and the blessing?

topics.name: Jacob's dream at Bethel
topics.description: Jacob dreams of a ladder to heaven, and the LORD renews the promise to him.
evidence: Retell the dream
State the promise in 28:13-15
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe Jacob's dream and what God promised?

topics.name: Jacob wrestles and is named Israel
topics.description: Jacob wrestles with a man until daybreak and is given the name Israel.
evidence: Retell the wrestling and the new name
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob became Israel?

topics.name: Joseph is sold by his brothers
topics.description: Joseph's brothers hate him and sell him to traders who take him to Egypt.
evidence: Retell the story from the dreams to the sale
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why Joseph's brothers sold him?

topics.name: Joseph is raised up in Egypt
topics.description: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams and is set over the land of Egypt.
evidence: Retell the dreams and what Joseph advised
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Joseph came to rule in Egypt?

topics.name: God meant it for good: providence
topics.description: Joseph tells his brothers that although they meant evil, God meant it for good (50:20); Paul teaches a similar confidence in Romans 8:28.
evidence: Explain Genesis 50:20 in context
Compare it with Romans 8:28
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Joseph meant in Genesis 50:20?

topics.name: Jacob's blessing of Judah
topics.description: Jacob blesses his sons, and says the sceptre shall not depart from Judah.
evidence: Read 49:10 and identify to whom the blessing is addressed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jacob promised Judah in Genesis 49:10?

topics.name: The gospel is the power of God
topics.description: Paul introduces himself and states the letter's theme: the gospel is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, and in it the righteousness of God is revealed.
evidence: Recite or paraphrase 1:16-17
Say what Paul calls himself in 1:1
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Romans 1:16-17?

topics.name: God's wrath against unrighteousness
topics.description: Paul says God's wrath is revealed against ungodliness and that people suppress the truth about God.
evidence: State what Paul says can be known of God from creation (1:19-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about knowing God from creation in Romans 1?

topics.name: God's impartial judgment
topics.description: God will judge each person according to his works with no partiality; Jew and Gentile alike.
evidence: Explain "there is no respect of persons with God" (2:11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Romans 2 teaches about God's judgment?

topics.name: All have sinned
topics.description: Paul gathers Old Testament testimony to show that all are under sin and that no one is justified by the works of the law.
evidence: State the conclusion of 3:19-20
Quote or paraphrase 3:23
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says every mouth is stopped (3:19)?

topics.name: Justification by faith
topics.description: The righteousness of God is through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe; we are justified freely by his grace through the redemption in Christ.
evidence: Explain "justified freely by his grace" (3:24)
Say what propitiation means in 3:25 in the passage's context
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Romans 3:21-26 says a sinner is justified?

topics.name: Abraham justified by faith
topics.description: Paul uses Abraham to show that righteousness is counted to the one who believes, before circumcision, and that Abraham is the father of all who believe.
evidence: Link Romans 4:3 to Genesis 15:6
Explain why it matters that Abraham was counted righteous before circumcision (4:9-12)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Romans 4 uses Genesis 15:6?

topics.name: Peace with God
topics.description: Justified by faith, we have peace with God through Jesus Christ; Christ died for us while we were sinners.
evidence: State what believers have according to 5:1-2
Explain 5:8
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 5:8 says about God's love?

topics.name: Adam and Christ
topics.description: As sin and death came into the world through one man, so grace and righteousness come through one man, Jesus Christ.
evidence: Compare Adam and Christ in 5:15-19
Connect 5:12 to Genesis 3
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the contrast between Adam and Christ in Romans 5?

topics.name: Dead to sin, alive to God
topics.description: Believers are united with Christ in his death and resurrection and are to consider themselves dead to sin and alive to God.
evidence: Explain what baptism pictures in 6:3-4
State 6:11
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what it means to be dead to sin and alive to God (6:11)?

topics.name: Slaves of righteousness
topics.description: Believers, freed from sin, become servants of righteousness; the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life.
evidence: Quote or paraphrase 6:23
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Romans 6:23?

topics.name: The law and sin
topics.description: Paul explains the law's relationship to sin and describes the struggle with sin in the one who delights in God's law.
evidence: Explain 7:12
Describe the struggle in 7:15-25
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Paul says the law is good for and what it cannot do (Romans 7)?

topics.name: No condemnation: life in the Spirit
topics.description: There is now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus; those led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.
evidence: State 8:1
Explain adoption in 8:14-17
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Romans 8:1 and what it means to be a son of God (8:14-15)?

topics.name: Adoption as sons
topics.description: Believers receive the Spirit of adoption and cry "Abba, Father", being heirs with Christ.
evidence: Explain "Spirit of adoption" (8:15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 8:15-17 says about being God's children?

topics.name: Called according to his purpose
topics.description: God works all things for good to those who love him, and those he foreknew he predestined, called, justified and glorified.
evidence: List the steps in 8:29-30 in order
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list the steps of Romans 8:29-30?

topics.name: Nothing can separate us from the love of God
topics.description: Paul concludes that nothing in creation can separate believers from the love of God in Christ Jesus.
evidence: Read 8:38-39 and list what Paul says cannot separate us
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the end of Romans 8?

topics.name: God's sovereign election
topics.description: Paul answers the question of Israel by pointing to God's sovereign choice, from Isaac and Jacob onward, and his mercy.
evidence: Link 9:7 to Genesis 21:12 and 9:12 to Genesis 25:23
Explain 9:15-16
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 9 says about God's choice and mercy?

topics.name: Faith comes by hearing
topics.description: Righteousness is for everyone who believes; faith comes by hearing the word of Christ.
evidence: State 10:9-10
Explain 10:17
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Romans 10:9-10 and 10:17?

topics.name: The remnant and the olive tree
topics.description: God has not cast off his people; a remnant is saved by grace, and Gentiles are grafted into the olive tree.
evidence: Explain the olive tree illustration in 11:17-24
Say how the chapter ends (11:33-36)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the olive tree picture in Romans 11?

topics.name: A living sacrifice
topics.description: In view of God's mercies, believers present their bodies as a living sacrifice, are transformed by the renewing of the mind, and live in love as members of one body.
evidence: Explain 12:1-2
List ways Paul describes love in practice (12:9-21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Romans 12:1-2?

topics.name: Governing authorities
topics.description: Paul teaches submission to governing authorities as God's servants, and sums up the law in love for neighbour.
evidence: State what Paul says about authorities (13:1-7)
Explain 13:8-10
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 13:1-7 teaches?

topics.name: The strong and the weak
topics.description: Believers are to welcome one another, not judge over disputable matters, and seek the good of their neighbour.
evidence: Explain 14:1 and 14:17
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says to treat a brother who disagrees on disputable matters?

topics.name: Closing greetings and doxology
topics.description: Paul's plans, personal greetings, a warning, and the closing benediction and doxology.
evidence: Read the doxology (16:25-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how Romans ends?

topics.name: Cain's line and the birth of Seth
topics.description: Cain builds a city and his descendants include tent-dwellers, musicians and metalworkers, while Lamech boasts of killing a man. Adam and Eve have Seth in place of Abel, and in Seth's day men begin to call on the name of the LORD.
evidence: Name some of Cain's descendants and what they were known for (4:20-22)
Contrast Lamech's words in 4:23-24 with the birth of Seth and the calling on the LORD's name in 4:25-26
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Genesis 4 ends with two family lines, Cain's and Seth's, and what is said about Seth's son Enos?

topics.name: From Adam to Noah: the first genealogy
topics.description: Genesis 5 lists ten generations from Adam to Noah, repeating that each one lived a number of years and died, except Enoch, who walked with God and was not, for God took him. Lamech names his son Noah with a hope of comfort from the cursed ground.
evidence: Point out the repeated phrase 'and he died' in the chapter and the one exception in verse 24
Explain what Lamech hoped for when he named Noah (5:29)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Genesis 5 tells us about Enoch, and why the chapter keeps repeating that each man died?

topics.name: The sons of God and the daughters of men
topics.description: As men multiply, the sons of God take wives of the daughters of men, and the LORD limits man's days to one hundred and twenty years. The text notes mighty men of renown born in those days.
evidence: Summarise what Genesis 6:1-4 reports happening and what the LORD says in 6:3
Say honestly which points in the passage are plainly stated and which are debated
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what Genesis 6:1-4 says, and explain why the identity of the 'sons of God' needs careful study of the text?

topics.name: A new start: blessing, food and the sanctity of life
topics.description: After the flood God blesses Noah and his sons, tells them to be fruitful, puts the animals under their hand, permits meat but not blood, and requires an account for the shedding of man's blood because man is made in God's image.
evidence: List what God tells Noah's family to do and what He permits and forbids in 9:1-5
Explain the reason given in 9:6 for the penalty for shedding man's blood
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why God says in Genesis 9:6 that shedding man's blood is so serious?

topics.name: Noah's vineyard and the curse on Canaan
topics.description: Noah plants a vineyard, becomes drunk and lies uncovered in his tent. Ham tells his brothers, while Shem and Japheth cover their father, and Noah then curses Canaan and blesses the LORD God of Shem.
evidence: Contrast what Ham did with what Shem and Japheth did (9:22-23)
State exactly whom Noah curses and whom he blesses (9:25-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened in Noah's tent and how Shem, Ham and Japheth each responded?

topics.name: The table of nations
topics.description: Genesis 10 traces the families of Japheth, Ham and Shem after the flood, naming nations, lands and tongues, including Nimrod's kingdom beginning at Babel. It closes by saying the nations were divided in the earth after the flood.
evidence: Name Noah's three sons and one nation or person listed under each
Find where Nimrod and Babel appear in the chapter (10:8-10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Genesis 10 teaches about where the nations came from?

topics.name: From Shem to Abram's family
topics.description: A second genealogy runs from Shem to Terah and his sons Abram, Nahor and Haran. It notes that Haran died in Ur, that Sarai was barren, and that Terah set out for Canaan but settled in Haran, where he died.
evidence: Trace the line from Shem to Abram in 11:10-26
Say what is told about Sarai in 11:30 and where Terah's journey stopped (11:31-32)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Genesis 11:10-32 introduces Abram and Sarai, and why Sarai's barrenness matters?

topics.name: Abram in Egypt
topics.description: A famine sends Abram down to Egypt, where he asks Sarai to say she is his sister for fear of being killed. Pharaoh takes her, the LORD plagues his house, and Pharaoh sends Abram away with his wife and all he had.
evidence: Explain why Abram told Sarai to say she was his sister (12:11-13)
Say who acts to rescue Sarai (12:17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what happened in Egypt and say who protected Sarai?

topics.name: Abram and Lot separate
topics.description: Abram returns to Bethel and calls on the LORD. Strife between the herdmen leads Abram to offer Lot his choice of land; Lot chooses the plain near Sodom, and the LORD then renews the promise of land and seed to Abram.
evidence: Describe how Abram settled the quarrel and what Lot chose
Say what the LORD promises Abram after Lot leaves (13:14-17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Abram handled the quarrel with Lot, and what God promised him afterward?

topics.name: Abram rescues Lot
topics.description: Four kings defeat the kings of the plain and carry off Lot with his goods. Abram arms 318 trained servants, pursues them by night and brings back Lot, the goods and the people.
evidence: Explain why Abram went to war (14:12-14)
Describe how he pursued and what he brought back (14:14-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why Abram went after the four kings and what he recovered?

topics.name: Melchizedek blesses Abram
topics.description: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, brings bread and wine and blesses Abram, who gives him tithes of all. Abram refuses the king of Sodom's goods, saying he has lifted his hand to the LORD, the most high God.
evidence: Say who Melchizedek is according to 14:18 and what he does and says
Explain why Abram refuses to take anything from the king of Sodom (14:22-23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what Melchizedek did for Abram and what Abram gave him?

topics.name: Hagar and the birth of Ishmael
topics.description: Sarai, still childless, gives her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram; Hagar conceives and is treated harshly and flees. The angel of the LORD finds her at a spring, tells her to return, promises many descendants and names her son Ishmael, and she calls God the one who sees her.
evidence: Explain how Hagar came to be Abram's wife (16:1-3)
Tell what the angel of the LORD says to Hagar and what she calls the LORD (16:7-13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened to Hagar in the wilderness and what she learned about God?

topics.name: The LORD visits Abraham and Sarah
topics.description: The LORD appears to Abraham in the plains of Mamre as three men; Abraham hurries to feed them. One says Sarah will have a son at the appointed time, Sarah laughs inside the tent, and the LORD asks whether anything is too hard for Him.
evidence: Describe Abraham's hospitality to the three men (18:2-8)
Repeat the question the LORD asks in 18:14 and say what it is about
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what the visitors promised Sarah and why she laughed?

topics.name: Abraham pleads for Sodom
topics.description: The LORD tells Abraham He will see whether the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is as great as it seems. Abraham draws near and asks whether the Judge of all the earth will do right, and the LORD agrees to spare the city for fifty, then down to ten righteous.
evidence: Say why the LORD decides to tell Abraham what He will do (18:17-19)
Trace the numbers Abraham names and the LORD's answers (18:24-32)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Abraham asked the LORD about Sodom and how the LORD answered?

topics.name: Sodom and Gomorrah are destroyed
topics.description: Two angels come to Lot in Sodom, the men of the city press against his house, and the angels strike them with blindness. They lead Lot, his wife and daughters out; the LORD rains brimstone and fire on the cities and Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.
evidence: Describe how the angels protected Lot and urged him to leave (19:10-17)
Say what God did to the cities and why 19:29 says He remembered Abraham
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how Lot was brought out of Sodom and what happened to the cities?

topics.name: Lot's daughters and the birth of Moab and Ammon
topics.description: Lot goes up out of Zoar to live in a cave with his two daughters. Fearing no man remains to give them children, they make their father drunk and conceive sons, Moab and Ben-ammi, who become the fathers of the Moabites and Ammonites.
evidence: State the origin of the Moabites and Ammonites as given in 19:37-38
Observe how the text reports the daughters' plan without commending it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say which nations descend from Lot's daughters according to Genesis 19:30-38?

topics.name: Abimelech takes Sarah
topics.description: In Gerar, Abraham again calls Sarah his sister and King Abimelech takes her. God warns Abimelech in a dream that he is a dead man, withheld him from sin, and tells him to restore her, for Abraham is a prophet who will pray for him.
evidence: Explain how God intervened to keep Abimelech from touching Sarah (20:3-6)
Say what Abraham does for Abimelech at the end of the chapter (20:17-18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how God protected Sarah in Gerar and what Abraham's reason was for saying she was his sister?

topics.name: Hagar and Ishmael are sent away
topics.description: After Isaac is weaned, Sarah sees Ishmael mocking and asks that he and Hagar be cast out. God tells Abraham that his seed will be called in Isaac but he will also make a nation of Ishmael; in the wilderness God hears the boy's voice and opens Hagar's eyes to a well.
evidence: Say what God told Abraham in 21:12-13
Describe how God provided for Hagar and Ishmael in the wilderness (21:17-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what God promised about Ishmael, even as Isaac was the child of promise?

topics.name: Abraham and Abimelech at Beersheba
topics.description: Abimelech and Phichol ask Abraham to swear he will not deal falsely with them. Abraham reproves Abimelech about a seized well, the two make a covenant with seven ewe lambs as a witness, and Abraham calls on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God.
evidence: Explain why Abraham set apart seven ewe lambs (21:28-30)
Say how Beersheba got its name (21:31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the well at Beersheba led to a covenant between Abraham and Abimelech?

topics.name: Abraham buries Sarah at Machpelah
topics.description: Sarah dies in Hebron, and Abraham, calling himself a stranger and sojourner, negotiates with the sons of Heth to buy the cave of Machpelah from Ephron for four hundred shekels of silver. He buries Sarah there.
evidence: Describe how Abraham obtained the burial place and what he paid (23:8-16)
Explain why a purchase of land in Canaan is notable in view of God's promise (cf. 13:15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Abraham came to own a piece of the promised land?

topics.name: A wife for Isaac
topics.description: Abraham sends his eldest servant under oath to his own kindred to find a wife for Isaac, not from the Canaanites. At the well the servant prays, Rebekah, a granddaughter of Abraham's brother Nahor, answers the sign, and after her family agrees she goes with him and marries Isaac.
evidence: Retell the servant's prayer at the well and how Rebekah answered it (24:12-20)
Point to places where the servant and Laban and Bethuel credit the LORD (24:27, 24:50)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Abraham's servant found Rebekah and who he said had guided him?

topics.name: Abraham's death and Ishmael's line
topics.description: Abraham takes Keturah, gives all he has to Isaac and gifts to his other sons, and dies at one hundred and seventy-five. Isaac and Ishmael bury him at Machpelah, God blesses Isaac, and the generations of Ishmael's twelve princes are listed.
evidence: Say who inherited Abraham's possessions and who buried him (25:5, 25:9)
Count the sons of Ishmael called princes (25:13-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened after Abraham died and how God treated Isaac?

topics.name: Isaac in Gerar
topics.description: In a famine the LORD tells Isaac not to go to Egypt and repeats the promise made to Abraham. Isaac calls Rebekah his sister, is rebuked by Abimelech, prospers, digs wells that herdsmen contest, and the LORD appears at Beersheba before Abimelech makes a covenant with him.
evidence: Compare Isaac's words about Rebekah with Abraham's in chapters 12 and 20
Name the three wells Isaac dug after Gerar and what each name recalls (26:20-22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how God renewed His promise to Isaac and what happened with the wells?

topics.name: Jacob sent to Padan-aram
topics.description: Isaac blesses Jacob, charges him not to marry a Canaanite and sends him to Laban's house for a wife, with the blessing of Abraham. Esau, seeing this, marries a daughter of Ishmael.
evidence: State what Isaac charges Jacob and the blessing he pronounces (28:1-4)
Say what Esau does in response (28:6-9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Jacob was sent away to Laban and what Isaac asked God to give him?

topics.name: Jacob, Rachel and Leah
topics.description: At a well Jacob meets Rachel and serves Laban seven years for her, but Laban gives him Leah first and Jacob serves seven more for Rachel. The LORD sees that Leah is hated and opens her womb, and she bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah.
evidence: Describe the deception on the wedding night and how Laban explained it (29:23-27)
Name Leah's four sons and note which one is Judah (29:32-35)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob came to marry both Leah and Rachel and what the LORD did for Leah?

topics.name: Jacob's sons are born and his flocks increase
topics.description: Rachel and Leah compete, giving their maids to Jacob, and sons are born including Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun and Dinah. God remembers Rachel and she bears Joseph; Jacob then bargains with Laban over the flocks and grows exceedingly rich.
evidence: Match each son with his mother as the chapter reports (Bilhah, Zilpah, Leah, Rachel)
Describe the wages Jacob proposed to Laban and the result (30:31-43)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the family of Jacob grew in Haran and which son was born to Rachel?

topics.name: Jacob flees from Laban
topics.description: After Laban's sons complain and Laban's face turns against him, the LORD tells Jacob to return to his kindred. Jacob leaves in secret, Rachel takes her father's household images, and Laban pursues him but is warned by God in a dream not to speak good or bad; the two make a covenant with a heap of stones.
evidence: Say what God told Jacob in 31:3 and 31:13
Explain how God protected Jacob when Laban caught up with him (31:24, 31:42)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Jacob left Laban secretly and how God kept him safe?

topics.name: Jacob prepares to meet Esau
topics.description: Angels of God meet Jacob at Mahanaim. Hearing that Esau is coming with four hundred men, Jacob divides his company, prays to the God of Abraham and Isaac, reminding Him of His promise, and sends droves of animals ahead as a present.
evidence: Summarise Jacob's prayer in 32:9-12 and note what promises he recalls
Describe the present he sent to Esau and why (32:13-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob responded when he heard Esau was coming with four hundred men?

topics.name: Jacob and Esau meet
topics.description: Jacob bows seven times as Esau runs to embrace him, and the two weep. Jacob urges Esau to accept the present, they part, and Jacob settles near Shechem, buys a field and raises an altar.
evidence: Describe how Esau greeted Jacob in 33:4
Say what Jacob did when he arrived near Shechem (33:18-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened when Jacob and Esau finally met after so many years?

topics.name: Dinah and the men of Shechem
topics.description: Shechem takes Dinah and defiles her, then asks to marry her. Jacob's sons answer deceitfully and demand circumcision; on the third day Simeon and Levi kill the males of the city, and Jacob rebukes them for troubling him.
evidence: Explain how the sons of Jacob used circumcision to deceive the men of Shechem (34:13-25)
Note Jacob's reaction in 34:30 and what the text reports of Simeon and Levi's reply
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Simeon and Levi did at Shechem and how their father responded?

topics.name: Back to Bethel: God confirms Israel's name
topics.description: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel; Jacob has his household put away their strange gods. At Bethel God blesses him, repeats that his name is Israel, and renews the promise of nations and land; Rachel dies bearing Benjamin, and Isaac dies at one hundred and eighty.
evidence: Say what Jacob told his household to do before going to Bethel (35:2-4)
List the twelve sons of Jacob by their mothers (35:22-26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what God said to Jacob at Bethel in Genesis 35 and who the twelve sons of Jacob were?

topics.name: The generations of Esau, who is Edom
topics.description: Genesis 36 lists Esau's wives, sons and chiefs, notes that he moved to Mount Seir because the land could not bear both his and Jacob's herds, and lists the Horite families and the kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over Israel.
evidence: Find the verse that says Esau is Edom and the verse that says why he moved (36:1, 36:6-8)
Point out the phrase about kings reigning before any king ruled Israel (36:31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain who the Edomites came from according to Genesis 36?

topics.name: Judah and Tamar
topics.description: Judah's sons Er and Onan die, and he withholds his third son Shelah from Tamar. Tamar disguises herself, conceives by Judah, produces his signet, cord and staff, and Judah says she is more righteous than he; she bears twins.
evidence: Say what Tamar did and what proof she showed Judah (38:14-25)
Quote or state Judah's verdict in 38:26 and say why he gives it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Judah says Tamar was more righteous than he was?

topics.name: Joseph in Potiphar's house
topics.description: Joseph is bought by Potiphar in Egypt, and the LORD is with him so that all prospers in his hand. When Potiphar's wife presses him he refuses as a great wickedness before God; she falsely accuses him and he is put in prison, where the LORD is still with him.
evidence: Give Joseph's reason for refusing Potiphar's wife (39:8-9)
Note how often the chapter says the LORD was with Joseph (39:2, 39:21, 39:23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Joseph did when Potiphar's wife tempted him and what happened to him afterward?

topics.name: The butler and the baker's dreams
topics.description: In prison Joseph serves Pharaoh's chief butler and chief baker, who each dream. Saying that interpretations belong to God, Joseph tells the butler he will be restored and the baker hanged; it happens in three days, but the butler forgets Joseph.
evidence: Compare the two dreams and Joseph's interpretations (40:9-19)
Say what Joseph asks of the butler and what happens (40:14, 40:23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Joseph interpreted the two prisoners' dreams and who he said gives interpretations?

topics.name: Joseph's brothers come to Egypt
topics.description: In the famine Jacob sends ten sons to buy grain in Egypt while keeping Benjamin at home. Joseph recognises them and remembers his dreams, accuses them of spying, binds Simeon and sends the rest home with the demand to bring Benjamin; their money is found in their sacks.
evidence: Point to 42:6-9 and say why the brothers do not know Joseph but he knows them
Say what the brothers admit to one another in 42:21-22
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Joseph demanded of his brothers and why they said they were guilty?

topics.name: The second journey with Benjamin
topics.description: With the grain eaten, Judah promises to be surety for Benjamin, and Jacob reluctantly lets him go with a gift and double money. Joseph has the brothers brought to his house for a meal, weeps in his chamber on seeing Benjamin, and serves Benjamin five times as much.
evidence: Say what Judah offers his father in 43:8-9
Describe Joseph's reaction on seeing Benjamin (43:29-31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob was persuaded to send Benjamin and what Joseph did when he saw him?

topics.name: The silver cup and Judah's plea
topics.description: Joseph has his silver cup put in Benjamin's sack and sends his steward after the brothers. When the cup is found Judah pleads with Joseph, tells how Jacob loves the boy, and offers himself as a bondman in Benjamin's place.
evidence: Explain how the cup came to be in Benjamin's sack (44:1-2, 44:12)
Summarise Judah's offer and the reason he gives (44:32-34)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Judah offered to do for Benjamin and why?

topics.name: Joseph makes himself known
topics.description: Joseph cannot hold back and tells his brothers he is Joseph, saying not to be grieved that they sold him, for God sent him before them to preserve life. Pharaoh invites the family to Egypt, and Jacob's spirit revives when he hears Joseph is alive.
evidence: Retell what Joseph says in 45:4-8 about who sent him to Egypt
Say how Jacob reacted to the news (45:26-28)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Joseph understood what had happened to him and what he told his brothers?

topics.name: Jacob goes down to Egypt
topics.description: At Beersheba God tells Israel not to fear going down into Egypt, promising to make him a great nation there, go down with him and bring him up again. The household that came into Egypt is listed, and Joseph meets his father in Goshen and prepares them to speak to Pharaoh as shepherds.
evidence: State God's three promises to Jacob in 46:3-4
Give the total number of Jacob's house who came into Egypt (46:26-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what God promised Jacob before he went down to Egypt?

topics.name: Jacob before Pharaoh
topics.description: Joseph presents his brothers and father to Pharaoh, who gives them the land of Goshen to dwell in. Jacob blesses Pharaoh and describes his years as a pilgrimage, few and evil.
evidence: Say what land Pharaoh gave Jacob's family and what their trade was (47:3-6)
Report what Jacob says about the years of his pilgrimage (47:9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell where Jacob's family settled in Egypt and who blessed whom in Pharaoh's court?

topics.name: The famine and Pharaoh's ownership of the land
topics.description: As the famine deepens Joseph gathers the money of Egypt and Canaan, then takes the people's cattle and finally their land in exchange for bread. The people become Pharaoh's servants and give a fifth of the increase, while the priests' land is not bought.
evidence: List in order what the people gave Joseph for bread (47:14-20)
State the law Joseph made about the fifth part (47:26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Joseph handled the famine in Egypt and what the people said in return (47:25)?

topics.name: Israel's oath and the blessing of Ephraim and Manasseh
topics.description: Israel makes Joseph swear to bury him with his fathers, then recalls God Almighty's promise at Luz and takes Ephraim and Manasseh as his own. He crosses his hands to bless the younger Ephraim first, over Joseph's objection, and says God will bring them back to the land of their fathers.
evidence: Say where Jacob asked to be buried and who swore to do it (47:29-31)
Explain what was unusual about the way Jacob blessed the two boys (48:13-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob blessed Joseph's sons and what he said God would do for the family?

topics.name: Jacob blesses his twelve sons
topics.description: Jacob gathers his sons to tell what will befall them in the last days, speaking in turn to Reuben, Simeon and Levi, Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher, Naphtali, Joseph and Benjamin. The chapter names these the twelve tribes of Israel; Judah's blessing is treated separately.
evidence: Say what Jacob says about Reuben and why (49:3-4)
Find the verse that calls the twelve sons the tribes of Israel (49:28)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name at least six of Jacob's sons and say one thing Jacob said about one of them?

topics.name: The death and burial of Jacob
topics.description: Jacob charges his sons to bury him in the cave of Machpelah with Abraham, Isaac and their wives, and then dies. Joseph has him embalmed, Egypt mourns, and a great company goes up to Canaan to bury him there.
evidence: Say who is already buried in the cave according to 49:31
Describe who went up with Joseph to bury Jacob (50:7-9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell where Jacob was buried and why it was the same place as Abraham and Sarah?

topics.name: Exodus: overview
topics.description: Exodus tells of Israel enslaved in Egypt (1:1-14) and delivered through the plagues, Passover and the sea (chapters 7-15), then of the covenant at Sinai (19-24) and the tabernacle (25-40), ending with the glory of the LORD filling it (40:34-38).
evidence: Name the main sections: bondage, deliverance, the journey to Sinai, the law and covenant, and the tabernacle
Say where Exodus begins (1:1) and ends (40:38)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline Exodus in order, from the bondage in Egypt to the glory filling the tabernacle?

topics.name: Israel is oppressed in Egypt
topics.description: Jacob's family grows into a numerous people in Egypt, and a new king who did not know Joseph sets taskmasters over them and makes their lives bitter with hard bondage. The more they are afflicted, the more they multiply.
evidence: Say why the new king feared the Israelites (1:9-10)
Describe the work they were forced to do (1:11-14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Israel went from being Joseph's family in Egypt to being slaves, and what happened the more they were afflicted?

topics.name: The midwives fear God
topics.description: Pharaoh orders the Hebrew midwives to kill the baby boys, but Shiphrah and Puah fear God and let them live. God deals well with them, and Pharaoh then commands that every newborn son be cast into the river.
evidence: Name the two midwives (1:15)
Say what they did and why (1:17)
Say what Pharaoh then commanded all his people (1:22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Shiphrah and Puah did when the king gave his order, and why?

topics.name: Moses is born and drawn from the water
topics.description: A Levite woman hides her baby son for three months, then places him in a basket of bulrushes by the river. Pharaoh's daughter finds him, has compassion, and the baby's own mother is paid to nurse him; he is named Moses.
evidence: Retell how the baby was hidden and found (2:2-6)
Say who nursed him and why that was surprising (2:7-9)
Explain the meaning of the name Moses given in 2:10
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how baby Moses was saved from the river?

topics.name: Moses flees to Midian and God hears Israel's cry
topics.description: Grown up, Moses kills an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, learns the deed is known, and flees to Midian, where he helps the priest's daughters and marries Zipporah. In Egypt the people groan, and God hears and remembers his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
evidence: Say why Moses left Egypt (2:11-15)
Say what Moses did at the well in Midian (2:16-17)
Find the verse that says God remembered his covenant (2:24)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Moses ended up in Midian, and what 2:23-25 says God did about Israel's cry?

topics.name: The burning bush
topics.description: While keeping Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses sees a bush burning without being consumed. God calls him by name from it, declares the ground holy, identifies himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and says he has seen Israel's affliction and will send Moses to Pharaoh.
evidence: Describe what Moses saw and what God told him to do with his shoes (3:2-5)
Say what God said he had seen and heard (3:7-9)
Say what God sent Moses to do (3:10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened at the burning bush and what God said to Moses there?

topics.name: "I AM": God's name and Moses' commission
topics.description: Moses asks who he is to go to Pharaoh and what to tell Israel God's name. God promises to be with him, gives the name I AM THAT I AM and the LORD God of your fathers, and tells him what will happen: Pharaoh will refuse until God stretches out his hand.
evidence: Quote the name God gave in 3:14 from the Bible
Say the promise God gave Moses in 3:12
Say what God predicted about Pharaoh (3:19-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what name God gave Moses to tell Israel, and what God promised him?

topics.name: Three signs and Aaron as spokesman
topics.description: Moses fears the people will not believe him. God gives him three signs (the rod that becomes a serpent, the leprous hand, water turned to blood). When Moses says he is slow of speech, God answers that he made man's mouth, is angry at the further refusal, and appoints Aaron as spokesman.
evidence: List the three signs (4:2-9)
Say how God answered Moses' complaint about his speech (4:11-12)
Say who God appointed to speak for Moses (4:14-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name the signs God gave Moses and say how God answered Moses' excuse about his speech?

topics.name: Moses returns to Egypt
topics.description: Moses leaves Jethro with his wife and sons, is told Israel is God's firstborn son and that Pharaoh's firstborn will die if he refuses, and is met by the LORD on the way, when Zipporah circumcises her son. Aaron meets him, and the elders believe and worship when they hear that God has visited them.
evidence: Say what message about "my son, even my firstborn" Moses was to give (4:22-23)
Say how the people responded (4:31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what God told Moses to say to Pharaoh in 4:22-23 and how the Israelites responded in 4:31?

topics.name: Pharaoh refuses and the work grows harder
topics.description: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let Israel hold a feast to the LORD; he says he does not know the LORD and orders the people to make the same number of bricks while gathering their own straw. The officers blame Moses and Aaron, and Moses asks the LORD why he has not delivered his people.
evidence: Quote Pharaoh's answer in 5:2 in your own words
Say how the work changed (5:6-9)
Say what Moses asked God (5:22-23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened when Moses and Aaron first spoke to Pharaoh?

topics.name: "I am the LORD": God's promises to redeem
topics.description: God answers Moses by saying he is the LORD and has remembered his covenant with the patriarchs, then makes a series of promises: to bring Israel out, rid them of bondage, redeem them with a stretched out arm, take them as his people and be their God, and bring them to the land.
evidence: Name some of the promises God made to Israel in 6:6-8
Say what God said he had remembered (6:4-5)
Say how the people responded (6:9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list what God promised Israel in 6:6-8 and say what he said he remembered?

topics.name: The heads of the fathers' houses
topics.description: A genealogy lists the sons of Reuben, Simeon and Levi, tracing Aaron and Moses to the house of Levi, then returns to the LORD's command to speak to Pharaoh, to which Moses answers that he is of uncircumcised lips.
evidence: Say which tribe Moses and Aaron came from (6:16-20)
Say what concern Moses repeated in 6:30
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say from which tribe Moses and Aaron came, according to this genealogy?

topics.name: Aaron's rod and Pharaoh's magicians
topics.description: God says he has made Moses as a god to Pharaoh with Aaron as prophet, and that he will harden Pharaoh's heart. Aaron's rod becomes a serpent; the magicians do likewise, but Aaron's rod swallows theirs, and Pharaoh's heart stays hard.
evidence: Say what happened to Aaron's rod and the magicians' rods (7:10-12)
Say how Pharaoh responded (7:13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened when Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh?

topics.name: The first plague: the river turned to blood
topics.description: At the river's brink Moses and Aaron strike the water at the LORD's command; the river turns to blood, the fish die and the Egyptians cannot drink. The magicians do the same and Pharaoh's heart remains hard.
evidence: Say what God said Pharaoh would know by this sign (7:17)
Say what happened to the river and the fish (7:20-21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the first plague and how Pharaoh responded?

topics.name: The second plague: frogs
topics.description: Frogs come up over Egypt into houses, beds and ovens. Pharaoh asks Moses to entreat the LORD and promises to let the people go; the frogs die at Moses' prayer, but when Pharaoh sees respite he hardens his heart.
evidence: Say what Pharaoh promised and what he did when the frogs were gone (8:8, 8:15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Pharaoh promised during the plague of frogs and what he did afterwards?

topics.name: Lice and flies: a division between Israel and Egypt
topics.description: Aaron strikes the dust and it becomes lice; the magicians cannot imitate it and say it is the finger of God. Swarms of flies then fill Egypt but not Goshen, where Israel lives, and Pharaoh offers a compromise before hardening his heart again.
evidence: Say what the magicians said about the lice (8:19)
Say how Goshen was treated differently (8:22-23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what was different about the land of Goshen in the plague of flies?

topics.name: Livestock plague and boils
topics.description: A grievous murrain kills the Egyptians' cattle while none of Israel's die, then ashes sprinkled by Moses become boils on man and beast, even on the magicians. The LORD hardens Pharaoh's heart.
evidence: Say what happened to the livestock of Egypt and of Israel (9:6)
Say what happened to the magicians (9:11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the fifth and sixth plagues and what was different for Israel?

topics.name: The plague of hail
topics.description: God tells Pharaoh he has raised him up to show his power and make his name known in all the earth, and sends hail with fire that destroys everything in the fields, except in Goshen. Pharaoh says he has sinned and the LORD is righteous, but hardens his heart again when the hail stops.
evidence: Say why God said he had raised Pharaoh up (9:16)
Say what some servants did when they feared the word of the LORD (9:20)
Describe Pharaoh's confession and what followed (9:27-35)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Pharaoh said after the hail and what he did once it stopped?

topics.name: The plague of locusts
topics.description: God says he has hardened Pharaoh so that parents may tell their children of the signs. His servants urge him to let the men go, but Pharaoh will not release the families; locusts cover Egypt and eat what the hail left, and after Pharaoh's confession the LORD removes them but hardens his heart.
evidence: Say why the LORD said he did these signs (10:2)
Say what Pharaoh offered and what Moses asked for (10:8-11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Moses wanted to take with him to the feast in 10:9 and what the locusts did?

topics.name: The plague of darkness
topics.description: Thick darkness covers Egypt for three days while Israel has light in their dwellings. Pharaoh offers to let the people go but keep their flocks, Moses refuses, and Pharaoh tells Moses never to see his face again.
evidence: Say how long the darkness lasted and where there was light (10:22-23)
Say why Moses insisted on taking the livestock (10:25-26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the ninth plague and where there was light?

topics.name: Pharaoh's hard heart
topics.description: The text says both that Pharaoh hardened his own heart and that the LORD hardened it, and ties this to the LORD multiplying his signs and being known and honoured. The topic invites careful reading of each verse without going beyond what is said.
evidence: Find one verse where Pharaoh hardens his own heart (8:15) and one where the LORD does (9:12)
Say what purposes God gives for the hardening (7:3-5, 9:16, 10:1-2, 14:4)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} point to verses that say Pharaoh hardened his heart and verses that say the LORD hardened it, and say what purposes the text gives?

topics.name: The last plague announced
topics.description: God tells Moses one more plague will bring Pharaoh to let Israel go. Moses announces that at midnight every firstborn in Egypt will die, but not even a dog will move its tongue against Israel, to show that the LORD makes a difference between Egypt and Israel.
evidence: Say what Moses announced (11:4-5)
Say how Israel would be treated differently (11:7)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what the last plague was to be and how Israel would be treated differently?

topics.name: The Passover instituted
topics.description: God tells Israel to take an unblemished lamb for each household on the tenth day, kill it at evening on the fourteenth, put its blood on the door posts and lintel, and eat it roasted in haste with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. When he sees the blood he will pass over; the day is to be kept as a memorial, and children are to be told what it means.
evidence: List what the lamb must be like and what was done with its blood (12:5-7)
Say what God promised when he saw the blood (12:13)
Say what parents were to tell their children (12:26-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the Israelites did with the lamb and its blood, and what God promised?

topics.name: The firstborn die and Israel leaves Egypt
topics.description: At midnight the LORD strikes all the firstborn in Egypt, and Pharaoh urges Israel to leave. They go with their dough unleavened, taking silver, gold and clothing given by the Egyptians, about six hundred thousand men on foot, at the end of the four hundred and thirty years.
evidence: Describe what happened at midnight (12:29-30)
Say what the Egyptians gave Israel (12:35-36)
Say how long the sojourning in Egypt was (12:40-41)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened at midnight and how Israel left Egypt?

topics.name: Rules for keeping the Passover
topics.description: The ordinance of the Passover is set out: no foreigner or hired servant may eat of it, a bought servant who is circumcised may, the lamb is eaten in one house and no bone of it broken, and a sojourner who wants to keep it must be circumcised. One law covers native and stranger.
evidence: Say what is required of a stranger who wants to keep the Passover (12:48)
Say what was not to be done with the lamb's bones (12:46)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what the Passover rules say about foreigners and about the lamb's bones?

topics.name: The firstborn and the feast of unleavened bread
topics.description: God says all the firstborn of man and beast are his; the firstborn of men are to be redeemed and an ass's firstling redeemed with a lamb. Israel is to remember the day of the exodus, keep the feast of unleavened bread and tell their sons what the LORD did.
evidence: Say what God claimed as his in 13:2
Say what Israelites were to tell their sons (13:8, 13:14-15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say why the firstborn belonged to the LORD and what children were to be told?

topics.name: Led by the pillar of cloud and fire
topics.description: God leads Israel by the wilderness way and not the near road through Philistia, lest they see war and return. Moses carries the bones of Joseph, and the LORD goes before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
evidence: Say why God did not lead them by the nearest road (13:17)
Describe how the LORD led them by day and by night (13:21-22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how God led Israel out of Egypt, day and night?

topics.name: Crossing the Red Sea
topics.description: Pharaoh pursues Israel with chariots and traps them at the sea. Moses says to stand still and see the LORD's salvation; the LORD divides the sea, Israel walks through on dry ground, and the returning waters cover Pharaoh's army.
evidence: Say what the people said when they saw the Egyptians (14:10-12)
Say what Moses answered (14:13-14)
Say what happened to the Egyptians and how Israel responded (14:27-31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the crossing of the sea and what Moses told the people to do?

topics.name: The song of Moses and Miriam
topics.description: Moses and Israel sing to the LORD for triumphing over Pharaoh's horse and rider, praising him as strength, song, salvation and warrior, asking who is like him among the gods, and looking ahead to leading his people in to his sanctuary. Miriam leads the women in the refrain.
evidence: Say what the song says the LORD did (15:1, 15:4)
Find where the song says who is like the LORD (15:11)
Say who led the women (15:20-21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Israel praised the LORD for in the song at the sea?

topics.name: Bitter water at Marah
topics.description: After three days without water Israel comes to Marah, where the water is bitter and the people murmur. The LORD shows Moses a tree which sweetens it, and promises healing for obedience, then they come to Elim.
evidence: Say why the people murmured at Marah (15:23-24)
Say how the water was made sweet (15:25)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Marah?

topics.name: Bread from heaven: manna and quails
topics.description: Israel murmurs for the food of Egypt. The LORD sends quails in the evening and manna in the morning, a day's portion to be gathered daily, with a double portion on the sixth day for the sabbath. An omer of manna is kept before the Testimony.
evidence: Say what the people were to do each day and on the sixth day (16:4-5, 16:22-26)
Say what happened to manna kept overnight against the command (16:19-20)
Say how long Israel ate manna (16:35)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the manna was gathered each day and what was different on the sixth and seventh days?

topics.name: Water from the rock at Massah and Meribah
topics.description: At Rephidim there is no water, and the people chide Moses and test the LORD. At the LORD's direction Moses strikes the rock at Horeb and water comes out; the place is named Massah and Meribah.
evidence: Say what the people asked (17:7)
Say what Moses did and what came of it (17:5-6)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what the people said at Rephidim and how God provided water?

topics.name: Amalek attacked, and Moses' hands held up
topics.description: Amalek fights Israel at Rephidim. While Joshua fights, Moses stands on the hill with the rod of God; Israel prevails when his hand is up, and Aaron and Hur support his hands until the sun sets. The LORD says he will blot out Amalek's remembrance.
evidence: Say what happened when Moses held up his hand and when he let it down (17:11)
Say who helped Moses (17:12)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the battle with Amalek and how Moses' hands were held up?

topics.name: Jethro visits and rejoices
topics.description: Jethro brings Moses' wife and two sons to the mount of God. Moses tells him what the LORD did to Pharaoh and Egypt, and Jethro rejoices, blesses the LORD, says he knows the LORD is greater than all gods, and offers a burnt offering and sacrifices.
evidence: Say what Jethro concluded about the LORD (18:10-11)
Say who ate with Jethro before God (18:12)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Jethro said after hearing what the LORD had done for Israel?

topics.name: Jethro's counsel: judges over Israel
topics.description: Moses sits all day judging the people. Jethro tells him the burden is too heavy and advises him to teach the statutes and appoint able men who fear God as rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, bringing only hard cases to him. Moses does so.
evidence: Say what problem Jethro saw (18:14-18)
Describe the kind of men Moses was to choose (18:21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Moses appointed other judges and what kind of men he chose?

topics.name: At Sinai: a kingdom of priests
topics.description: In the third month Israel reaches Sinai. God reminds them how he bore them on eagles' wings and says that if they obey his voice and keep his covenant they will be his peculiar treasure, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. The people answer together that they will do all the LORD has spoken.
evidence: Say what God reminded Israel of (19:4)
Say what God said Israel would be if they obeyed and kept his covenant (19:5-6)
Say how the people answered (19:8)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what God offered Israel at Sinai in 19:5-6 and how the people answered?

topics.name: The LORD descends on Mount Sinai
topics.description: Israel is told to sanctify themselves and not to touch the mountain. On the third day there are thunders, lightning, a thick cloud and a loud trumpet, and the LORD descends on Sinai in fire; Moses goes up and is told to warn the people again.
evidence: Say how the people prepared (19:10-15)
Describe what happened on the third day (19:16-19)
Say what boundary was set and why (19:12, 19:21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what happened when the LORD came down on Mount Sinai, and why bounds were set?

topics.name: The Ten Commandments
topics.description: God speaks all these words, beginning by saying he is the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt. They cover having no other gods, no images, not taking his name in vain, remembering the sabbath, honouring father and mother, and not killing, committing adultery, stealing, bearing false witness or coveting.
evidence: Recite the ten commandments in order from the Bible
Say what 20:2 says before the commandments begin
Say the reason given for the sabbath (20:11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say the Ten Commandments in order and say what comes before them in 20:2?

topics.name: The people stand afar off; altars of earth
topics.description: The people see the thunder, lightning and smoke, tremble, and ask Moses to speak with them rather than God lest they die. Moses says God has come to prove them so that they sin not, and God then gives instructions about no gods of silver or gold and about altars of earth or uncut stone.
evidence: Say what the people asked Moses (20:19)
Say what Moses said was God's purpose (20:20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say why the people stood far off and what they asked Moses to do?

topics.name: Judgments: Hebrew servants
topics.description: God sets judgments before Israel, beginning with Hebrew servants: a servant serves six years and goes out free in the seventh, and rules protect a servant's wife and a maidservant sold by her father.
evidence: Say what must happen in the seventh year (21:2)
Say what protections 21:7-11 gives a woman
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what the law of 21:2 said about a Hebrew servant?

topics.name: Judgments: injury and death
topics.description: Laws deal with striking and killing, a refuge for accidental killing, striking or cursing parents, kidnapping, injuries, the life-for-life principle and an owner's responsibility for a goring ox or an open pit.
evidence: Say how deliberate and accidental killing are treated differently (21:12-14)
Find the verses that state life for life, eye for eye (21:23-25)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between the cases in 21:12-14?

topics.name: Judgments: theft and property
topics.description: Laws require restitution for stolen and damaged property, such as five oxen for an ox, and set rules for animals that trespass, fire, goods left in trust and borrowed animals.
evidence: Say what a thief had to give back (22:1, 22:4)
Say what was required when a man's beast fed in another's field (22:5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what the law required of a thief in 22:1-4?

topics.name: Judgments: purity, the poor and the stranger
topics.description: Laws cover seduction of a maid, sorcery, sacrificing to another god, and care for strangers, widows, the fatherless and the poor, whom Israel must not oppress because they themselves were strangers in Egypt. Firstfruits and the firstborn are to be given to the LORD.
evidence: Say how strangers, widows and orphans were to be treated and why (22:21-24)
Say what was to be done with a neighbour's pledged cloak (22:26-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what 22:21-27 says about strangers, widows and the poor and why?

topics.name: Judgments: honest justice
topics.description: Israel is not to spread false reports, follow a crowd to pervert justice, favour the poor or wrest justice from the poor, take a bribe or oppress a stranger; they must even return an enemy's straying ox and help his fallen ass.
evidence: List some commands about witnesses and judgment (23:1-3, 23:6-8)
Say what to do if you see your enemy's ox going astray (23:4-5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what 23:1-9 teaches about honesty in court and fairness?

topics.name: Judgments: sabbath years and three feasts
topics.description: The land is to rest in the seventh year so the poor may eat, and every seventh day all work is to rest. Three times a year Israel keeps a feast: unleavened bread, harvest and ingathering.
evidence: Say why the land was to rest in the seventh year (23:11)
Name the three feasts (23:14-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name the three yearly feasts and the rest of the seventh day and seventh year?

topics.name: The angel before Israel and the land
topics.description: God promises to send an Angel before Israel to bring them to the prepared place, saying his name is in him. If they obey, he will be an enemy to their enemies and drive out the nations little by little; they must not serve those nations' gods or make a covenant with them.
evidence: Say what God promised and what he required (23:20-25)
Say why the nations would be driven out gradually (23:29-30)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what God promised about the Angel and the land, and what Israel was not to do?

topics.name: The covenant ratified with blood
topics.description: Moses tells the people all the LORD's words and judgments, and they answer with one voice that they will do them. Moses writes the words, builds an altar and twelve pillars, reads the book of the covenant, and sprinkles the people with blood, saying it is the blood of the covenant the LORD has made with them.
evidence: Say how the people answered (24:3, 24:7)
Say what Moses did with the blood and what he said (24:6-8)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened when the covenant was made in Exodus 24, and what Moses said as he sprinkled the blood?

topics.name: The elders see God; Moses on the mountain
topics.description: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and seventy elders go up and see the God of Israel and eat and drink. Moses goes further up with Joshua into the cloud, where the glory of the LORD abides on Sinai and he stays forty days and forty nights.
evidence: Say who went up and what they saw and did (24:9-11)
Say how long Moses stayed on the mountain and what covered it (24:15-18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say who went up the mountain in Exodus 24 and how long Moses stayed?

topics.name: "Let them make me a sanctuary"
topics.description: God tells Moses to ask Israel for a willing offering of gold, silver, brass, fabrics, skins, wood, oil, spices and stones, so they can make a sanctuary so that he may dwell among them, according to the pattern he shows.
evidence: Say how the offering was to be given (25:2)
Say why God wanted the sanctuary (25:8)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say why God asked for a sanctuary and how the gifts were to be given?

topics.name: The ark and the mercy seat
topics.description: Moses is told to make an ark of acacia wood overlaid with gold, to put the testimony in it, and to make a gold mercy seat with two cherubim on top, where God says he will meet and speak with Moses.
evidence: Say what was to be put in the ark (25:16)
Say what God said would happen at the mercy seat (25:22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the ark and say what God said would happen above the mercy seat?

topics.name: The table and the golden lampstand
topics.description: Instructions are given for a gold-covered table for the bread of the presence and a pure gold lampstand with seven lamps, made after the pattern shown on the mount.
evidence: Say what was to be set on the table (25:30)
Say how many lamps the lampstand had (25:37)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name the two furnishings made in 25:23-40?

topics.name: The curtains, boards and veil
topics.description: The tabernacle is to be made of ten linen curtains with cherubim, goat-hair curtains and skin coverings, upright boards in silver sockets, and a veil that divides the holy place from the most holy place, where the ark is to be set.
evidence: Say what the veil separated (26:33)
Say what was to go in the most holy place (26:33-34)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what the veil in 26:31-33 was for?

topics.name: The bronze altar and the court
topics.description: Instructions for an altar of acacia wood overlaid with bronze, a court enclosed by linen hangings on bronze pillars, and pure olive oil so a lamp burns always before the veil, tended by Aaron and his sons.
evidence: Say what the altar of 27:1-8 was made of
Say who was to tend the lamp (27:21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what stood in the court of the tabernacle according to 27:1-19?

topics.name: Aaron and his sons: the priestly garments
topics.description: Aaron and his sons are to be priests, with holy garments for glory and beauty: ephod, breastplate with twelve stones for the tribes, robe with bells, a turban with a gold plate "Holiness to the LORD", and linen undergarments. Aaron bears the names of Israel on his shoulders and heart.
evidence: Say what names were on the stones of the ephod and breastplate (28:9-12, 28:21)
Say what was engraved on the gold plate (28:36)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Aaron carried on his shoulders and heart when he went in before the LORD?

topics.name: The consecration of the priests
topics.description: Aaron and his sons are washed, clothed, anointed and consecrated over seven days with a bullock and rams. Daily lambs are offered at morning and evening, and God says he will meet Israel there, sanctify the tabernacle and dwell among them.
evidence: Name some steps of the consecration (29:4-9, 29:20-21)
Say what God promised in 29:45-46
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what was done to make Aaron and his sons priests and what God promised in 29:45-46?

topics.name: The incense altar and the atonement money
topics.description: God gives instructions for a gold altar of incense before the veil, burned morning and evening, with atonement made on its horns once a year, and for a half-shekel ransom for each person numbered, rich and poor alike.
evidence: Say what was to be burned on the altar and when (30:7-8)
Say how much each person gave (30:13-15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what the atonement money was and who gave it?

topics.name: The laver, anointing oil and incense
topics.description: A bronze laver is made for priests to wash hands and feet before entering the tabernacle or approaching the altar, lest they die. A holy anointing oil and a special incense are described; neither may be copied for ordinary use.
evidence: Say when Aaron and his sons were to wash (30:19-21)
Say what was forbidden about the anointing oil and incense (30:32-33, 30:37-38)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what the laver was for and why Aaron and his sons washed?

topics.name: Bezalel and Oholiab are called
topics.description: The LORD calls by name Bezalel of the tribe of Judah and fills him with the spirit of God in wisdom and workmanship, and gives Aholiab of Dan and others to help make the tabernacle and all its furnishings.
evidence: Say who was called and what filled him (31:2-3)
Say what he was to make (31:7-11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say who God appointed to build the tabernacle and what equipped him?

topics.name: The sabbath as a sign; the tablets of testimony
topics.description: God says Israel must keep his sabbaths as a sign between him and them throughout their generations, a perpetual covenant, grounded in his six days of making and rest on the seventh. At the end he gives Moses two tablets of stone written by the finger of God.
evidence: Say what the sabbath is called in 31:13, 31:16-17
Say what God gave Moses at the end of the conversation (31:18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say why the sabbath is called a sign and what God gave Moses on the mountain?

topics.name: The sabbath in Exodus
topics.description: Exodus follows the sabbath from the manna (16) through the fourth commandment (20:8-11), the law for rest (23:12), and its description as a sign and perpetual covenant (31:12-17) to a final reminder before building the tabernacle (35:1-3).
evidence: Say what the fourth commandment says is the reason for the sabbath (20:11)
Say what 31:13 says the sabbath is a sign of
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} trace what Exodus says about the sabbath from the manna to chapter 31?

topics.name: The golden calf
topics.description: When Moses delays on the mountain, the people ask Aaron to make gods for them. Aaron collects their gold earrings and fashions a molten calf, builds an altar and proclaims a feast, and the people offer sacrifices and rise up to play.
evidence: Say what the people asked and what Aaron made (32:1-4)
Say what Aaron proclaimed (32:5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what the people did while Moses was on the mountain?

topics.name: Moses pleads for the people
topics.description: God tells Moses the people have corrupted themselves and he will consume them and make a great nation of Moses. Moses pleads that the LORD brought them out and remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, and the LORD repents of the evil he thought to do.
evidence: Say what God threatened (32:9-10)
Say what Moses asked God to remember (32:13)
Say what the LORD did in response (32:14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how Moses pleaded for Israel and what he asked God to remember?

topics.name: Moses breaks the tablets; judgment on the calf
topics.description: Moses comes down with tablets written by God, sees the calf, breaks the tablets, burns the calf and makes Israel drink it. The Levites answer his call to be on the LORD's side, about three thousand fall, and Moses goes back to seek atonement and offers to be blotted out with them; the LORD plagues the people.
evidence: Say what Moses did with the tablets and the calf (32:19-20)
Say what Aaron said in his defence (32:22-24)
Say what Moses asked the LORD in 32:32
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Moses did when he saw the calf and what he asked God in 32:32?

topics.name: The tent of meeting and the cloud
topics.description: God tells Israel to go to the land but says he will not go up in their midst because they are stiffnecked, and the people mourn. Moses pitches a tent outside the camp where the cloudy pillar descends and the LORD speaks with him face to face as with a friend.
evidence: Say what God said he would not do (33:3)
Describe how the LORD spoke with Moses (33:9-11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say why Moses pitched the tent outside the camp and how the LORD spoke with him there?

topics.name: Moses asks to see God's glory
topics.description: Moses asks that God's presence go with them and then to see his glory. The LORD says his presence will go with Moses, that he will make all his goodness pass and proclaim his name, but no man can see his face and live; Moses is hidden in a cleft of the rock and sees only his back.
evidence: Say what Moses asked in 33:15 and 33:18
Say what God said he would do and what he would not allow (33:19-23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Moses asked to see and how God answered?

topics.name: The LORD proclaims his name
topics.description: Moses hews two new tablets and goes up Sinai, where the LORD descends in the cloud and proclaims his name as merciful, gracious, longsuffering and abundant in goodness and truth, forgiving iniquity yet not clearing the guilty. Moses bows and asks God to go among them and pardon their sin.
evidence: List words from 34:6-7 that describe the LORD
Say what Moses asked in 34:9
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how the LORD described himself in 34:6-7 and what Moses asked?

topics.name: The covenant renewed and the words written
topics.description: The LORD says he makes a covenant and will do marvels, and commands Israel to destroy the altars of the nations, make no covenant with them, make no molten gods, and keep the feasts and the sabbath. He tells Moses to write the words, and after forty days Moses writes on the tables the words of the covenant, the ten commandments.
evidence: Say what God said in 34:10 and 34:27
Say what was written on the tables (34:28)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what the LORD told Moses to write in 34:27-28 and what it is called?

topics.name: Moses' shining face
topics.description: Moses comes down with the two tablets and does not know that the skin of his face shines; Aaron and Israel are afraid to come near. Moses speaks to them and wears a veil over his face except when he goes in before the LORD.
evidence: Say why people were afraid to come near (34:30)
Say when Moses took the veil off (34:34)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what happened to Moses' face and when he wore a veil?

topics.name: The people bring willing offerings
topics.description: Moses gathers Israel, repeats the sabbath, and calls for the offerings and for every wise-hearted person to make what the LORD commanded. Men and women bring jewels, materials and spun thread with willing hearts.
evidence: Say who brought offerings (35:21-29)
Say what Moses repeated about the sabbath (35:2-3)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how the people responded when Moses asked for offerings for the tabernacle?

topics.name: Bezalel and the workers build; enough and too much
topics.description: Moses announces that the LORD has called Bezalel and Aholiab, and the workers receive the offerings. The people bring so much that Moses has the camp stop giving, and the workers make the curtains, boards, bars and veil.
evidence: Say what happened when the people brought too much (36:5-7)
Name what the workers made in chapter 36
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say why Moses told the people to stop bringing offerings?

topics.name: The ark, table, lampstand and incense altar are made
topics.description: Bezalel makes the ark with its mercy seat and cherubim, the table, the lampstand, the incense altar, the anointing oil and the incense, as commanded.
evidence: Name the furnishings made in chapter 37
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list the furnishings Bezalel made in chapter 37?

topics.name: The altar, the laver, the court and the accounts
topics.description: Bezalel makes the altar of burnt offering, the laver from the women's mirrors, and the court, and the metals given for the work are totalled.
evidence: Say what the laver was made from (38:8)
Say what was counted in 38:24-31
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Bezalel made in chapter 38 and what the laver was made from?

topics.name: The priestly garments are made
