topics.name: Stephen's speech: Abraham, the patriarchs and Joseph
topics.description: Asked by the high priest if the charges are true, Stephen begins with the God of glory appearing to Abraham, the promise of the land, the covenant of circumcision and the sons of Jacob. He tells how the patriarchs sold Joseph in envy, yet God was with him and raised him up in Egypt, and how Jacob and his family came down there.
evidence: Say what God promised Abraham and how long his seed would be in a strange land (7:3-7)
Retell what Stephen says about Joseph and his brothers (7:9-14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline how Stephen begins his speech from Abraham to Joseph?

topics.name: Stephen's speech: Moses and the people's refusal
topics.description: Stephen recounts Israel's growth in Egypt, the birth and upbringing of Moses, his first attempt to help his brethren and their rejection, and God's call from the burning bush. He says the people refused Moses, turned back in their hearts to Egypt, and made a calf.
evidence: Retell the stages of Moses' life Stephen names (7:20-36)
Say how Stephen says the fathers treated Moses (7:35, 7:39-41)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Stephen says Israel treated Moses, whom God sent as ruler and deliverer?

topics.name: Stephen's speech: tabernacle, temple and stiffnecked people
topics.description: Stephen recalls the tabernacle in the wilderness and David and Solomon's house, then says the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands. He charges the council with resisting the Holy Ghost like their fathers, who persecuted the prophets and now betrayed and murdered the Just One.
evidence: Say what Stephen says about where God dwells (7:48-50)
State the charge Stephen makes against the council (7:51-53)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Stephen answers the charge about the temple and what he accuses the council of?

topics.name: Stephen sees Jesus and is stoned
topics.description: The council is cut to the heart, but Stephen, full of the Holy Ghost, sees the glory of God and Jesus standing at God's right hand. They stone him outside the city, with the witnesses laying their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul, and Stephen prays that the Lord Jesus receive his spirit and that this sin not be laid to their charge.
evidence: Say what Stephen saw and said before he died (7:55-56)
Give his two prayers as he was stoned (7:59-60)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Stephen saw, how he died, and what he asked for his killers?

topics.name: Persecution scatters the church
topics.description: Saul consents to Stephen's death and a great persecution scatters the church in Jerusalem throughout Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles. Saul ravages the church, entering houses and imprisoning men and women, while the scattered believers go everywhere preaching the word.
evidence: Say what Saul did to the church (8:3)
Explain what the scattered believers did (8:4)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the persecution after Stephen spread the word?

topics.name: Philip in Samaria and Simon the sorcerer
topics.description: Philip preaches Christ in Samaria with miracles, and many believe and are baptized, including Simon who had practised sorcery. Peter and John come, pray, and lay hands on them so they receive the Holy Ghost; when Simon offers money for this power, Peter rebukes him and tells him to repent.
evidence: Describe what happened in Samaria through Philip (8:5-8, 8:12)
Explain why Peter rebuked Simon (8:18-23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Philip did in Samaria and why Peter rebuked Simon?

topics.name: Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch
topics.description: An angel and the Spirit send Philip to a chariot on the road to Gaza, where an Ethiopian officer is reading Isaiah. Philip begins at that scripture and preaches Jesus; the man believes, is baptized, and goes on his way rejoicing.
evidence: Say what the eunuch was reading and what Philip did with it (8:28-35)
Describe the baptism and what happened to Philip (8:36-40)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how Philip explained the scripture to the Ethiopian and what happened afterward?

topics.name: Saul meets Jesus on the road to Damascus
topics.description: Saul, breathing threats against the disciples, is stopped near Damascus by a light from heaven and the voice of Jesus asking why he persecutes him. Struck blind, he is led into the city, and Ananias, sent by the Lord, lays hands on him; he receives sight, is filled with the Holy Ghost, and is baptized.
evidence: Say what Jesus said to Saul and what Saul asked (9:4-6)
Explain what the Lord told Ananias about Saul (9:15-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Saul on the Damascus road and how Ananias helped him?

topics.name: Saul preaches and escapes from Damascus
topics.description: Saul immediately preaches in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God, and the Jews plot to kill him, so the disciples let him down the wall in a basket. In Jerusalem Barnabas brings him to the apostles, and when the Grecians try to kill him he is sent to Tarsus while the churches have rest.
evidence: Describe how Saul escaped Damascus (9:23-25)
Say what Barnabas did for Saul (9:26-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Saul was accepted by the disciples in Jerusalem?

topics.name: Peter heals Aeneas and raises Dorcas
topics.description: Peter heals the paralysed Aeneas at Lydda in the name of Jesus Christ and many turn to the Lord. At Joppa he kneels, prays, and says "Tabitha, arise" to the disciple Dorcas, who is presented alive, and many believe.
evidence: Describe the two miracles Peter did (9:34, 9:40)
Say what Dorcas was known for (9:36, 9:39)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell the stories of Aeneas and Dorcas and what people did afterward?

topics.name: Cornelius and Peter see visions
topics.description: Cornelius, a devout centurion at Caesarea, is told by an angel to send for Simon Peter at Joppa. Meanwhile Peter sees a sheet of animals let down from heaven and is told what God has cleansed not to call common, and the Spirit tells him to go with the three men.
evidence: Describe Cornelius' vision and what he did (10:3-8)
Say what the voice told Peter and what it meant for his actions (10:13-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the two visions and how they brought Peter and Cornelius together?

topics.name: Peter preaches to Cornelius and the Gentiles receive the Spirit
topics.description: Peter tells Cornelius' household that God is no respecter of persons and that everyone who believes in Jesus receives remission of sins. While he is speaking the Holy Ghost falls on the Gentiles, and Peter commands them to be baptized.
evidence: State what Peter says about God and every nation (10:34-35)
Explain why Peter orders the Gentiles to be baptized (10:44-48)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Peter preached to Cornelius and why he baptized the Gentiles?

topics.name: Peter explains himself in Jerusalem
topics.description: Believers in Judaea criticise Peter for eating with uncircumcised men, so he retells the vision and the Spirit falling on the Gentiles. Hearing it, they glorify God and say he has granted repentance unto life to the Gentiles also.
evidence: Say what the believers objected to (11:2-3)
State the conclusion the church reached (11:17-18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Peter answered those who criticised him about the Gentiles?

topics.name: The church at Antioch and the first Christians
topics.description: Scattered believers preach the Lord Jesus to Greeks at Antioch and a great number believe; Barnabas is sent, finds Saul at Tarsus, and they teach there a year, where the disciples are first called Christians. The Antioch disciples send relief to Judaea after Agabus foretells a famine.
evidence: Say where the disciples were first called Christians (11:26)
Describe what the Antioch church did when famine was foretold (11:27-30)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the Antioch church began and what it did for the brethren in Judaea?

topics.name: James killed and Peter freed from prison
topics.description: Herod kills James and imprisons Peter, but the church prays unceasingly. An angel leads Peter out past the guards at night, and he comes to the house of Mary, where Rhoda is so glad she forgets to open the gate and the astonished believers at last let him in.
evidence: Describe how Peter was brought out of prison (12:6-10)
Say what the church was doing and how they reacted (12:5, 12:12-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how God rescued Peter and what the church was doing at the time?

topics.name: Herod's death and the word of God grows
topics.description: Herod, in royal apparel, receives the people's shout that he speaks as a god; the angel of the Lord strikes him because he gave not God the glory. The word of God grows and multiplies, and Barnabas and Saul return with John Mark.
evidence: Say why Herod was struck down (12:22-23)
Contrast Herod's end with what happened to the word of God (12:24)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Herod died and what happened to the word of God?

topics.name: Barnabas and Saul are sent out from Antioch
topics.description: The Holy Ghost tells the Antioch prophets and teachers to separate Barnabas and Saul for the work, and the church fasts, prays and sends them. On Cyprus, Saul (also called Paul) strikes the sorcerer Elymas blind and the deputy Sergius Paulus believes.
evidence: Say how Barnabas and Saul were sent (13:2-4)
Describe what happened to Elymas and the deputy (13:8-12)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain who sent Barnabas and Saul out and what happened on Cyprus?

topics.name: Paul preaches in the synagogue at Pisidian Antioch
topics.description: Invited to speak after the reading of the law and prophets, Paul traces Israel's story from Egypt through the judges and David to Jesus, whom God raised from the dead. He declares forgiveness of sins and that by Jesus all who believe are justified from what the law of Moses could not justify.
evidence: Outline the history Paul recounts to reach Jesus (13:17-23)
State what Paul says is preached through Jesus (13:38-39)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} summarise Paul's sermon from Israel's history to forgiveness through Jesus?

topics.name: Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles
topics.description: Gentiles ask to hear more, and the next sabbath almost the whole city gathers; the envious Jews contradict, so Paul and Barnabas say they turn to the Gentiles, citing the Lord's command to be a light to them. The Gentiles rejoice, those ordained to eternal life believe, and the apostles are expelled.
evidence: Say why Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles (13:45-47)
Describe how the Gentiles and the disciples responded (13:48, 13:52)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles at Antioch?

topics.name: Iconium and Lystra: healing, worship refused, stoning
topics.description: At Iconium many believe but the city is divided and the apostles flee. At Lystra Paul heals a man lame from birth and the crowd calls them gods; the apostles stop the sacrifice and preach the living God who made heaven and earth, but Jews from Antioch and Iconium turn the people and stone Paul, who rises up and goes on.
evidence: Say how Paul and Barnabas responded when the people wanted to sacrifice to them (14:14-18)
Describe what happened to Paul after the healing (14:19-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Lystra and what the apostles said to the crowd?

topics.name: The return to Antioch: elders appointed
topics.description: Paul and Barnabas return through the cities, confirming the disciples, warning that entering the kingdom is through much tribulation, and ordaining elders in every church with prayer and fasting. Back at Antioch they report that God had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
evidence: Say what the apostles told the disciples about tribulation (14:22)
Describe the report given at Antioch (14:26-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Paul and Barnabas did on their way back and what they reported?

topics.name: The Jerusalem council on circumcision
topics.description: Men from Judaea teach that Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved, so Paul and Barnabas go to Jerusalem. Peter recalls God giving the Gentiles the Holy Ghost and says salvation is through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ; James cites the prophets and judges that Gentile believers should not be troubled, only asked to abstain from idols, fornication, strangled things and blood.
evidence: State the question that began the dispute (15:1, 15:5)
Say what Peter and James each concluded (15:7-11, 15:13-19)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the question the Jerusalem council settled and how they answered it?

topics.name: The letter to the Gentile churches
topics.description: The apostles and elders send Judas Barsabas and Silas with Paul and Barnabas, carrying a letter saying that it seemed good to the Holy Ghost and to them to lay no greater burden than the necessary things. The Antioch believers read it and rejoice.
evidence: Say who delivered the letter and what it asked of Gentile believers (15:22-29)
Describe how Antioch received it (15:30-32)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the letter from Jerusalem said and how Antioch responded?

topics.name: Paul and Barnabas part ways
topics.description: Paul proposes revisiting the churches, and Barnabas wants to take John Mark, whom Paul will not take since he left them in Pamphylia. The contention is so sharp that they separate; Barnabas takes Mark to Cyprus and Paul takes Silas through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
evidence: Say what the disagreement was about (15:37-38)
Describe where each pair went (15:39-41)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why Paul and Barnabas separated and who went with each?

topics.name: Timothy joins and the call to Macedonia
topics.description: At Lystra Paul takes Timothy, whose mother is a believing Jewess and whose father is Greek, and circumcises him because of the Jews there, while delivering the Jerusalem decrees. Forbidden by the Spirit to go to Asia or Bithynia, Paul sees a vision of a man of Macedonia and concludes the Lord has called them to preach there.
evidence: Say why Paul circumcised Timothy (16:3)
Describe how the Spirit directed the journey (16:6-10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Paul was led to go to Macedonia?

topics.name: Lydia's heart is opened at Philippi
topics.description: At Philippi on the sabbath Paul speaks to women by the river, and the Lord opens the heart of Lydia, a seller of purple who worshipped God. She and her household are baptized, and she constrains the missionaries to stay in her house.
evidence: Say who Lydia was and how she came to believe (16:14)
Describe what she did after being baptized (16:15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Lydia came to believe at Philippi?

topics.name: Paul and Silas in the Philippian jail
topics.description: After Paul casts a spirit out of a slave girl, her owners have Paul and Silas beaten and jailed. At midnight they pray and sing, an earthquake opens the doors, and the jailer asks what he must do to be saved; they tell him to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and he and his household are baptized.
evidence: Describe what Paul and Silas did in the prison at midnight (16:25)
Give the jailer's question and the answer (16:30-31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened in the Philippian jail and how the jailer was saved?

topics.name: Paul insists on his rights as a Roman
topics.description: The magistrates send word to let Paul and Silas go, but Paul says they were beaten openly uncondemned, being Romans, and demands that the magistrates come themselves. The magistrates fear and ask them to leave, and the pair visit Lydia's house and encourage the brethren before departing.
evidence: Say what Paul demanded and why (16:37)
Describe the magistrates' reaction (16:38-39)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Paul would not leave the Philippian prison quietly?

topics.name: Thessalonica and Berea: reasoning from the scriptures
topics.description: At Thessalonica Paul reasons from the scriptures for three sabbaths that Christ must suffer and rise again; some believe but jealous Jews raise an uproar against Jason's house. At Berea the Jews receive the word readily and search the scriptures daily to see whether these things are so, but opponents from Thessalonica follow.
evidence: Say what Paul argued from the scriptures (17:2-3)
Explain what made the Bereans noble (17:11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the Bereans did with Paul's message?

topics.name: Paul at the Areopagus in Athens
topics.description: Distressed by the idols of Athens, Paul is brought to the Areopagus, where he speaks of the altar to the unknown God. He says God who made the world does not dwell in temples, gave life and breath to all, made all nations of one blood, commands all men to repent, and will judge the world by the man he raised from the dead; some mock, and some believe.
evidence: Say what Paul tells the Athenians about the God who made the world (17:24-28)
State the command and the warning in 17:30-31
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} summarise what Paul said to the Athenians about God, repentance and judgment?

topics.name: Paul at Corinth
topics.description: At Corinth Paul works with Aquila and Priscilla and reasons in the synagogue; when the Jews oppose, he goes to the Gentiles, and Crispus the synagogue ruler believes. The Lord tells him in a night vision not to be afraid, for he has much people in the city, and Gallio dismisses the Jews' charge against him.
evidence: Say what the Lord told Paul in the night (18:9-10)
Describe how Gallio handled the accusation (18:14-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Paul at Corinth and what the Lord told him?

topics.name: Apollos is taught more perfectly
topics.description: Paul sails to Ephesus, Caesarea and Antioch and then strengthens the disciples in Galatia and Phrygia. Apollos, an eloquent man mighty in the scriptures who knows only the baptism of John, is taken aside by Aquila and Priscilla, who expound the way of God to him more perfectly, and he helps the believers in Achaia.
evidence: Say what Apollos knew and lacked (18:24-25)
Describe what Aquila and Priscilla did for him (18:26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Apollos was helped by Priscilla and Aquila?

topics.name: Paul at Ephesus: the twelve disciples and the school of Tyrannus
topics.description: Paul finds about twelve disciples at Ephesus who know only John's baptism; they are baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, and when Paul lays hands on them the Holy Ghost comes and they speak with tongues and prophesy. Paul then reasons for two years, so that all in Asia hear the word of the Lord Jesus.
evidence: Say what the disciples had and had not received (19:2-5)
Describe where and how long Paul taught after leaving the synagogue (19:9-10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the twelve disciples at Ephesus?

topics.name: Miracles at Ephesus and the burning of the books
topics.description: God works special miracles through Paul, and the seven sons of Sceva who try to use the name of Jesus over an evil spirit are overpowered. Fear falls on Ephesus, the name of the Lord Jesus is magnified, and believers burn their magic books worth fifty thousand pieces of silver.
evidence: Say what happened to the sons of Sceva (19:13-16)
Describe how the believers responded (19:17-19)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the sons of Sceva and what the believers did with their books?

topics.name: The riot of the silversmiths at Ephesus
topics.description: Demetrius the silversmith, whose trade in shrines for Diana is threatened by Paul's teaching that gods made with hands are no gods, stirs up the craftsmen. The whole city rushes into the theatre shouting "Great is Diana", until the town clerk quiets the crowd and says that disputes belong to the law courts and a lawful assembly.
evidence: Say what Demetrius said was at stake (19:24-27)
Explain how the town clerk calmed the crowd (19:35-41)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the craftsmen at Ephesus were angry and how the riot ended?

topics.name: Eutychus falls from the window at Troas
topics.description: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece to Troas, where the disciples meet on the first day of the week to break bread. Paul speaks until midnight, young Eutychus falls from a third-floor window and is taken up dead, and Paul embraces him and tells them his life is in him.
evidence: Describe what happened to Eutychus (20:9-10)
Say what the disciples were doing when Paul preached (20:7)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what happened to Eutychus while Paul was preaching?

topics.name: Paul's farewell to the Ephesian elders
topics.description: At Miletus Paul calls the Ephesian elders and recalls his service and teaching in Asia, telling them he goes bound in the Spirit to Jerusalem. He charges them to feed the church of God, warns of grievous wolves arising even from among them, commends them to God and the word of his grace, and recalls that it is more blessed to give than to receive.
evidence: Say what Paul told the elders to do and why (20:28-31)
Describe how the elders and Paul parted (20:36-38)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Paul's charge to the Ephesian elders and the warnings he gave?

topics.name: Warnings along the road to Jerusalem
topics.description: Paul sails to Tyre, where disciples tell him through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem, and stays at Caesarea with Philip the evangelist. The prophet Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul's girdle and says the Jews will bind him; Paul replies that he is ready to die for the name of the Lord Jesus, and they say the will of the Lord be done.
evidence: Say what Agabus did and said (21:10-11)
Explain Paul's answer to those who begged him not to go (21:13-14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the warnings Paul received on his way to Jerusalem and how he answered?

topics.name: Paul and the vow in the temple
topics.description: At Jerusalem James and the elders glorify God for Paul's report, but tell him that thousands of Jews zealous for the law have heard he teaches against Moses. They advise him to join four men with a vow, and restate that Gentile believers need keep only the things in the earlier letter; Paul does so in the temple.
evidence: Say what rumour the elders mention and what they advised (21:20-24)
Restate the instruction about Gentile believers (21:25)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why James and the elders advised Paul to take part in the vow?

topics.name: Paul is seized in the temple and arrested
topics.description: Jews from Asia stir up the people against Paul, saying he teaches against the people, the law and the place and has brought Greeks into the temple. They drag him out to kill him, the chief captain rescues him and binds him with chains, and Paul asks leave to speak to the people.
evidence: Describe the charges of the Asian Jews (21:28-29)
Say how Paul was saved from the mob (21:31-33)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why Paul was seized in the temple and how he was rescued?

topics.name: Paul tells his story to the crowd
topics.description: Speaking in Hebrew from the stairs, Paul tells of his upbringing under Gamaliel, his persecution of the Way, the vision on the Damascus road, and Ananias' words. He says that in the temple the Lord told him to depart because he would be sent far to the Gentiles, and at that word the crowd cries out for his death.
evidence: Summarise the parts of his life Paul describes (22:3-5, 22:6-16)
Say which word made the crowd shout (22:21-22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell Paul's own account of how he came to follow Jesus and why the crowd shouted?

topics.name: Paul declares he is a Roman
topics.description: As the chief captain orders Paul to be examined by scourging, Paul asks the centurion whether it is lawful to scourge a Roman uncondemned. The chief captain is afraid on learning that Paul is a Roman, freeborn, and next day sets him before the chief priests and council.
evidence: Say what Paul asked the centurion (22:25)
Describe how the chief captain reacted (22:26-29)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Paul's Roman citizenship affected his treatment?

topics.name: Paul before the council: the resurrection
topics.description: Paul tells the council he has lived in all good conscience, and when the high priest orders him struck, he rebukes him and then says he did not know he was the high priest. Perceiving Sadducees and Pharisees, he says he is called in question for the hope of the resurrection, the council divides, and the Lord stands by him that night to say he must bear witness at Rome.
evidence: Say how Paul divided the council (23:6-9)
State what the Lord told Paul that night (23:11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Paul used the question of the resurrection before the council?

topics.name: The plot against Paul and his transfer to Caesarea
topics.description: More than forty Jews bind themselves by a curse to neither eat nor drink till they have killed Paul. Paul's sister's son tells the chief captain, who sends Paul by night with a large escort and a letter to Felix at Caesarea.
evidence: Describe the plot and who uncovered it (23:12-16)
Say what the chief captain's letter reports (23:26-30)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the plot against Paul was discovered and how he was kept safe?

topics.name: Paul before Felix
topics.description: The high priest and the orator Tertullus accuse Paul before Felix; Paul answers that he worships the God of his fathers, believes the law and the prophets, and hopes for a resurrection of the just and unjust. Felix trembles when Paul reasons of righteousness, temperance and judgment to come, but defers him and leaves him bound for two years.
evidence: Say what Paul confessed about the way he worships (24:14-16)
Describe Felix's response and how long Paul stayed bound (24:25-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Paul defended himself before Felix and how Felix responded?

topics.name: Paul appeals to Caesar
topics.description: Festus succeeds Felix and the Jews ask that Paul be sent to Jerusalem, intending an ambush. Paul says he has not offended against the law, the temple or Caesar, refuses to be handed over, and appeals to Caesar; Festus answers that he will go to Caesar.
evidence: Say what Paul said when Festus proposed a trial at Jerusalem (25:9-11)
Give Festus' decision (25:12)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Paul appealed to Caesar?

topics.name: Festus lays Paul's case before King Agrippa
topics.description: King Agrippa and Bernice visit Festus, who explains that the accusers brought no charge he expected, only questions about their religion and about one Jesus who was dead whom Paul affirmed to be alive. Agrippa wishes to hear Paul and Festus brings him forth, saying he has no certain thing to write to Caesar.
evidence: Say how Festus summarised the case (25:18-19)
State why Festus brought Paul before Agrippa (25:26-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Festus told Agrippa about Paul's case?

topics.name: Paul's defence before Agrippa
topics.description: Paul tells Agrippa of his life as a Pharisee, his persecution of the saints and the vision on the road to Damascus, where Jesus sends him to open eyes and turn Gentiles from darkness to light. He says he says nothing beyond what Moses and the prophets said, that Christ should suffer and rise first, and Agrippa answers "Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian".
evidence: State the commission Jesus gave Paul (26:16-18)
Say what Paul says the prophets and Moses foretold (26:22-23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell Paul's speech to Agrippa and how Agrippa replied?

topics.name: The voyage to Rome and the storm
topics.description: Paul and other prisoners are delivered to the centurion Julius and sail for Italy; Paul warns of danger but the centurion trusts the master of the ship. A tempest drives the ship for many days until all hope is lost, then an angel tells Paul he must stand before Caesar and that God has given him all who sail with him.
evidence: Say what Paul warned and who was believed (27:9-11)
Give the angel's message to Paul (27:23-25)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the storm began and what God told Paul in it?

topics.name: The shipwreck and the escape to land
topics.description: On the fourteenth night the sailors try to flee and Paul tells the centurion they must stay in the ship; Paul urges all to eat and gives thanks to God before them. The ship runs aground and breaks up, the centurion stops the soldiers from killing the prisoners, and all 276 reach land safe.
evidence: Describe what Paul urged before the wreck (27:31, 27:33-36)
Say what happened to the people on board (27:42-44)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how everyone on the ship came safely to land?

topics.name: Paul on Malta
topics.description: The islanders show kindness; when a viper fastens on Paul's hand he shakes it off unharmed, and they change their minds and say he is a god. Paul prays for and heals the father of Publius and others on the island.
evidence: Describe the viper and the islanders' two opinions (28:3-6)
Say what Paul did for Publius' father (28:8)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Paul on Malta?

topics.name: Paul arrives at Rome
topics.description: After three months the party sails in a ship of Alexandria and lands at Puteoli, where they find brethren. Believers from Rome come to meet Paul on the road, and he thanks God and takes courage; at Rome he is allowed to dwell by himself with a soldier.
evidence: Say how the Roman brethren met Paul (28:15)
Describe the conditions of his stay at Rome (28:16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Paul arrived at Rome and who welcomed him?

topics.name: Paul preaches in Rome
topics.description: Paul tells the Jewish leaders at Rome that he is bound for the hope of Israel and expounds the kingdom of God from Moses and the prophets, with some believing and others not. He quotes Isaiah on hardened hearts, says salvation is sent to the Gentiles, and for two years receives all who come, preaching with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
evidence: Say how the Jews divided in response (28:24-25)
Describe how the book ends (28:30-31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Paul did and said at Rome and how Acts ends?

topics.name: James: overview
topics.description: James is a letter from James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, with practical teaching on trials, living faith, the tongue, humility, wealth and patience.
evidence: Name the main themes of James in order
Say who the letter is from and to whom it is written
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what James tells believers to do with trials, words and wealth?

topics.name: Trials, wisdom and the crown of life
topics.description: James says to count trials as joy because tested faith produces patience, to ask God for wisdom without wavering, and promises the crown of life to the one who endures.
evidence: Explain what testing of faith produces
Say how James tells believers to ask for wisdom
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why James says to count it all joy when trials come?

topics.name: Temptation, the word and doing it
topics.description: James says God does not tempt anyone; desire gives birth to sin and sin to death, while every good gift comes from the Father of lights who gave new birth by the word of truth, and believers must be doers of the word.
evidence: Describe the path from desire to death in 1:14-15
Contrast hearing the word with doing it
State what James calls pure religion
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between hearing the word and doing it?

topics.name: No partiality: the royal law
topics.description: James rebukes giving the rich seats of honour and shaming the poor in the assembly, reminds them God chose the poor rich in faith, and calls loving your neighbour the royal law.
evidence: Describe the example of partiality in the assembly
Say what James calls the royal law
Explain why partiality is sin according to 2:9
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what James says is wrong with favouring the rich over the poor?

topics.name: Faith and works
topics.description: James argues that faith without works is dead, using the demons who believe, Abraham offering Isaac, and Rahab, and concludes a man is justified by works and not by faith only.
evidence: Explain what James means by faith that is alone and dead
Retell how Abraham and Rahab are used as examples
Compare the wording of James 2:24 with Romans 3:28 and 4:2-3
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what James is arguing about the kind of faith that is dead?

topics.name: The tongue
topics.description: James warns that few should be teachers, compares the tongue to a bit, a rudder and a fire, and says it cannot be tamed by man yet is used both to bless God and curse people.
evidence: Name the three pictures James uses for the tongue
Say what inconsistency James points out in 3:9-10
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say why James calls the tongue a fire?

topics.name: Wisdom from above and earthly wisdom
topics.description: James contrasts envy and strife, which he calls earthly, sensual and devilish wisdom, with wisdom from above, which is pure, peaceable, gentle and full of mercy and good fruits.
evidence: List the marks of wisdom from above
Describe what comes with bitter envying and strife
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how to tell wisdom from above from earthly wisdom?

topics.name: Conflicts, the world and humbling before God
topics.description: James traces fightings to desires within, calls friendship with the world enmity with God, and says God gives grace to the humble, so believers must submit, resist the devil and draw near to God.
evidence: Say where James says wars and fightings come from
List the commands in 4:7-10
Explain what God does with the proud and the humble
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what James says to do instead of fighting and loving the world?

topics.name: Judging others and boasting about tomorrow
topics.description: James forbids speaking evil of a brother and judging him since there is one lawgiver, and rebukes plans made without saying if the Lord will, since life is a vapour.
evidence: Say why James says there is one lawgiver
Explain what James says we should say about our plans
State the point of 4:17
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why James says to say, If the Lord will?

topics.name: Warning to the rich who defraud
topics.description: James tells rich men to weep for coming miseries: their riches are corrupted, wages withheld from labourers cry out to the Lord of sabaoth, and they have lived in luxury and condemned the just.
evidence: Name the charges James brings against the rich in 5:1-6
Say who hears the cries of the harvest labourers
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what the rich are accused of in James 5:1-6?

topics.name: Patience until the coming of the Lord
topics.description: James urges patience like the farmer waiting for rain, points to the prophets and Job as examples, says the Lord is pitiful and merciful, and tells them not to swear oaths.
evidence: Describe the farmer picture of patience
Name the examples of endurance James gives
Say what James tells them about oaths
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why James says to be patient until the coming of the Lord?

topics.name: Prayer, healing and restoring the wanderer
topics.description: James tells the afflicted to pray, the sick to call the elders, believers to confess faults and pray for one another, cites Elijah as a man like us whose prayer was answered, and ends by urging restoring one who strays from the truth.
evidence: Describe what the sick are told to do in 5:14-15
Say how James uses Elijah
Explain what happens when someone turns a sinner from error
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what James says to do when someone is sick, sinning or wandering?

topics.name: 1 Peter: overview
topics.description: 1 Peter is a letter from the apostle Peter to scattered strangers in Asia Minor, written to encourage them in suffering with the living hope, the example of Christ, holy conduct and humility under God.
evidence: Say who wrote 1 Peter and to whom
Name the main themes: hope, holiness, suffering and humility
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how 1 Peter encourages believers who suffer?

topics.name: Born again to a living hope
topics.description: Peter blesses God who by the resurrection of Jesus has given new birth to a living hope and an inheritance kept in heaven, while faith is tested like gold and the prophets searched out this salvation.
evidence: Describe the inheritance in 1:4
Explain why trials test faith in 1:6-7
Say what the prophets searched into in 1:10-11
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what living hope Peter says believers have and why they can rejoice in trials?

topics.name: Be holy: redeemed by precious blood
topics.description: Peter calls believers to be holy as God is holy, reminds them they were redeemed by the precious blood of Christ the lamb without blemish, and says they were born again by the abiding word.
evidence: Say what Peter says redeemed them and what it was not
Explain the call to be holy in 1:15-16
Describe what the word of the Lord does according to 1:23-25
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Peter says paid the price for believers, and how they should live because of it?

topics.name: The living stone and the holy priesthood
topics.description: Peter calls Christ the living stone chosen by God, says believers are built up as a spiritual house and royal priesthood, and says they were once not a people but are now the people of God.
evidence: Explain the stone picture in 2:4-8
List the names Peter gives believers in 2:9
Say what 2:10 says changed for them
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name three things Peter calls believers in 1 Peter 2:9?

topics.name: Strangers and pilgrims: honourable conduct and submission
topics.description: Peter tells believers living as pilgrims among Gentiles to keep honest conduct, submit to rulers and honour all, and servants to be subject to masters even when treated wrongly.
evidence: Say why Peter tells them to keep honest conduct among the Gentiles
Describe how Peter says to treat the king and all men
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how Peter says believers should behave under authorities?

topics.name: Christ suffered for us, an example
topics.description: Peter says believers are called to follow the steps of Christ, who did not sin, did not revile in return, bore our sins on the tree, and brings the strayed sheep back to the Shepherd.
evidence: Describe how Christ responded when reviled
Say what Christ did on the tree in 2:24
Explain the sheep and Shepherd picture
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain both what Christ did for us and what example he left in 1 Peter 2:21-25?

topics.name: Wives, husbands and the hidden person of the heart
topics.description: Peter addresses wives with the example of Sarah and holy women, stressing a meek and quiet spirit as precious to God, and tells husbands to live with their wives with understanding and honour as fellow heirs of the grace of life.
evidence: Say what Peter calls the adorning of great price
Describe what husbands are told in 3:7
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Peter tells husbands and wives in 1 Peter 3:1-7?

topics.name: Blessing, good conscience and suffering for doing good
topics.description: Peter tells all to be of one mind and repay evil with blessing, says suffering for righteousness is blessed, and that believers should always be ready to give a reason for their hope with meekness and a good conscience.
evidence: Say how Peter tells believers to answer evil
Explain what being ready to answer for hope looks like in 3:15
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Peter says to respond when others speak evil of us?

topics.name: Christ suffered once, the days of Noah and baptism
topics.description: Peter says Christ suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, to bring us to God, and was made alive; he mentions the spirits who were disobedient in the days of Noah, the eight saved by water, and says baptism saves by the resurrection of Jesus, who is now at God's right hand.
evidence: Say why Christ suffered once according to 3:18
Retell what 3:20 says about Noah and the eight saved through water
State where Christ is now according to 3:22
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Peter 3:18-22 says about Christ and about Noah?

topics.name: Living to the will of God
topics.description: Peter says believers who have the mind of Christ in suffering should end the old life of Gentile excess, live to God, and prepare for the end by prayer, fervent love, hospitality and using gifts for God's glory.
evidence: Describe the old life Peter says to leave behind
List the commands in 4:7-11
Explain why gifts are to be used for God's glory
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list how Peter says to live because the end of all things is at hand?

topics.name: The fiery trial and suffering as a Christian
topics.description: Peter says not to be surprised by fiery trial but to rejoice in sharing Christ's sufferings, not to suffer as an evildoer, and to entrust the soul to a faithful Creator while judgment begins at the house of God.
evidence: Say how Peter tells believers to view fiery trials
Distinguish suffering as a Christian from suffering as an evildoer
Say whom believers entrust their souls to in 4:19
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says not to be surprised by a fiery trial?

topics.name: Shepherd the flock, humility and the roaring lion
topics.description: Peter exhorts elders to shepherd willingly as examples with the chief Shepherd coming, tells all to be clothed with humility, cast cares on God, resist the devil who prowls like a roaring lion, and ends with greetings from Babylon.
evidence: Describe how elders are to lead in 5:2-3
Say what Peter tells believers to do with their cares
Say how Peter describes the devil and how to resist him
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what Peter tells elders and everyone else to do in chapter 5?

topics.name: 2 Peter: overview
topics.description: 2 Peter is a letter from Simon Peter urging growth in the knowledge of Christ, warning against false teachers and scoffers, and pointing to the certain day of the Lord and new heavens and a new earth.
evidence: Name the three sections: growth, false teachers, the day of the Lord
Say what Peter wants believers to remember
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what 2 Peter warns about and what it tells believers to do?

topics.name: Precious promises and growing in godliness
topics.description: Peter says God has given all that pertains to life and godliness and great promises, and tells believers to add virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness and charity to faith so they are fruitful and make their calling sure.
evidence: List the qualities to add to faith in 1:5-7
Say what Peter says God has given in 1:3-4
Explain what lacking these things means in 1:9
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list the qualities Peter says to add to faith?

topics.name: Eyewitnesses and the sure word of prophecy
topics.description: Peter says he will remind believers before his death, that the apostles were eyewitnesses of Christ's majesty when the Father's voice spoke on the holy mount, and that prophecy of scripture came from men moved by the Holy Ghost.
evidence: Say what the apostles saw and heard on the holy mount
Explain where Peter says prophecy of scripture came from
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says the apostles did not follow cunningly devised fables?

topics.name: False teachers and the examples of judgment
topics.description: Peter warns that false teachers will bring in destructive heresies out of covetousness, and shows that God judged sinning angels, the old world in Noah's day, and Sodom and Gomorrah while delivering Noah and Lot.
evidence: Describe what the false teachers do and why
List the three examples of judgment in 2:4-6
Say who God delivered in 2:5-9
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what examples Peter uses to show God judges the ungodly and rescues the godly?

topics.name: The character and end of the false teachers
topics.description: Peter describes the false teachers as presumptuous, greedy and following Balaam, promising freedom while enslaved to corruption, and says to return to the way of righteousness after knowing it is worse than never knowing it.
evidence: Name the charges in 2:13-15
Explain the saying about the dog and the sow in 2:22
Say who Peter compares them to in 2:15-16
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Peter portrays the false teachers and why turning back is so serious?

topics.name: Scoffers and the longsuffering of the Lord
topics.description: Peter says scoffers will ask where the promised coming is, recalls that the world once perished by water and the present heavens and earth are kept for fire, and says the Lord delays because he is longsuffering, not willing that any perish.
evidence: Say what the scoffers claim in 3:4
Explain what Peter says they forget in 3:5-7
Say why the Lord has not yet come, according to 3:9
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says the Lord seems slow to keep his promise?

topics.name: The day of the Lord and new heavens and earth
topics.description: Peter says the day of the Lord will come like a thief with fire dissolving the heavens and the elements, so believers should live in holiness and look for new heavens and a new earth where righteousness dwells, and grow in grace.
evidence: Describe how the day of the Lord comes
Say what kind of people Peter says we ought to be in 3:11
Say what new thing believers look for in 3:13
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how Peter tells believers to live while they wait for the day of the Lord?

topics.name: 1 John: overview
topics.description: 1 John is a letter written so that believers may have fellowship with the Father and the Son, know they have eternal life, walk in the light, love one another, and hold to the truth that Jesus is the Christ come in the flesh.
evidence: Name the main themes: light, love, truth about Jesus, assurance
Say what John says he wrote so that in 5:13
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what 1 John wants believers to know?

topics.name: Fellowship, walking in the light and confessing sin
topics.description: John declares the Word of life that he has heard, seen and touched, says God is light, and teaches that walking in the light brings cleansing by the blood of Jesus and that confessed sins are forgiven.
evidence: Say what John says he saw and heard
Explain what God is according to 1:5
Describe what happens when we confess sins in 1:9
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what John says to do when we sin?

topics.name: Our advocate and keeping his commandments
topics.description: John writes that we may not sin, but if anyone sins we have an advocate, Jesus Christ the righteous, the propitiation for our sins and the whole world, and that knowing him is shown by keeping his commandments.
evidence: Name what Jesus is called in 2:1-2
Say how we know that we know him
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say who our advocate is and how we know we know him?

topics.name: The old and new commandment: light and hatred
topics.description: John says the commandment to love is old and yet new because the true light shines, and that hating a brother means walking in darkness while loving a brother abides in the light.
evidence: Contrast loving and hating a brother in light and darkness
Say who John addresses in 2:12-14
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how John connects loving a brother with being in the light?

topics.name: Not loving the world, and antichrists
topics.description: John tells believers not to love the world, since its lust of the flesh, lust of the eyes and pride of life pass away, and warns of many antichrists who went out from them, while the anointing from the Holy One teaches them.
evidence: List what John says is in the world
Say who John calls antichrist in 2:22
Describe what he says about those who left in 2:19
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what John says about the world and about those who deny the Son?

topics.name: Abiding in him and being children of God
topics.description: John urges abiding in Christ with confidence at his appearing, says we are now sons of God and shall be like him, and that Christ appeared to take away sins and destroy the works of the devil.
evidence: Say what we shall be when he appears
Explain why the Son of God was manifested according to 3:8
Contrast the children of God with the children of the devil
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what John says about being God's children now and later?

topics.name: Love in deed and truth, assurance and the commandment
topics.description: John says love is the message from the beginning, unlike Cain who killed his brother, that Christ laid down his life for us so we ought to love in deed and truth, and that God is greater than a condemning heart.
evidence: Say how John contrasts Cain with the love Christ showed
Explain what loving in deed and truth means in 3:17-18
State the commandment in 3:23
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what John means by loving not in word only but in deed and in truth?

topics.name: Testing the spirits
topics.description: John tells believers to test every spirit, says the spirit of God confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, and says those in them have overcome because greater is he that is in them than he that is in the world.
evidence: Say how to test a spirit according to 4:2-3
Explain why believers have overcome in 4:4
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how John tells us to test what teachers say?

topics.name: God is love
topics.description: John says love is of God and God is love, shown when God sent his only Son as propitiation, that we love because he first loved us, and that perfect love casts out fear and one who hates a brother cannot love God.
evidence: Say how God showed his love in 4:9-10
Explain 4:19
Describe what John says about loving God and hating a brother
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how John says we know that God is love?

topics.name: Born of God, overcoming and the witness to the Son
topics.description: John says everyone who believes Jesus is the Christ is born of God and overcomes the world through faith, and the witness of God about his Son is that God gave eternal life in the Son.
evidence: Say what overcomes the world in 5:4
State the record God gave in 5:11
Say what 5:12 says about having the Son
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what John says is the witness God gave about his Son?

topics.name: Assurance, prayer and keeping from idols
topics.description: John says he wrote so believers may know they have eternal life, that God hears prayer according to his will, mentions sin not unto death and sin unto death, and ends by telling them to keep from idols.
evidence: Say why John wrote this letter according to 5:13
Describe the confidence in prayer in 5:14-15
State John's last command
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what John wants his readers to know about eternal life and prayer?

topics.name: 2 John: overview
topics.description: 2 John is a short letter from the elder to an elect lady and her children, about walking in truth and love and not receiving those who do not bring the doctrine of Christ.
evidence: Say who writes and who receives 2 John
Name its two concerns: love and truth
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what 2 John tells believers about truth and love?

topics.name: Walk in truth and love; beware of deceivers
topics.description: The elder rejoices that the children walk in truth, repeats the commandment to love, warns of deceivers who deny Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, and says not to receive those who bring no such doctrine.
evidence: Say what the commandment from the beginning is in 2JN 1:5-6
Describe the deceivers in 2JN 1:7
Say what the elder says to do about visitors without the doctrine
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 2 John says to love and also to be careful about false teachers?

topics.name: 3 John: overview
