evidence: Name several qualifications in 3:2-7
Say how deacons are to be proved (3:10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list some qualities of an overseer in 3:2-7 and say why household management matters (3:5)?

topics.name: The church and the mystery of godliness
topics.description: Paul writes so Timothy may know how to behave in the house of God, the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and states the mystery of godliness: God manifest in the flesh, received up into glory.
evidence: Say how 3:15 describes the church
List the six statements about Christ in 3:16
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name what Paul says about Christ in 1 Timothy 3:16?

topics.name: Departing from the faith: good creation received with thanks
topics.description: The Spirit says some will depart from the faith, forbidding marriage and certain foods; Paul says every creature of God is good and sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
evidence: State what the false teachers forbid (4:3)
Explain why 4:4-5 says food is not to be refused
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says nothing is to be refused if received with thanksgiving (4:4-5)?

topics.name: A good minister of Jesus Christ
topics.description: Timothy is to refuse profane fables, train himself in godliness, set an example in word, conduct, love, faith and purity, devote himself to reading, exhortation and doctrine, and not neglect his gift.
evidence: Recite or paraphrase 4:12
List the three things in 4:13
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Paul tells Timothy to do so that no one despises his youth (4:12-16)?

topics.name: Honouring widows and caring for family
topics.description: Timothy is to treat people of every age with respect, honour widows who are truly widows, expect families to care for their own, and set guidelines for enrolling widows and for younger widows.
evidence: State what 5:8 says about providing for one's own
Describe the tasks of a widow indeed (5:5, 5:10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain who is to care for widows according to 5:4 and 5:16?

topics.name: Elders: honour, accusation and impartiality
topics.description: Elders who rule well are worthy of double honour; an accusation against an elder needs two or three witnesses; Timothy is to rebuke sin openly, act without partiality, and not lay hands hastily.
evidence: Say how 5:18 supports honouring elders
State the rule about accusations in 5:19
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says an accusation against an elder should be handled (5:19-21)?

topics.name: Servants, false gain, and godliness with contentment
topics.description: Servants are to honour their masters; those who teach otherwise and suppose gain is godliness are to be avoided; godliness with contentment is great gain, and the love of money is a root of all evil.
evidence: Recite 6:6-8
Explain what 6:10 says about the love of money
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about godliness with contentment and the love of money (6:6-10)?

topics.name: Fight the good fight; charge to the rich
topics.description: Timothy, a man of God, is to flee these things, pursue righteousness and godliness, fight the good fight of faith and keep the commandment until Christ's appearing; the rich are to trust the living God and do good.
evidence: List what Timothy flees and follows (6:11)
State what the rich are told in 6:17-19
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Paul charges Timothy to do in 6:11-14?

topics.name: 1 Timothy: overview
topics.description: Paul's letter to Timothy at Ephesus about sound doctrine, prayer, order in the church, qualified leaders, and a minister's conduct and charge.
evidence: Describe how 3:15 states the letter's purpose
Name the main sections: false teaching, prayer and conduct, leaders, Timothy's ministry, groups in the church, closing charge
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what 1 Timothy is about (see 3:14-15)?

topics.name: Stir up the gift; do not be ashamed of the gospel
topics.description: Paul remembers Timothy's sincere faith and tells him to stir up God's gift, not be ashamed of the testimony, and share in the afflictions of the gospel, since God saved and called us by his own purpose and grace and Christ brought life and immortality to light.
evidence: Say whose faith dwelt in Timothy first (1:5)
Explain how 1:9-10 describes salvation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Paul tells Timothy to do in 1:6-8 and why (1:9-10)?

topics.name: Those who turned away and Onesiphorus who refreshed Paul
topics.description: Paul notes that all in Asia have turned away from him, including Phygellus and Hermogenes, while Onesiphorus often refreshed him and sought him out in Rome.
evidence: Contrast the two groups in 1:15-16
Tell what Onesiphorus did in Rome (1:17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Onesiphorus did for Paul and why Paul prays for him (1:16-18)?

topics.name: Strong in grace: soldier, athlete, farmer
topics.description: Timothy is to pass on what he heard to faithful men, endure hardness as a good soldier, strive lawfully like an athlete and labour like a farmer; Paul endures for the elect, and the faithful saying says if we die with him we shall live with him.
evidence: Name the three pictures in 2:3-6
Recite the faithful saying of 2:11-13
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the soldier, athlete and farmer pictures in 2:3-6 and what they teach?

topics.name: A workman approved by God
topics.description: Timothy is to avoid wrangling about words and profane babblings, rightly handle the word of truth, and flee youthful lusts; the Lord's servant must be gentle and patient, instructing opponents in hope that God grants repentance.
evidence: State the goal of 2:15
Describe how the Lord's servant treats opponents (2:24-26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what it means to be a workman who rightly divides the word of truth (2:15)?

topics.name: Perilous times in the last days
topics.description: Paul describes men in the last days with a form of godliness but denying its power, compares them to Jannes and Jambres who withstood Moses, and says they will not progress further.
evidence: List several marks of the men in 3:2-4
Say who Jannes and Jambres are compared to (3:8)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what Paul says about people in the last days and what Timothy should do about them (3:1-5)?

topics.name: Continue in Scripture, inspired by God
topics.description: Timothy is to continue in what he learned, having known the holy scriptures from childhood; all scripture is given by inspiration of God and is profitable for teaching, reproof, correction and training in righteousness, so the man of God is thoroughly furnished.
evidence: Say what the scriptures are able to do (3:15)
List the four uses in 3:16
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what 3:16-17 says about Scripture and what it is for?

topics.name: Preach the word: Paul's charge and finished course
topics.description: Paul charges Timothy before God and Christ to preach the word in season and out, warns of those who will not endure sound doctrine, and says he is ready to be offered, having fought the good fight and awaiting a crown of righteousness.
evidence: Recite 4:2
Describe what Paul says of his own course in 4:6-8
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Paul charges Timothy to do and what Paul says awaits him (4:2, 4:7-8)?

topics.name: Paul's last requests and greetings
topics.description: Paul asks Timothy to come, names companions who left or remain, recounts that none stood with him at his first answer but the Lord stood with him, and sends greetings.
evidence: Say who is with Paul in 4:11
Tell who stood with Paul at his first answer (4:16-17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say who stood with Paul at his first defence and what he asks Timothy to bring (4:11-17)?

topics.name: 2 Timothy: overview
topics.description: Paul's last letter in this collection, written as a prisoner to Timothy, urging faithfulness, endurance, trust in Scripture and preaching the word until the end.
evidence: Describe the four chapters: not ashamed (1), endure and handle the word (2), Scripture in the last days (3), the charge and Paul's last words (4)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what 2 Timothy is about?

topics.name: Elders in every city of Crete
topics.description: Paul greets Titus, mentions the hope of eternal life promised before the world began, and tells him he left him in Crete to appoint elders who are blameless and hold fast the faithful word.
evidence: State why Paul left Titus in Crete (1:5)
List some qualities of an elder in 1:6-9
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Paul left Titus in Crete and what kind of men were to be elders (1:5-9)?

topics.name: Rebuking the unruly teachers
topics.description: Many unruly talkers, especially of the circumcision, subvert households for gain; Titus is to rebuke them sharply, since they profess to know God but deny him by their works.
evidence: Say what these teachers do (1:11)
Explain 1:16
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about those who profess to know God but deny him by works (1:16)?

topics.name: Sound doctrine in every household
topics.description: Titus is to teach what fits sound doctrine to older men and women, younger women and men, and servants, and to be a pattern of good works himself.
evidence: Name the groups in 2:2-10
State why Titus must be an example (2:7-8)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Paul wants the different groups to live and why (2:5, 2:8, 2:10)?

topics.name: The grace of God has appeared
topics.description: The grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all men, teaching us to deny ungodliness and live soberly while looking for the glorious appearing of our great God and Saviour Jesus Christ, who gave himself to redeem and purify a people for himself.
evidence: Say what grace teaches in 2:12
State what Christ gave himself to do in 2:14
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Titus 2:11-14 says grace teaches us and what Christ did for us?

topics.name: Saved by mercy, not by works
topics.description: Believers once lived in folly and malice, but God our Saviour saved them according to his mercy, not works, through the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Ghost, that they might be justified by grace and be heirs; they are to be careful to maintain good works.
evidence: Say what 3:5 says saved us and what it says did not
Describe how believers are to treat others (3:1-2)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Titus 3:4-7 says about how God saved us?

topics.name: Avoiding division, and final instructions
topics.description: Titus is to avoid foolish questions and genealogies, reject a divisive man after two admonitions, and Paul closes with travel instructions, names of helpers and greetings.
evidence: State what to do with a divisive man (3:10)
Name people mentioned in 3:12-13
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Paul says to avoid and what to do after admonishing a divisive person twice (3:9-10)?

topics.name: Titus: overview
topics.description: Paul's letter to Titus in Crete about appointing elders, opposing unruly teachers, sound doctrine in daily life, and salvation by grace that leads to good works.
evidence: Describe the three chapters: order and elders (1), sound doctrine and grace (2), mercy and good works (3)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Titus is about?

topics.name: Greeting and thanks for Philemon's love
topics.description: Paul and Timothy greet Philemon, Apphia, Archippus and the church in his house, and Paul thanks God for Philemon's love and faith toward the Lord Jesus and all saints.
evidence: Name the people greeted in 1:1-2
Say what Paul has heard of Philemon (1:5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Paul thanks God for about Philemon (1:4-7)?

topics.name: Paul appeals for Onesimus
topics.description: Paul, an aged prisoner, urges Philemon out of love to receive Onesimus, whom he begot in his bonds, no longer as a servant but as a beloved brother.
evidence: State how Paul describes Onesimus in 1:10-11
Say how Paul wants Philemon to receive him (1:16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Paul asks Philemon to do about Onesimus and why he asks by love rather than command (1:8-16)?

topics.name: Receive him as myself
topics.description: Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus as he would receive Paul, offers to repay anything Onesimus owes, expresses confidence in Philemon, and sends greetings from his companions.
evidence: Say what Paul offers in 1:18-19
Name the fellow workers who send greetings (1:23-24)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Paul offers to do if Onesimus has wronged Philemon (1:17-19)?

topics.name: Philemon: overview
topics.description: Paul's short personal letter to Philemon, appealing on behalf of Onesimus.
evidence: Summarise the letter's one request in 1:10-17
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Philemon is about?

topics.name: God has spoken by his Son
topics.description: God who spoke by the prophets has in these last days spoken by his Son, heir of all things, maker of the worlds, radiance of his glory, who purged sins and sat at God's right hand, better than the angels.
evidence: List what 1:2-3 says about the Son
Say how 1:4-14 compares him with angels
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Hebrews 1:1-4 says about how God has spoken and who the Son is?

topics.name: Do not neglect so great salvation
topics.description: Because the word spoken through angels was steadfast, the readers must give heed to the salvation first spoken by the Lord and confirmed by those who heard him, with God bearing witness by signs and wonders.
evidence: State the question of 2:3
Say how the message was confirmed (2:3-4)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the warning of 2:1-3 and why it is serious?

topics.name: Jesus made like his brothers
topics.description: Jesus, made a little lower than the angels, tasted death for everyone, shared flesh and blood to destroy the devil and free those enslaved by fear of death, and became a merciful and faithful high priest able to help the tempted.
evidence: Say why he shared flesh and blood (2:14-15)
State what kind of high priest he is (2:17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus became like his brothers according to Hebrews 2:14-18?

topics.name: Christ greater than Moses
topics.description: Moses was faithful as a servant in God's house, but Christ is faithful as a Son over his own house, and believers are that house if they hold fast.
evidence: Compare servant and son in 3:5-6
Say what condition 3:6 states
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the text says Christ is greater than Moses (3:3-6)?

topics.name: Do not harden your hearts as in the wilderness
topics.description: Quoting the warning that God swore the generation that provoked him in the wilderness would not enter his rest, the writer urges them to beware an evil heart of unbelief and to exhort one another daily.
evidence: Say why that generation could not enter (3:19)
Describe what 3:12-13 tells the readers to do
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened to those who came out of Egypt and what warning the writer draws (3:16-19)?

topics.name: A rest remains for the people of God
topics.description: The promise of entering God's rest still stands: the gospel preached to them did not profit those without faith, God rested on the seventh day, and a Sabbath rest remains for God's people, so they must labour to enter it.
evidence: Cite the creation rest mentioned in 4:4
State what remains for the people of God (4:9)
Say what the word of God does in 4:12
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the rest is that remains for God's people, and what warning goes with it (4:9-11)?

topics.name: A great high priest who sympathises
topics.description: We have a great high priest, Jesus the Son of God, who passed into the heavens and was tempted in all points like us yet without sin, so we may come boldly to the throne of grace.
evidence: Say how Jesus is like and unlike us (4:15)
State where we may come (4:16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why we may come boldly to the throne of grace (4:14-16)?

topics.name: Called as high priest after Melchizedek's order
topics.description: Every high priest is taken from men to offer gifts and sacrifices and is called of God as Aaron was; Christ was so called, learned obedience through suffering, and became the source of eternal salvation, a priest after the order of Melchizedek.
evidence: List what a high priest does (5:1-3)
Say how Christ became a high priest (5:5-6, 5:10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the text says Christ was called to be high priest (5:4-10)?

topics.name: From milk to solid food: a warning and encouragement
topics.description: The writer says the readers are dull of hearing and need milk, urges them to go on to maturity, warns about falling away after being enlightened, and is persuaded of better things, praising their work of love and urging diligence and patience.
evidence: Contrast milk and strong meat (5:12-14)
Describe the two earth pictures of 6:7-8
Say what the writer is persuaded of (6:9-10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the writer asks the readers to do in 6:1 and why (5:11-14)?

topics.name: God's oath to Abraham: an anchor of the soul
topics.description: God promised Abraham and confirmed it by an oath, swearing by himself; by two unchangeable things the heirs of promise have strong comfort, a hope like an anchor that enters within the veil where Jesus has gone as forerunner, a high priest after Melchizedek's order.
evidence: State why God swore by himself (6:13)
Describe the anchor picture of 6:19-20
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the text says about God's promise and oath to Abraham, and why it gives us hope (6:13-19)?

topics.name: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest
topics.description: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, met Abraham, blessed him and received tithes; this shows he is greater than Abraham and the Levites, and is made like the Son of God, abiding a priest continually.
evidence: Retell how 7:1-2 summarises Genesis 14
Explain the argument that the lesser is blessed by the greater (7:7)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Hebrews 7:1-10 says about Melchizedek and why he is called greater than Abraham?

topics.name: Another priest, a change of law, an unchangeable priesthood
topics.description: Because perfection did not come through the Levitical priesthood, another priest arose from Judah after the order of Melchizedek, by an oath and the power of an endless life; Jesus is surety of a better testament and lives to save to the uttermost and intercede.
evidence: State why another priest was needed (7:11)
Explain how Jesus differs from the many priests (7:23-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the writer says the priesthood had to change and what Jesus' priesthood is like (7:11-25)?

topics.name: A better covenant: the new covenant promised
topics.description: Jesus ministers in the true tabernacle as mediator of a better covenant on better promises; the writer cites the promise of a new covenant, in which God will write his laws on hearts, be their God, and remember their sins no more, making the first old.
evidence: State what is better about the covenant (8:6)
List the promises of 8:10-12
Say what 8:13 says about the first covenant
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what the writer says God promised in the new covenant (8:8-12)?

topics.name: The first covenant's tabernacle and ordinances
topics.description: The first covenant had a worldly sanctuary with a first tent and Most Holy Place containing the ark, and only the high priest entered once a year with blood; the writer says the Holy Spirit signified this could not perfect the conscience until a time of reformation.
evidence: Name items in the Holiest of all (9:3-4)
Say what the Holy Spirit showed by the arrangement (9:8)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the tabernacle arrangements and what they could not do (9:1-10)?

topics.name: Christ's own blood and the mediator of the new testament
topics.description: Christ entered the heavenly sanctuary once by his own blood, obtained eternal redemption, and is the mediator of the new testament; the first was dedicated with blood, without shedding of blood there is no remission, and he will appear a second time without sin for salvation.
evidence: Contrast animal blood and Christ's blood (9:12-14)
State what 9:22 says about blood and remission
Describe the two appearings in 9:26-28
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the writer says Christ's blood does what the blood of bulls and goats could not (9:12-14)?

topics.name: One sacrifice for sins for ever
topics.description: The law's repeated sacrifices could not take away sins, but Christ came to do God's will and by one offering of his body perfected for ever those who are sanctified; the writer again cites the covenant promise that sins will be remembered no more.
evidence: Say why the old sacrifices were repeated (10:1-4)
State what Christ did and where he sat down (10:10-14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Christ's single offering is enough according to Hebrews 10:10-18?

topics.name: Draw near with full assurance
topics.description: Because of boldness to enter the holiest by the blood of Jesus, through the veil of his flesh, and with a great priest over God's house, believers are to draw near with a true heart, hold fast their hope, provoke one another to love and good works, and not stop meeting together.
evidence: List the three "let us" calls in 10:22-24
Say what 10:25 warns against
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the writer says believers should do because of Jesus' blood and high priesthood (10:19-25)?

topics.name: Warning against wilful sin; endure and live by faith
topics.description: The writer warns that no sacrifice remains for wilful sin after receiving the truth, reminds readers of their earlier endurance, and urges patience, since the just shall live by faith and they are not of those who draw back.
evidence: Describe the warning of 10:26-29
State what the just shall do (10:38)
Tell what the readers endured before (10:32-34)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the writer asks the readers to remember and do in 10:32-39?

topics.name: What faith is: Abel, Enoch and Noah
topics.description: Faith is the substance of things hoped for and evidence of things unseen; by faith Abel offered a better sacrifice, Enoch was translated, and Noah built the ark; without faith it is impossible to please God.
evidence: Recite or paraphrase 11:1
Say what 11:6 requires of one who comes to God
Name what each of Abel, Enoch and Noah did by faith
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what faith is (11:1) and give the example of Noah (11:7)?

topics.name: By faith Abraham, Sarah and the patriarchs
topics.description: By faith Abraham went out not knowing where, sojourned as a stranger seeking a city built by God, Sara received strength to bear a child, Abraham offered Isaac, and Isaac, Jacob and Joseph acted in faith about things to come.
evidence: Say what Abraham did by faith in 11:8-10 and 11:17-19
Name what Isaac, Jacob and Joseph did in 11:20-22
State what 11:13-16 says these people sought
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Abraham did by faith and what the patriarchs were looking for (11:8-16)?

topics.name: By faith Moses, Israel and Rahab
topics.description: By faith Moses' parents hid him, Moses chose affliction with God's people over Egypt's pleasures, kept the Passover, Israel crossed the Red Sea and the walls of Jericho fell, and Rahab was not destroyed.
evidence: List what Moses did by faith (11:24-28)
Name the two events of 11:29-30
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what Moses chose by faith and why (11:24-27)?

topics.name: The rest of the cloud: triumph and suffering by faith
topics.description: The writer lists Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets, and describes those who conquered and those who suffered, none of whom received the promise without us.
evidence: Name some people in 11:32
Contrast the two kinds of experience in 11:33-38
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the writer says about those who by faith suffered and had not yet received the promise (11:35-40)?

topics.name: Looking to Jesus, the author and finisher of faith
topics.description: Surrounded by a cloud of witnesses, believers lay aside every weight and sin and run with patience, looking to Jesus, who endured the cross for the joy set before him and sat down at God's right hand.
evidence: State what we lay aside and what we run (12:1)
Say what Jesus endured and where he is (12:2)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what 12:1-2 tells believers to do and why they should look to Jesus?

topics.name: The Lord's discipline of his sons
topics.description: The writer reminds readers that the Lord chastens those he loves as a father disciplines sons, for their profit and holiness, and that discipline afterwards yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness.
evidence: State why God chastens (12:6, 12:10)
Describe the result in 12:11
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the writer says God's discipline is a sign of sonship (12:5-11)?

topics.name: Pursue peace and holiness; the example of Esau
topics.description: The readers are to follow peace and holiness, watch against a root of bitterness, and not be like Esau, who sold his birthright for one meal and later found no place of repentance though he sought the blessing with tears.
evidence: Say what we are to follow (12:14)
Tell what Esau did and what happened afterward (12:16-17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the writer says about Esau as a warning (12:15-17)?

topics.name: Not Mount Sinai but Mount Zion
topics.description: Believers have not come to the fearful mountain of Sinai but to mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem, to God, to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant and to the blood of sprinkling; they must not refuse the one who speaks, and receive a kingdom that cannot be shaken.
evidence: Contrast the two mountains (12:18-24)
State what is said of the kingdom and of God (12:28-29)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Hebrews 12:18-24 contrasts Sinai with Zion and names Jesus there?

topics.name: Brotherly love, marriage and contentment
topics.description: The writer calls for brotherly love and hospitality to strangers, remembering prisoners, honour in marriage, and a life free from covetousness because God has said he will never leave or forsake.
evidence: List the commands of 13:1-5
Say what promise supports contentment (13:5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name some practical commands in 13:1-5 and the promise that supports them?

topics.name: Leaders, Jesus outside the camp, and sacrifices of praise
topics.description: Readers are to remember their leaders, avoid strange doctrines, go out to Jesus outside the camp bearing his reproach, seeking the city to come, and offer sacrifices of praise and doing good.
evidence: Recite 13:8
Say where Jesus suffered and what believers are to do (13:12-13)
List the sacrifices of 13:15-16
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what it means to go to Jesus outside the camp and what sacrifices God is pleased with (13:12-16)?

topics.name: Obey leaders; blessing and farewell
topics.description: The writer asks them to obey their leaders and pray for him, prays that the God of peace who raised Jesus through the blood of the everlasting covenant would equip them, and closes with news of Timothy and greetings.
evidence: Say what the benediction asks of God (13:20-21)
Note the greeting from those of Italy (13:24)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the prayer of 13:20-21 and what it says about Jesus?

topics.name: Hebrews: overview
topics.description: The letter to the Hebrews presents Jesus as God's Son, greater than angels and Moses, our great high priest after Melchizedek who mediates a better covenant by one sacrifice, and calls readers to faith and endurance.
evidence: Describe the main parts: the Son (1-2), Moses and rest (3-4), the high priest (4-7), the new covenant and sacrifice (8-10), faith (11), endurance and exhortations (12-13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Hebrews teaches about Jesus and what the readers are told to do?

topics.name: 1 Corinthians: overview
topics.description: Paul writes to the church at Corinth about divisions, sin in the church, questions they asked him, worship, the resurrection and the collection (1:1-16:24).
evidence: Name the main problems Paul addresses: divisions, immorality, lawsuits, marriage, food offered to idols, the Lord's supper, gifts, the resurrection
Say who the letter is addressed to from 1:2
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 1 Corinthians and name three problems Paul corrects in the Corinthian church?

topics.name: Greeting and the call to unity
topics.description: Paul thanks God for the grace given to the Corinthians, then appeals to them to end their divisions over which leader they follow.
evidence: Quote the slogans the Corinthians were using (1:12)
Explain why Paul says Christ is not divided (1:13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why following one teacher against another is wrong, using 1 Corinthians 1:10-13?

topics.name: The cross: God's wisdom and power
topics.description: Paul says the preaching of the cross looks foolish to those perishing but is the power of God to those being saved, and that God chose the weak and low so that no one may boast.
evidence: Contrast how the cross is seen by those perishing and by those saved (1:18)
List who God chose according to 1:26-29 and why (1:29)

topics.description: The LORD tells the builders to be strong, for his Spirit remains among them according to the word covenanted when they came out of Egypt; he will shake the nations and fill the house with glory, greater than the former, and give peace in this place.
evidence: Read 2:3-5 and say how the LORD encourages them
Describe the promise of 2:6-9
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD encourages the builders in Haggai 2:1-9?

topics.name: Holy and unclean; blessing from this day
topics.description: Haggai asks the priests whether holiness or uncleanness spreads by touch and applies the answer to the people and their offerings, recalls their failed harvests, and says that from the day the temple foundation was laid the LORD will bless them.
evidence: Retell the two questions to the priests (2:12-13)
Say what changes 'from this day' (2:18-19)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the questions Haggai asked the priests and the promise that ends the section?

topics.name: Zerubbabel the signet
topics.description: On the same day as the blessing the LORD says he will shake the heavens and earth and overthrow the thrones of kingdoms, and promises to take Zerubbabel his servant and make him as a signet, for he has chosen him.
evidence: Say what the LORD says he will do to kingdoms (2:22)
Say what he promises Zerubbabel (2:23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD promises Zerubbabel in Haggai 2:23?

topics.name: Zechariah: overview
topics.description: Zechariah, prophet in the second year of Darius, receives a call to return, eight night visions about Jerusalem, Joshua and Zerubbabel, answers about fasting and promises for Zion, and two later burdens about the shepherd, the pierced one and the day of the LORD.
evidence: Say that chapters 1-6 are visions and 7-8 answer a question about fasting
Name the two 'burdens' of 9-11 and 12-14 (9:1, 12:1)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline Zechariah as visions, a question about fasting and two later burdens?

topics.name: Turn unto me, and I will turn unto you
topics.description: In the second year of Darius the LORD tells Zechariah to say that he was sore displeased with the fathers, who did not heed the former prophets, and calls the people to turn to him so that he will turn to them.
evidence: Read the call of 1:3
Say what the fathers did when the prophets spoke (1:4-6)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the invitation in Zechariah 1:3 and why the fathers are mentioned?

topics.name: The riders among the myrtle trees
topics.description: Zechariah sees a night vision of riders sent through the earth; the angel of the LORD asks how long the LORD will withhold mercy from Jerusalem, and the LORD answers with comfort that he is jealous for Zion, will return with mercies, and his house will be built.
evidence: Describe the vision and the angel's question (1:8-12)
Describe the LORD's answer (1:13-17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what the angel of the LORD asks in Zechariah 1:12 and how the LORD replies?

topics.name: Four horns and four carpenters
topics.description: Zechariah sees four horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem, and four carpenters who come to terrify them and cast out the horns of the Gentiles.
evidence: Say what the horns are explained to be (1:19, 1:21)
Say what the carpenters come to do (1:21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the vision of the four horns and the four carpenters?

topics.name: The man with the measuring line
topics.description: A man goes to measure Jerusalem, but an angel says it will be inhabited like towns without walls, for the LORD will be a wall of fire and the glory in her midst; exiles are called to flee Babylon, and many nations will be joined to the LORD.
evidence: Describe the vision and the message about walls (2:1-5)
Say what the LORD promises in 2:10-11
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says about Jerusalem's walls in Zechariah 2:4-5?

topics.name: Joshua the high priest cleansed
topics.description: Joshua the high priest stands in filthy garments before the angel of the LORD with Satan accusing; the LORD rebukes Satan, has the filthy clothes removed, says he has caused Joshua's iniquity to pass, and promises his servant the Branch and the removal of the land's iniquity in one day.
evidence: Retell what happens to Joshua's clothing (3:3-5)
Say what the LORD says about the Branch and 'one day' (3:8-9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the vision of Joshua in filthy garments and what the LORD does for him?

topics.name: The lampstand and the two olive trees
topics.description: Zechariah sees a gold lampstand with two olive trees; the LORD tells Zerubbabel that it is not by might nor power but by his spirit, that Zerubbabel who laid the foundation will finish the house, and that none should despise the day of small things.
evidence: Read 4:6 and say whom it is spoken to
Say what Zerubbabel's hands do (4:9)
Describe the two olive trees (4:14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD tells Zerubbabel in Zechariah 4:6 and 4:9-10?

topics.name: The flying roll and the woman in the ephah
topics.description: Zechariah sees a flying scroll that is a curse on thieves and false swearers, and an ephah in which a woman called wickedness is shut with lead and carried by two women with wings to the land of Shinar.
evidence: Say what the flying roll is and whom it enters (5:3-4)
Say what the woman in the ephah is called and where the ephah goes (5:8, 5:11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the two visions of Zechariah 5 and what each is said to mean?

topics.name: Four chariots; crowns for Joshua; the Branch
topics.description: Four chariots come out from between two bronze mountains as spirits of the heavens going throughout the earth; then Zechariah is told to make crowns and set them on Joshua the high priest, speaking of a man called the Branch who will build the temple and rule.
evidence: Describe the vision of the chariots (6:1-8)
Describe the crown action and what it says of the Branch (6:11-13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Zechariah is told to do with the crown and what is said about the Branch?

topics.name: Fasting question: did ye fast unto me?
topics.description: Messengers ask whether the people should continue the fast of the fifth month; the LORD asks whether they fasted for him and tells them to render true judgment and mercy, since the fathers hardened their hearts against the law and were scattered.
evidence: State the question that is asked (7:3)
Read the commands of 7:9-10
Say what happened because the fathers would not hear (7:11-14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says in Zechariah 7:9-10 in answer to the question about fasting?

topics.name: The LORD returns to dwell in Jerusalem
topics.description: The LORD says he has returned to Zion and Jerusalem will be a city of truth with old people and playing children in her streets; he will save his people, make them a blessing, and tells them to speak truth and judge truly.
evidence: Describe the picture of 8:4-5
Read the promise of 8:8
List the commands of 8:16-17
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Zechariah 8:1-17 pictures Jerusalem when the LORD returns?

topics.name: Fasts become feasts; nations seek the LORD
topics.description: The LORD says the fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh and tenth months will become joy and cheerful feasts, and many peoples and strong nations will come to Jerusalem to seek the LORD, with ten men from all languages taking hold of a Jew.
evidence: Name the fasts that become feasts (8:19)
Describe what the peoples say and do (8:20-23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how the LORD answers the fasting question and what the nations will do?

topics.name: Thy King cometh, lowly and riding on an ass
topics.description: A burden against Hadrach, Damascus, Tyre and Philistia is followed by a call for Zion to rejoice because her just and saving King comes lowly on an ass; he cuts off chariot and bow, speaks peace to the nations, and the LORD saves his people.
evidence: Say what is said of the King in 9:9
Describe his rule in 9:10
Read the promise to prisoners in 9:11-12
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the King of Zechariah 9:9-10 and what he does?

topics.name: The LORD visits his flock
topics.description: The LORD tells his people to ask him for rain, rejects idols and false shepherds, and promises to strengthen Judah and Joseph, gather and bring them back, and make them strong in him.
evidence: Say what Israel is told to ask (10:1)
Say what the LORD says of the shepherds and flock (10:2-3)
Describe the regathering (10:8-10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promises his flock in Zechariah 10 and what he says about idols and shepherds?

topics.name: Two staves and thirty pieces of silver
topics.description: Zechariah is told to shepherd the flock of the slaughter and takes two staves called Beauty and Bands; the flock rejects him, he breaks the staves, is paid thirty pieces of silver which the LORD tells him to cast to the potter, and a foolish shepherd is announced.
evidence: Name the two staves and what breaking each means (11:10, 11:14)
Retell what happens to the thirty pieces of silver (11:12-13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what Zechariah does with the two staves and the thirty pieces of silver?

topics.name: Jerusalem a burdensome stone; they look on the pierced
topics.description: The LORD will make Jerusalem a cup of trembling and a burdensome stone to the nations that gather against her, and will pour on David's house and Jerusalem the spirit of grace and supplications, so that they look on him whom they have pierced and mourn.
evidence: Describe what happens to nations that attack Jerusalem (12:2-3, 12:9)
Read 12:10 and describe the mourning that follows (12:10-14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what Zechariah 12:10 says the LORD will pour out and what the people do?

topics.name: A fountain opened; the shepherd smitten
topics.description: In that day a fountain is opened for sin and uncleanness and idols and false prophets are cut off; the LORD calls the sword against his shepherd, the sheep are scattered, and a third part is refined as silver and calls on his name.
evidence: Read 13:1
Say what the LORD calls the sword to do (13:7)
Describe the refining of the third part (13:9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the fountain of Zechariah 13:1 and what the LORD says about the shepherd and the refined third in 13:7-9?

topics.name: The day of the LORD: king over all the earth
topics.description: The LORD gathers all nations against Jerusalem, then goes forth to fight, standing on the mount of Olives; living waters flow, he is king over all the earth, the survivors keep the feast of tabernacles, and everything is holiness to the LORD.
evidence: Describe the siege and the LORD's coming (14:2-5)
Read 14:9 and describe the closing picture (14:16-21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Zechariah 14:9 says about the LORD and how the book ends?

topics.name: Malachi: overview
topics.description: The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi: a series of disputes in which the LORD states a charge, the people ask how, and he answers, ending with the coming day of the LORD and the promise to send Elijah.
evidence: Notice the pattern of 'Wherein?' questions (1:2, 1:6, 2:17, 3:7-8)
Say how the book ends (4:5-6)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Malachi's disputes work and how the book ends?

topics.name: I have loved you
topics.description: The LORD says he loved Israel, and when they ask how, he points to Jacob and Esau, saying he loved Jacob and hated Esau and laid waste Esau's mountains; he promises that he will be magnified from the border of Israel.
evidence: Read the exchange of 1:2
Say what happens to Edom's plans (1:4)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the LORD answers the question 'Wherein hast thou loved us?' in Malachi 1:2-3?

topics.name: Polluted offerings and a great name
topics.description: The LORD rebukes priests who despise his name by bringing blind, lame and sick animals as offerings and call his table contemptible; he says he has no pleasure in them and that his name will be great among the Gentiles everywhere.
evidence: Describe the offerings and the priests' attitude (1:7-8, 1:12-13)
Read the promise of 1:11
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what was wrong with the offerings in Malachi 1 and what the LORD says about his name?

topics.name: The covenant with Levi corrupted
topics.description: The LORD sends a commandment to the priests: his covenant with Levi was of life and peace, and Levi feared him and turned many from iniquity, but the priests have departed from the way, caused many to stumble and been partial in the law.
evidence: Describe what Levi was like (2:5-6)
Say what the priests did (2:8-9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} contrast Levi and the priests of Malachi's day in chapter 2?

topics.name: Treachery against brother and wife
topics.description: Malachi charges Judah with profaning the covenant of the fathers and marrying the daughter of a strange god, and with dealing treacherously with the wife of their youth, since the LORD hates putting away; they also weary him by saying evildoers please him.
evidence: Say what wearies the LORD in 2:17
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what the LORD condemns in Malachi 2:10-16?

topics.name: The messenger and the refiner
topics.description: The LORD announces a messenger to prepare the way before him and the LORD coming suddenly to his temple, like a refiner's fire who purifies the sons of Levi; he will be a swift witness against sinners, for he does not change.
evidence: Say what is promised in 3:1
Describe the refiner (3:2-3)
Read 3:6
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe who is coming in Malachi 3:1 and what he does in 3:2-3?

topics.name: Return to me: tithes and offerings
topics.description: The LORD tells the people to return, and when they ask how, says they have robbed him in tithes and offerings; he calls them to bring the whole tithe into the storehouse and promises to open the windows of heaven and rebuke the devourer.
evidence: Read the charge of 3:8-9
Describe the promises of 3:10-12
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says about tithes and offerings in Malachi 3:7-12?

topics.name: Is it vain to serve God?
topics.description: The people say it is vain to serve God and call the proud happy; those who fear the LORD speak together and he writes a book of remembrance, and says they will be his jewels on the day he makes, spared as a son.
evidence: Describe what the people complained (3:14-15)
Describe what the LORD does for those who fear him (3:16-17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the book of remembrance in Malachi 3:16-17?

topics.name: The day that burns; the Sun of righteousness; Elijah
topics.description: The coming day burns the wicked like stubble, but for those who fear the LORD the Sun of righteousness arises with healing; the people are told to remember the law of Moses, and the LORD will send Elijah the prophet before the great day to turn hearts of fathers and children.
evidence: Contrast the two outcomes of 4:1-3
Read the closing command and promise (4:4-6)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the two outcomes on the day of the LORD in Malachi 4 and what the LORD promises to send?

topics.name: Luke: The Gospel Orderly Told
topics.description: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus so he may know the certainty of what he was taught, from the births of John and Jesus to the resurrection, ascension and the apostles' commission.
evidence: Say who Luke addresses, why he wrote, and how the book begins and ends.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Luke wrote his Gospel and where it begins and ends?

topics.name: Luke's Purpose and Eyewitnesses
topics.description: Luke says many have set out an account, that eyewitnesses and ministers of the word handed it down, and that he writes in order so Theophilus may know the certainty of what he was taught.
evidence: Name the reason Luke gives for writing and the sources he mentions.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say why Luke wrote and who he says handed the story down?

topics.name: Gabriel Promises a Son to Zacharias
topics.description: While Zacharias serves in the temple at the hour of incense, the angel Gabriel says Elisabeth will bear a son, John; Zacharias doubts, is struck dumb, and Elisabeth conceives.
evidence: Retell the angel's message, Zacharias's question and its result.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what Gabriel told Zacharias and what happened to him because he doubted?

topics.name: Gabriel Announces Jesus to Mary
topics.description: In the sixth month Gabriel tells the virgin Mary, betrothed to Joseph of David's house, that she will bear Jesus, who will receive David's throne and be called Son of the Highest; Mary submits.
evidence: Say what the angel promised about Jesus and how Mary answered.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Gabriel told Mary about her son and how she responded?

topics.name: Mary Visits Elisabeth and Sings
topics.description: Mary hurries to Elisabeth's house; the child leaps in Elisabeth's womb, Elisabeth blesses Mary, and Mary praises God for mercy, for scattering the proud and lifting the lowly, and for remembering Abraham.
evidence: Retell the meeting and name two things Mary praises God for in her song.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell Mary's visit to Elisabeth and name things Mary praises God for?

topics.name: John Is Born; Zacharias Prophesies
topics.description: Elisabeth bears a son, the family insists on the name John, Zacharias's tongue is loosed, and he blesses God for the horn of salvation, the oath to Abraham, and his son who will go before the Lord.
evidence: Describe how Zacharias regained speech and what he said about God's covenant and about John.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Zacharias spoke again and what he said about John and God's promise?

topics.name: The Birth of Jesus and the Shepherds
topics.description: A decree brings Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, where Jesus is born and laid in a manger; angels announce a Saviour, Christ the Lord, to shepherds, who go and tell what they saw.
evidence: Retell the birth, the angel's announcement and what the shepherds did.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the birth of Jesus and the shepherds' part in it?

topics.name: Simeon and Anna in the Temple
topics.description: Jesus is named and presented at the temple; Simeon, to whom the Spirit promised he would see the Lord's Christ, blesses God for salvation for all peoples, and Anna the prophetess speaks of him to those awaiting redemption.
evidence: Say what Simeon was waiting for and what he and Anna said.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Simeon and Anna said when they saw the child Jesus?

topics.name: The Boy Jesus in the Temple
topics.description: At twelve, Jesus stays in Jerusalem after the Passover and is found after three days among the teachers; he tells his parents he must be about his Father's business and then returns home subject to them.
evidence: Retell where Jesus was found and what he said, and how he lived afterwards.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of Jesus at twelve in the temple?

topics.name: John the Baptist Prepares the Way
topics.description: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius the word comes to John, who preaches a baptism of repentance, calls for fruits worthy of repentance, answers the crowds, tax collectors and soldiers, points to one mightier, and is imprisoned by Herod.
evidence: List what John told the crowds, tax collectors and soldiers to do and what he said about the coming one.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain John's message of repentance and what he said about the one coming after him?

topics.name: The Baptism of Jesus
topics.description: When the people were baptized, Jesus is baptized and prays; heaven opens, the Holy Ghost descends like a dove, and a voice from heaven calls him beloved Son.
evidence: Say what happened at Jesus' baptism and what the voice said.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what happened when Jesus was baptized?

topics.name: The Genealogy of Jesus
topics.description: Luke lists Jesus' descent, as was supposed from Joseph, back through David, Abraham, Noe and Seth to Adam, who was the son of God.
evidence: Say where the list begins, which famous names it passes, and where it ends.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say who the genealogy in Luke 3 ends with and name some people on the list?

topics.name: The Temptation in the Wilderness
topics.description: Full of the Spirit, Jesus is tempted forty days by the devil and answers each of three temptations with 'It is written' and a word of Scripture; the devil departs for a season.
evidence: Name the three temptations and how Jesus answered each.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the three temptations and how Jesus answered them?

topics.name: Jesus Reads Isaiah at Nazareth
topics.description: In the Nazareth synagogue Jesus reads the passage about the anointed preacher of good news and says it is fulfilled in their hearing; he points to Elias and Eliseus helping outsiders, and the crowd tries to throw him down.
evidence: Say what Jesus read, what he said about it, and why the people turned on him.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus read in Nazareth and why the people were angry?

topics.name: Teaching and Healing in Capernaum
topics.description: Jesus teaches with authority in the Capernaum synagogue, casts out an unclean spirit, heals Simon's wife's mother and many at sunset, and tells the crowds he must preach the kingdom to other cities.
evidence: Name what Jesus did in Capernaum and why he moved on.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list what Jesus did in Capernaum and say why he went on to other cities?

topics.name: The Great Catch and the First Disciples
topics.description: After teaching from Simon's boat, Jesus tells him to let down the nets; a huge catch breaks them, Peter confesses he is a sinful man, and Simon, James and John leave all to follow Jesus.
evidence: Retell the catch and what Jesus said to Simon and what the fishermen did.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the great catch of fish and the call of Simon, James and John?

topics.name: Jesus Cleanses a Leper
topics.description: A man full of leprosy asks Jesus, if he is willing, to make him clean; Jesus touches him and he is cleansed, and is told to show himself to the priest as Moses commanded.
evidence: Say what the leper asked and what Jesus did and told him.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the leper?

topics.name: The Paralytic Let Down Through the Roof
topics.description: Friends lower a paralysed man through the tiles; Jesus forgives his sins, answers the scribes' charge of blasphemy by showing the Son of man has power to forgive sins, and tells the man to rise and walk.
evidence: Explain why Jesus healed him after forgiving his sins.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say why Jesus both forgave the man's sins and healed him?

topics.name: Levi's Feast and the Question of Fasting
topics.description: Jesus calls the tax collector Levi, who gives a feast; asked why he eats with sinners, Jesus says he came to call sinners to repentance, and he speaks of the bridegroom and of new wine and old wineskins.
evidence: Say who Jesus came to call, and what he said about the bridegroom and new wine.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain whom Jesus came to call and what his sayings about the bridegroom and new wine mean in the passage?

topics.name: Lord of the Sabbath
topics.description: The disciples pluck grain on the sabbath, and Jesus cites David eating the shewbread and says the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath; on another sabbath he heals a withered hand, asking whether it is lawful to do good or evil.
evidence: Describe the two sabbath conflicts and what Jesus said in each.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe both sabbath conflicts and what Jesus claimed?

topics.name: Jesus Chooses the Twelve
topics.description: After a night in prayer on a mountain, Jesus calls his disciples and names twelve apostles, including Simon Peter, Matthew and Judas Iscariot the traitor.
evidence: Say what Jesus did before choosing the twelve and name some of them.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name several of the twelve and say how Jesus prepared for choosing them?

topics.name: Blessings and Woes on the Plain
topics.description: Jesus blesses the poor, hungry, weeping and hated for his sake, and pronounces woe on the rich, full, laughing and well-spoken-of.
evidence: Compare who Jesus calls blessed with who he calls woe.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} contrast the blessings and woes Jesus gives in Luke 6?

topics.name: Love Your Enemies; Be Merciful
topics.description: Jesus tells his hearers to love enemies, bless those who curse them, do to others as they would have done to them, lend without hope of return, be merciful as the Father is, and not judge or condemn but forgive and give.
evidence: Say what Jesus commands about enemies, mercy and judging.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list what Jesus commands about enemies and judging others?

topics.name: The Blind Guide, the Tree, and Two Builders
topics.description: Jesus uses sayings about blind guides, a log and a speck, trees known by fruit, and a good treasure of the heart, and ends with the builder on rock who hears and does his words versus the builder with no foundation.
evidence: Explain what Jesus says separates the wise builder from the foolish one.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the two builders and why hearing without doing is not enough?

topics.name: The Centurion's Servant
topics.description: A centurion sends elders and friends to ask Jesus to heal his servant, saying a word is enough since he himself is under authority; Jesus marvels at such faith and the servant is found well.
evidence: Say what the centurion believed about Jesus' word and how Jesus responded.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the centurion's request and Jesus' response?

topics.name: Jesus Raises the Widow's Son at Nain
topics.description: Seeing a widow carrying out her only son, Jesus has compassion, touches the bier and tells the young man to arise; he sits up and speaks, and the people say God has visited his people.
evidence: Retell what Jesus did at Nain and what the crowd said.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the raising of the widow's son at Nain?

topics.name: John's Question and Jesus' Answer
topics.description: John in prison sends two disciples to ask whether Jesus is the one to come; Jesus points to the healings and the gospel preached to the poor, then calls John more than a prophet, the messenger sent before him.
evidence: Say how Jesus answered John's disciples and what he said about John.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus answered John's question and what he said about John?

topics.name: The Woman Who Anointed Jesus' Feet
topics.description: At Simon the Pharisee's house a sinful woman washes Jesus' feet with tears and anoints them; Jesus tells of two debtors forgiven and says her many sins are forgiven for she loved much.
evidence: Explain the parable of two debtors and how it applies to Simon and the woman.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the story of the two debtors and how Jesus applied it?

topics.name: The Parable of the Sower
topics.description: Jesus tours with the twelve and women who minister to him, and tells of a sower whose seed falls on four soils; he explains the seed is the word of God and the soils are ways of hearing, and tells them to take heed how they hear.
evidence: Name the four soils and what each stands for according to Jesus.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name the four soils in the parable of the sower and say what Jesus says each means?

topics.name: Jesus' Mother and Brothers
topics.description: When his mother and brothers cannot reach him for the crowd, Jesus says those who hear the word of God and do it are his mother and brothers.
evidence: Say whom Jesus calls his mother and brothers.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say who Jesus calls his family and why?

topics.name: Jesus Calms the Storm
topics.description: Crossing the lake, Jesus sleeps as a storm fills the boat; the disciples wake him, he rebukes wind and waves, and they marvel and wonder who he is.
evidence: Retell the storm and what the disciples asked afterwards.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the calming of the storm?

topics.name: The Man Among the Tombs
topics.description: In the country of the Gadarenes Jesus frees a man possessed by a legion of demons; they enter swine that rush into the lake, and the healed man is told to return home and tell what God has done.
evidence: Retell what happened to the man and the swine and what Jesus told the man to do.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the man called Legion?

topics.name: Jairus' Daughter and the Woman with the Issue
topics.description: Jairus asks Jesus to heal his dying daughter; on the way a woman with twelve years of bleeding touches his garment and is healed, and then Jesus raises the girl from death.
evidence: Say what happened to the woman and to Jairus' daughter and what Jesus told Jairus.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the woman and the raising of Jairus' daughter?

topics.name: The Twelve Are Sent Out; Herod Is Perplexed
topics.description: Jesus gives the twelve power and sends them to preach and heal, taking nothing for the journey; Herod hears of him and is perplexed, saying he beheaded John.
evidence: Say what the twelve were told to bring and do, and what Herod said.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus told the twelve and why Herod was perplexed?

topics.name: Feeding the Five Thousand
topics.description: When the crowd follows Jesus to a desert place, he tells the twelve to give them food; five loaves and two fishes are blessed and broken, all are filled, and twelve baskets of fragments remain.
evidence: Retell what Jesus did with the loaves and fishes and how much was left.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the feeding of the five thousand?

topics.name: Peter Confesses the Christ; Take Up the Cross
topics.description: Jesus asks who people say he is; Peter answers 'The Christ of God', and Jesus says the Son of man must suffer, be killed and rise, and that his followers must deny themselves and take up their cross daily.
evidence: Say what Peter confessed, what Jesus foretold, and what he asked of followers.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Peter's confession and what Jesus said discipleship costs?

topics.name: The Transfiguration
topics.description: About eight days later Jesus takes Peter, John and James up a mountain to pray; his appearance changes, Moses and Elias speak with him of his decease at Jerusalem, and a voice from the cloud says 'hear him'.
evidence: Say who appeared with Jesus, what they talked about, and what the voice said.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the transfiguration and what the voice from the cloud said?

topics.name: The Boy with the Spirit; Who Is Greatest
topics.description: Coming down the mountain, Jesus heals a boy the disciples could not help, again tells them he will be delivered into men's hands, and answers their argument about greatness by setting a child beside him and telling John not to forbid one who casts out demons in his name.
evidence: Say how Jesus answered the dispute about who is greatest.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus taught the disciples about greatness using the child?

topics.name: Setting His Face to Jerusalem
topics.description: As the time comes for him to be received up, Jesus sets his face toward Jerusalem; a Samaritan village refuses him and he rebukes James and John for wanting fire, then answers three would-be followers about the cost of following.
evidence: Say what happened in Samaria and what Jesus told the three would-be followers.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe Jesus turning toward Jerusalem and what he said to those who wanted to follow?

topics.name: The Seventy Sent Out
topics.description: Jesus sends seventy others two by two ahead of him with instructions like those given the twelve, pronounces woe on unrepentant towns, and when they return rejoicing tells them rather to rejoice that their names are written in heaven.
evidence: Say what the seventy were told to do and what Jesus said they should rejoice in.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus told the seventy and what he said to rejoice about?

topics.name: The Good Samaritan
topics.description: Asked by a lawyer what he must do to inherit eternal life, Jesus draws out love of God and neighbour; to the question 'who is my neighbour' he tells of a Samaritan who helps a man left by robbers after a priest and a Levite pass by.
evidence: Retell the parable and say what Jesus told the lawyer to do.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the good Samaritan and say what Jesus told the lawyer to do?

topics.name: Martha and Mary
topics.description: Martha is distracted by serving and asks Jesus to tell Mary to help; Jesus says Martha is troubled about many things but one thing is needful and Mary has chosen it.
evidence: Say what Jesus told Martha about Mary's choice.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said to Martha about Mary?

topics.name: Teach Us to Pray
topics.description: Asked by a disciple how to pray, Jesus gives a prayer to the Father about his name, kingdom, bread, forgiveness and temptation, and teaches persistence with the friend at midnight and the Father who gives the Holy Spirit to those who ask.
evidence: Say what the prayer asks for and what Jesus says about asking and seeking.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus taught about how to pray?

topics.name: Casting Out Demons: Beelzebub and the Sign of Jonas
topics.description: After Jesus casts out a mute spirit, some say he does it by Beelzebub; he answers that a divided kingdom falls, that he casts out by the finger of God, refuses a sign except the sign of Jonas, and speaks of light and the eye.
evidence: Say the charge made against Jesus and how he answered it.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the charge about Beelzebub and Jesus' answer?

topics.name: Woes on the Pharisees and Lawyers
topics.description: At a Pharisee's table Jesus rebukes the Pharisees for cleaning the outside while inside is full of wickedness and tithing herbs while neglecting judgment and the love of God, and the lawyers for burdening men and building the prophets' tombs; the scribes begin to lie in wait for him.
evidence: List some things Jesus faults the Pharisees and lawyers for.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list the faults Jesus names in the Pharisees and lawyers?

topics.name: Fear God, Not Men; Confess Christ
topics.description: Jesus warns against the leaven of the Pharisees, says nothing hidden will stay hidden, tells his friends to fear the One who has power after death, assures them God knows every sparrow and hair, and promises the Holy Ghost will teach them what to say.
evidence: Say who Jesus tells his friends to fear and why they need not be afraid.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain who Jesus says to fear and what he says about sparrows?

topics.name: The Parable of the Rich Fool
topics.description: Asked to settle an inheritance, Jesus warns against covetousness and tells of a rich man who plans bigger barns and is told 'thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee'.
evidence: Say what the rich man planned and what God said to him.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the rich fool and what it warns against?

topics.name: Do Not Be Anxious; Treasure in Heaven
topics.description: Jesus tells the disciples not to be anxious for food or clothing, pointing to ravens and lilies, to seek the kingdom, and to give alms, for where treasure is, the heart will be also.
evidence: Say what Jesus points to about God's care and what he says to seek first.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about worry using ravens and lilies?

topics.name: Watchful and Faithful Servants
topics.description: Jesus teaches being ready like servants awaiting their master's return, with the thief and the faithful steward as examples, and says to whom much is given much will be required.
evidence: Say what Jesus says about readiness and about the faithful and unfaithful servant.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about being ready for the Son of man?

topics.name: Fire, Division and Reading the Times
topics.description: Jesus says he came to send fire and has a baptism to undergo, that his coming will bring division even in households, rebukes the crowd for reading the sky but not the time, and urges settling with an adversary.
evidence: Say what Jesus says about division and about discerning the time.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus says about division and what the crowd failed to discern?

topics.name: Repent or Perish; The Barren Fig Tree
topics.description: Told about Galileans killed by Pilate and eighteen killed by a tower, Jesus says those victims were not worse sinners and everyone must repent or perish, then tells of a fig tree given one more year to bear fruit.
evidence: Say what Jesus says about those who died and what the fig-tree parable shows.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about the Galileans and the tower and the fig tree?

topics.name: The Woman Bent Eighteen Years
topics.description: Jesus heals a woman bound by a spirit for eighteen years in a synagogue on the sabbath; he answers the ruler's indignation by pointing to loosing an ox on the sabbath and calls her a daughter of Abraham.
evidence: Retell the healing and Jesus' answer to the ruler of the synagogue.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the bent woman and Jesus' reply?

topics.name: Mustard Seed and Leaven
topics.description: Jesus compares the kingdom of God to a grain of mustard seed that grows into a tree and to leaven hidden in three measures of meal.
evidence: Describe the two kingdom pictures Jesus gives.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the mustard seed and leaven parables?

topics.name: The Narrow Door and Lament over Jerusalem
topics.description: Journeying toward Jerusalem, Jesus tells those asking if few are saved to strive to enter the narrow gate before the master shuts the door, says people will come from every direction to the kingdom, calls Herod a fox, and laments over Jerusalem.
evidence: Say what Jesus says about the narrow gate and what he laments over Jerusalem.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about the narrow door and his lament over Jerusalem?

topics.name: Healing on the Sabbath and Humility at the Table
topics.description: At a chief Pharisee's house Jesus heals a man with dropsy, and tells guests not to seek the highest seats and hosts to invite the poor, since the humble will be exalted.
evidence: Say what Jesus did for the man with dropsy and what he taught about seats and invitations.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus taught about humility at the Pharisee's meal?

topics.name: The Parable of the Great Supper
topics.description: A man gives a great supper and invited guests make excuses about land, oxen and marriage, so the master sends servants to bring in the poor, maimed, lame and blind, and then those in the highways, and none of the first invited will taste it.
evidence: Say what excuses were given and who was invited instead.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the great supper and who was brought in?

topics.name: The Cost of Discipleship
topics.description: To the great crowds Jesus says a disciple must put him before family and his own life, bear his cross, count the cost like a tower-builder or king going to war, and forsake all; salt that loses its savour is thrown out.
evidence: List what Jesus says a disciple must be ready to give up and the two cost-counting pictures.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the tower builder and king illustrations about counting the cost?

topics.name: The Lost Sheep and the Lost Coin
topics.description: When Pharisees murmur that Jesus receives sinners, he tells of a shepherd seeking one lost sheep and a woman seeking one lost coin, and says there is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
evidence: Say why Jesus told these parables and what the joy in heaven is over.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the two parables of the lost sheep and coin and what they show about heaven?

topics.name: The Parable of the Prodigal Son
topics.description: A younger son takes his inheritance, wastes it, feeds swine, and returns repenting; the father runs to welcome him with robe, ring and feast, while the elder brother angrily refuses to join and the father pleads with him.
evidence: Retell the parable and say what the father says to each son.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the prodigal son and name what the father does for each son?

topics.name: The Unjust Steward and Serving Two Masters
topics.description: Jesus tells his disciples of a steward who reduces his master's debtors' bills and is commended for shrewdness, then teaches faithfulness in little and says no one can serve God and mammon.
evidence: Say what Jesus draws from the steward and what he says about two masters.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about money and faithfulness after the steward parable?

topics.name: The Pharisees' Pride and the Law Stands
topics.description: The covetous Pharisees deride Jesus, who says God knows their hearts and what men esteem is abomination to him, that the law and prophets were until John, and that not a tittle of the law will fail.
evidence: Say how Jesus answers the Pharisees who mocked him.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus tells the Pharisees about their hearts and the law?

topics.name: The Rich Man and Lazarus
topics.description: Jesus tells of a rich man and a beggar named Lazarus who both die; Lazarus is carried to Abraham's bosom and the rich man is in torment, where Abraham says a great gulf is fixed and that his brothers have Moses and the prophets.
evidence: Retell the parable and what Abraham says about Moses and the prophets.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of the rich man and Lazarus and what Abraham said about Moses and the prophets?

topics.name: Offences, Forgiveness, Faith and Duty
topics.description: Jesus warns against causing little ones to stumble, tells his disciples to rebuke and forgive a repenting brother even seven times a day, and answers a request for more faith with the mustard seed and the servant who does his duty.
evidence: Say what Jesus teaches about forgiving and about faith as a mustard seed.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus taught about offences, forgiveness and faith?

topics.name: Ten Lepers Cleansed
topics.description: Ten lepers cry for mercy and Jesus sends them to the priests; as they go they are cleansed, and only one, a Samaritan, returns to give thanks.
evidence: Retell what happened to the ten and what Jesus said about the one who returned.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the ten lepers and who came back to give thanks?

topics.name: The Kingdom's Coming and the Days of the Son of Man
topics.description: Asked when the kingdom comes, Jesus says it does not come with observation and is in the midst of them, then tells the disciples the Son of man will be revealed suddenly like lightning, as in the days of Noe and Lot, after he first suffers and is rejected.
evidence: Say how Jesus describes the coming of the Son of man and what examples he uses.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus compares his coming to the days of Noe and Lot?

topics.name: The Persistent Widow
topics.description: Jesus tells a parable that men ought always to pray and not faint: a widow keeps asking an unjust judge until he avenges her, and God will avenge his elect speedily.
evidence: Say what the parable teaches about prayer.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the widow and the judge and what it teaches about prayer?

topics.name: The Pharisee and the Publican
topics.description: Two men pray in the temple: a Pharisee thanking God he is not like others, and a tax collector beating his breast and asking mercy; Jesus says the publican went home justified and that the self-exalted will be humbled.
evidence: Contrast the two prayers and say who went home justified.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} contrast the two prayers and say who went home justified and why?

topics.name: Jesus Receives Little Children
topics.description: When people bring infants to Jesus and the disciples rebuke them, Jesus calls the children to him and says the kingdom belongs to such and must be received as a little child.
evidence: Say what Jesus said about the children and receiving the kingdom.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said when children were brought to him?

topics.name: The Rich Ruler
topics.description: A ruler asks what to do to inherit eternal life, says he has kept the commandments, and is told to sell all and follow; he goes away sorrowful, and Jesus says it is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom but possible with God.
evidence: Retell what the ruler asked, what Jesus told him and what Jesus said is possible with God.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of the rich ruler and Jesus' words about what is impossible and possible?

topics.name: Jesus Foretells His Suffering Again
topics.description: Jesus tells the twelve they go up to Jerusalem where things written by the prophets will be accomplished: he will be delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, scourged, killed, and rise the third day, but they understand none of it.
evidence: List what Jesus says will happen and how the disciples responded.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus told the twelve about Jerusalem and what they understood?

topics.name: The Blind Man near Jericho
topics.description: A blind beggar near Jericho calls Jesus 'thou son of David', persists when rebuked, asks to receive his sight, and is healed; he follows Jesus glorifying God.
evidence: Say what the blind man called Jesus and what happened.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the blind man near Jericho?

topics.name: Zacchaeus
topics.description: Zacchaeus, a rich chief tax collector, climbs a sycomore tree to see Jesus; Jesus invites himself to his house, Zacchaeus promises half his goods to the poor and fourfold restitution, and Jesus says the Son of man came to seek and save the lost.
evidence: Say what Zacchaeus did and what Jesus said he came to do.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of Zacchaeus and what Jesus said about seeking the lost?

topics.name: The Parable of the Pounds
topics.description: Because he is near Jerusalem and people expect the kingdom to appear, Jesus tells of a nobleman who gives ten servants a pound each before going away to receive a kingdom; on his return he rewards the faithful, rebukes the servant who hid his pound, and deals with the citizens who refused him.
evidence: Say what each servant did with the pound and what the nobleman did on his return.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the pounds?

topics.name: The Entry into Jerusalem
topics.description: Jesus sends two disciples for a colt, rides it toward Jerusalem as the disciples spread clothes and praise God, saying 'Blessed be the King that cometh', and weeps over the city that does not know the things of its peace.
evidence: Retell the entry and say why Jesus wept over Jerusalem.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' entry to Jerusalem and why he wept?

topics.name: Jesus Drives Out the Traders
topics.description: Jesus enters the temple and drives out those selling, saying his house is a house of prayer but they made it a den of thieves, and teaches there daily while the chief priests seek to destroy him.
evidence: Say what Jesus did in the temple and what he said.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what Jesus did in the temple and what he said about it?

topics.name: By What Authority?
