topics.description: In the temple the chief priests, scribes and elders ask by what authority Jesus acts; he asks them whether John's baptism was from heaven or men, they will not answer, and so he will not tell them either.
evidence: Say what Jesus asked and why the leaders would not answer.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' question about John's baptism and why the leaders were trapped?

topics.name: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants
topics.description: Jesus tells of a vineyard owner whose servants are beaten and sent away and whose beloved son is killed by the tenants; he says the owner will destroy them and give the vineyard to others, and cites the rejected stone that becomes the head of the corner.
evidence: Say what the tenants did to the servants and the son and what Jesus said about the stone.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the tenants and say what Jesus said about the rejected stone?

topics.name: Tribute to Caesar
topics.description: Spies sent by the scribes and chief priests ask whether it is lawful to pay tribute to Caesar; Jesus asks for a coin, asks whose image it bears, and says to render to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's.
evidence: Say how Jesus answered and why they could not trap him.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the tribute question and Jesus' answer?

topics.name: The Sadducees Ask About the Resurrection
topics.description: The Sadducees, who deny the resurrection, ask whose wife a woman married to seven brothers would be; Jesus says those counted worthy of that world neither marry nor die, and the dead are raised, as Moses called the Lord the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
evidence: Say what Jesus said about the resurrection and how he used Moses.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' answer to the Sadducees about the resurrection?

topics.name: David's Lord and Beware the Scribes
topics.description: Jesus asks how Christ can be David's son when David calls him Lord in the Psalms, and warns the disciples about scribes who love long robes and best seats and devour widows' houses.
evidence: Say the question Jesus asks about David and what he warns about the scribes.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' question about David calling Christ Lord and his warning about scribes?

topics.name: The Widow's Two Mites
topics.description: Jesus sees rich men giving gifts and a poor widow giving two mites, and says she gave more than all of them because she gave all she had.
evidence: Say why Jesus said the widow gave more than the rich.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the widow's offering and why Jesus praised it?

topics.name: The Temple Foretold to Fall; Signs and Persecution
topics.description: As some admire the temple's stones, Jesus says none will be left on another; asked when, he warns about deceivers, wars and signs, and tells the disciples they will be brought before rulers, given words and wisdom, and not lose a hair of their heads.
evidence: Say what Jesus says will happen to the temple and what he tells disciples about persecution.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} summarize what Jesus foretold about the temple and about persecution?

topics.name: Jerusalem Surrounded and the Son of Man Coming
topics.description: Jesus says when Jerusalem is surrounded by armies the disciples should flee, that days of vengeance will come, that they will see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power, and tells them to watch and pray; he gives the fig tree parable and says his words will not pass away.
evidence: Say what the disciples are told to do and what they are told to watch for.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about Jerusalem, his coming, and watching and praying?

topics.name: The Plot and Judas' Offer
topics.description: As Passover approaches, the chief priests and scribes seek to kill Jesus; Satan enters Judas Iscariot, who agrees with them to betray Jesus for money.
evidence: Say who plotted, what Judas agreed to, and what the text says entered Judas.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how Judas came to offer to betray Jesus?

topics.name: The Last Supper
topics.description: Jesus prepares and eats the Passover with the twelve, saying he desired to eat it before he suffers, and gives bread as his body and the cup as 'the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you'; he says one at the table will betray him.
evidence: Say what Jesus said over the bread and the cup and what he said about the betrayer.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus did and said at the Passover meal in Luke 22?

topics.name: Who Is Greatest: One Who Serves
topics.description: The disciples dispute who is greatest; Jesus contrasts Gentile kings with himself as one who serves, promises them a kingdom, tells Simon that Satan desired to sift him but he prayed for his faith, and foretells Peter's three denials.
evidence: Say what Jesus said about greatness and what he told Peter.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' teaching on greatness and his words to Peter?

topics.name: Prayer on the Mount of Olives
topics.description: On the Mount of Olives Jesus prays 'Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup... not my will, but thine be done'; an angel strengthens him, he prays in agony, and he finds the disciples asleep.
evidence: Say what Jesus prayed and what he told the disciples.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' prayer on the Mount of Olives?

topics.name: Betrayal and Arrest
topics.description: Judas comes with a crowd and betrays Jesus with a kiss; a disciple cuts off the high priest's servant's ear, Jesus heals it, and says to the leaders that this is their hour and the power of darkness.
evidence: Say how Judas betrayed Jesus and what Jesus did for the servant.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the arrest of Jesus and what he did for the wounded servant?

topics.name: Peter Denies Jesus
topics.description: Jesus is taken to the high priest's house; Peter follows afar and three times denies knowing him, the cock crows, the Lord looks at him, and Peter weeps bitterly; Jesus is mocked and struck.
evidence: Retell Peter's three denials and what happened after the third.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell Peter's denials and what he did after the cock crowed?

topics.name: Jesus Before the Council
topics.description: At day the elders, chief priests and scribes bring Jesus before their council and ask if he is the Christ and the Son of God; he says the Son of man will sit at God's right hand and answers 'Ye say that I am'.
evidence: Say what the council asked and how Jesus answered.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what the council asked Jesus and how he answered?

topics.name: Jesus Before Pilate and Herod
topics.description: The crowd accuses Jesus before Pilate, who three times finds no fault; he is sent to Herod, who mocks him, and Pilate at last releases Barabbas and delivers Jesus to be crucified.
evidence: Say what Pilate repeatedly said and who was released.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the trial before Pilate and Herod and who was released?

topics.name: The Crucifixion and the Thief
topics.description: Jesus is led to Calvary with Simon of Cyrene carrying the cross, prays 'Father, forgive them', is mocked, and tells the repentant criminal beside him that today he will be with him in paradise.
evidence: Say what Jesus said for those crucifying him and to the repentant criminal.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said on the cross to the Father and to the criminal?

topics.name: Jesus Dies and Is Buried
topics.description: Darkness falls, the temple veil is torn, Jesus cries 'Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit' and dies; the centurion glorifies God, and Joseph of Arimathaea lays the body in a new rock tomb as the women watch.
evidence: Say what signs and words marked Jesus' death and who buried him.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the death of Jesus and his burial?

topics.name: The Empty Tomb
topics.description: On the first day of the week the women find the stone rolled away and are told by two men in shining garments that Jesus is risen; the apostles think it idle talk, but Peter runs to the tomb and sees the linen clothes.
evidence: Say what the women found and were told and how the apostles reacted.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what the women found at the tomb and what they were told?

topics.name: The Road to Emmaus
topics.description: Two disciples walk to Emmaus when Jesus joins them unrecognised; he explains from Moses and all the prophets the things concerning himself, and their eyes are opened when he breaks bread; they return to Jerusalem to tell the eleven.
evidence: Say how the two disciples recognised Jesus and what he explained to them.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the Emmaus road and how Jesus opened the Scriptures?

topics.name: Jesus Appears and Ascends
topics.description: Jesus appears to the disciples, shows his hands and feet and eats fish, opens their minds to the Scriptures, tells them repentance and remission of sins will be preached to all nations beginning at Jerusalem, and is carried up to heaven as he blesses them.
evidence: Say what Jesus showed them, what he told them to preach, and how he left.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said to the disciples before ascending and how he left them?

topics.name: John: Believe That Jesus Is the Christ
topics.description: John presents Jesus as the Word made flesh through signs, 'I am' sayings, a farewell discourse, the cross and resurrection, and states that these things are written so readers believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in his name.
evidence: State why John says he wrote the book and name some signs or 'I am' sayings.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why John wrote his Gospel and how it begins and ends?

topics.name: The Word Became Flesh
topics.description: John opens with the Word, who was in the beginning with God and was God, through whom all things were made, who is life and light, and who became flesh and dwelt among us full of grace and truth; John the Baptist is sent to witness to the light.
evidence: Say what John says about the Word before creation, in creation and in becoming flesh.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what John 1 teaches about who the Word is and what he did?

topics.name: John the Baptist's Witness
topics.description: Priests and Levites ask John who he is; he says he is not the Christ but a voice crying in the wilderness, and next day he sees Jesus and calls him the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world and the Son of God.
evidence: Say who John said he was and what he called Jesus.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how John described himself and what he called Jesus?

topics.name: The First Disciples
topics.description: Andrew and another follow Jesus, Andrew brings Simon who is named Cephas, Philip finds Nathanael, who confesses Jesus the Son of God and King of Israel, and Jesus says they will see angels ascending and descending on the Son of man.
evidence: Name the first disciples called and what Nathanael confessed.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name the first disciples Jesus gathered and what Nathanael said about him?

topics.name: Water Made Wine at Cana
topics.description: At a wedding in Cana of Galilee the wine runs out; Jesus has the stone waterpots filled and the water becomes wine, which John calls the beginning of his signs, manifesting his glory so that his disciples believed.
evidence: Retell the miracle and what John says it showed.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the water becoming wine and what it revealed?

topics.name: Jesus Cleanses the Temple
topics.description: At Passover Jesus drives the sellers and money-changers out of the temple; asked for a sign, he says 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up', which John says he spoke of the temple of his body.
evidence: Say what Jesus did, what sign he named and what John says it meant.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did in the temple and what he meant by raising the temple in three days?

topics.name: Born Again: Nicodemus
topics.description: Nicodemus comes to Jesus by night and is told that no one can see the kingdom of God without being born of water and the Spirit; Jesus compares the Spirit to wind and says the Son of man must be lifted up like the serpent Moses lifted so that believers have eternal life.
evidence: Say what Jesus told Nicodemus about new birth and being lifted up.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told Nicodemus about being born again?

topics.name: God So Loved the World
topics.description: The discourse continues: God gave his only begotten Son so that whoever believes should not perish but have eternal life; the Son came not to condemn but to save, and men loved darkness rather than light.
evidence: Say what God gave, who receives life, and why people reject the light.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what John 3:16-21 says about God's love, belief and the light?

topics.name: John: He Must Increase
topics.description: John the Baptist, still baptizing, is told that Jesus baptizes and many come; he says he is only the bridegroom's friend and that Jesus must increase while he decreases, because the one who comes from above is above all.
evidence: Say how John responds to Jesus' growing following and what he says about the Son.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain John the Baptist's words about Jesus increasing?

topics.name: The Woman at the Well
topics.description: At Jacob's well in Samaria, Jesus asks a woman for water, offers living water, shows he knows her life, and tells her that true worshippers worship the Father in spirit and truth, and when she speaks of Messiah he says he is he.
evidence: Say what Jesus offered the woman and what he said about worship.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus offered the Samaritan woman and what he taught about worship?

topics.name: The Harvest in Samaria
topics.description: The woman tells the town, Jesus tells his disciples that his food is to do the will of him who sent him and to finish his work, and many Samaritans believe, some because of the woman and more because they heard him themselves.
evidence: Say what Jesus said was his food and how the Samaritans came to believe.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' words about food and the harvest and how Samaritans believed?

topics.name: The Nobleman's Son Healed
topics.description: A nobleman at Cana asks Jesus to come heal his dying son; Jesus says 'Thy son liveth', the man believes and finds his son recovered at the same hour, and John calls this the second sign in Galilee.
evidence: Say what Jesus said, how the father acted and what he learned.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the nobleman's son?

topics.name: Healing at Bethesda on the Sabbath
topics.description: At a feast in Jerusalem Jesus heals a man who had been ill thirty-eight years by the pool of Bethesda and tells him to take up his bed; because it is the sabbath the Jews persecute Jesus, and when he says his Father works they seek to kill him for making himself equal with God.
evidence: Say what Jesus did and why the leaders wanted to kill him.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the healing at Bethesda and why the Jews opposed Jesus?

topics.name: The Son's Work and Authority
topics.description: Jesus says the Son does only what he sees the Father do, gives life as the Father does, has been given all judgment, and that those who hear his word and believe have eternal life; the dead will hear his voice and come out of the graves to life or judgment.
evidence: Say what Jesus says the Son does with the Father and what he says about life and judgment.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about the Son's work, life and judgment?

topics.name: Witnesses to Jesus
topics.description: Jesus names the witnesses to him: John, his works, the Father, and the Scriptures, which testify of him, and says Moses wrote of him and accuses those who will not come to him for life.
evidence: List the witnesses Jesus names and what he says about Moses.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list the witnesses Jesus gives for himself and what he says about Moses?

topics.name: The Feeding of the Five Thousand
topics.description: Near Passover a large crowd follows Jesus; he tests Philip, takes a boy's five barley loaves and two fishes, gives thanks and distributes, all are filled and twelve baskets are gathered; the people want to take him by force to make him king.
evidence: Retell the miracle and what the crowd wanted to do after.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the feeding of the five thousand in John 6?

topics.name: Jesus Walks on the Sea
topics.description: At night, with a wind blowing, the disciples row across the sea and see Jesus walking on the water; he says 'It is I; be not afraid', and the boat is immediately at land.
evidence: Say what the disciples saw and what Jesus said.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell Jesus walking on the sea?

topics.name: I Am the Bread of Life
topics.description: The crowd seeks Jesus for the loaves; he says to labour for food that endures, that believing is the work of God, that Moses did not give the true bread from heaven, and that he is the bread of life; all the Father gives him will come and he will raise them at the last day.
evidence: Say what Jesus says he is and what he promises those who come to him.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus means by 'I am the bread of life' in this passage?

topics.name: Eat My Flesh, Drink My Blood
topics.description: The Jews murmur that Jesus said he came down from heaven; he says no man comes unless the Father draws him, and that unless they eat his flesh and drink his blood they have no life; he contrasts himself with the manna their fathers ate.
evidence: Say what Jesus says about the Father's drawing and about eating his flesh and drinking his blood.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says in John 6 about the Father drawing and about eating his flesh?

topics.name: Many Disciples Turn Back; Peter's Confession
topics.description: Many disciples find the teaching hard and leave; Jesus asks the twelve if they will go too, and Peter answers 'to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life' and confesses him as the Christ, the Son of the living God; Jesus says one of them is a devil.
evidence: Say why many left and what Peter said.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say why many disciples left and what Peter confessed?

topics.name: Jesus and His Brothers: Going Up to the Feast
topics.description: Near the feast of tabernacles, Jesus' brothers, who do not believe in him, tell him to show himself in Judaea; he says his time has not come and goes up later privately, while people murmur about him.
evidence: Say what his brothers said, what he answered, and how the people reacted.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what happened between Jesus and his brothers before the feast of tabernacles?

topics.name: Teaching in the Temple at the Feast
topics.description: In the middle of the feast Jesus teaches in the temple, saying his doctrine is from the one who sent him; he answers the charge about healing on the sabbath, the crowd debates whether he is the Christ, and officers sent to seize him do not.
evidence: Say where Jesus said his doctrine came from and how the crowd divided.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus claimed about his teaching and how people responded?

topics.name: Rivers of Living Water
topics.description: On the last great day of the feast Jesus cries out that anyone who thirsts should come to him and drink and rivers of living water will flow from the believer, which John says refers to the Spirit to be given after Jesus is glorified; the crowd, officers and Pharisees divide, and Nicodemus speaks for a fair hearing.
evidence: Say what Jesus invited people to do and what John says the living water means.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus offered on the last day of the feast and what John says it means?

topics.name: The Woman Taken in Adultery
topics.description: Scribes and Pharisees bring a woman caught in adultery to Jesus to test him; he says the one without sin may cast the first stone, they leave one by one, and Jesus tells her he does not condemn her and to go and sin no more.
evidence: Say what Jesus said to the accusers and to the woman.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of the woman taken in adultery and what Jesus said?

topics.name: I Am the Light of the World
topics.description: Jesus says 'I am the light of the world', that whoever follows him will not walk in darkness, and defends his testimony as true because the Father who sent him also bears witness; he says those who do not believe that he is he will die in their sins.
evidence: Say what Jesus says about himself as light and what he says to those who do not believe.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain 'I am the light of the world' and what Jesus warns those who do not believe?

topics.name: The Truth Will Set You Free
topics.description: To Jews who believed him, Jesus says continuing in his word means being his disciples and knowing the truth that makes free; he says whoever commits sin is sin's servant, and the Son sets free indeed, and denies that those seeking to kill him are doing Abraham's works.
evidence: Say what Jesus says sets people free and what he says about who is a servant of sin.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus means by the truth making free and who he says is a servant of sin?

topics.name: Before Abraham Was, I Am
topics.description: The Jews accuse Jesus of a devil; he says Abraham rejoiced to see his day, and when they say he is not fifty and has seen Abraham, Jesus says 'Before Abraham was, I am', and they take up stones.
evidence: Say what Jesus said about Abraham and how the Jews reacted.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about Abraham and how his hearers responded?

topics.name: A Man Born Blind Is Healed
topics.description: Jesus sees a man blind from birth, says the blindness is so God's works may be shown, declares himself the light of the world, anoints his eyes with clay and sends him to wash in Siloam, and the man sees.
evidence: Say why the man was blind according to Jesus and how he was healed.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how Jesus healed the man born blind?

topics.name: The Healed Man Before the Pharisees
topics.description: The Pharisees question the healed man and his parents, divide over the sabbath, and cast the man out when he says Jesus must be from God; Jesus finds him, the man believes and worships, and Jesus says those who say 'we see' remain in sin.
evidence: Say how the healed man answered the Pharisees and what happened when Jesus found him.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what happened when the healed man was questioned and what Jesus said to him afterwards?

topics.name: I Am the Door and the Good Shepherd
topics.description: Jesus says he is the door of the sheep and the good shepherd who knows his sheep, lays down his life for them, has other sheep not of this fold, and has power to lay down his life and take it again.
evidence: Say what Jesus says the good shepherd does and what he says about his life.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the good shepherd teaching and what it says about Jesus' life and death?

topics.name: I and My Father Are One
topics.description: At the feast of dedication the Jews ask Jesus to say plainly if he is the Christ; he says his sheep hear his voice and no one can pluck them from his hand and 'I and my Father are one', and they take up stones, but he escapes beyond Jordan.
evidence: Say what Jesus says about his sheep and about himself and the Father.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about his sheep and his oneness with the Father?

topics.name: Lazarus Is Sick and Dies
topics.description: Mary and Martha send word that Lazarus is sick; Jesus says the sickness is for the glory of God, stays two days, then tells the disciples Lazarus sleeps and is dead, and Thomas says they may go and die with him.
evidence: Say what Jesus said about Lazarus's sickness and what he did.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said about Lazarus's illness and why he waited?

topics.name: I Am the Resurrection and the Life
topics.description: Martha meets Jesus, who tells her that her brother will rise again and says 'I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live'; Martha confesses him the Christ, the Son of God, and Mary and the mourners weep and Jesus weeps.
evidence: Say what Jesus said to Martha and what she answered.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus says to Martha about the resurrection and life?

topics.name: Jesus Raises Lazarus
topics.description: At the tomb Jesus has the stone taken away, prays to the Father, and cries 'Lazarus, come forth'; the dead man comes out bound in graveclothes.
evidence: Retell the raising of Lazarus.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the raising of Lazarus?

topics.name: The Council Plots to Kill Jesus
topics.description: Many believe after the raising of Lazarus, but others tell the Pharisees; the chief priests and Pharisees hold a council, and Caiaphas says one man should die for the people, which John says was prophecy, and from that day they plan to put Jesus to death.
evidence: Say what the council feared, what Caiaphas said and what John says it meant.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the council plotted against Jesus and what Caiaphas said?

topics.name: Mary Anoints Jesus at Bethany
topics.description: Six days before Passover a supper is made at Bethany; Mary anoints Jesus' feet with costly ointment, Judas objects but John says he was a thief, and Jesus says she kept it for the day of his burying.
evidence: Say what Mary did, what Judas said and how Jesus answered.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell Mary's anointing of Jesus and Judas's objection?

topics.name: The Entry into Jerusalem
topics.description: The crowd takes palm branches and cries 'Hosanna', Jesus rides a young donkey as written, the disciples later remember this after he is glorified, and the Pharisees say the world has gone after him.
evidence: Say how the crowd greeted Jesus and what John says the disciples understood later.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' entry into Jerusalem in John?

topics.name: The Hour Has Come: A Grain of Wheat
topics.description: Greeks ask to see Jesus; he says the hour has come for the Son of man to be glorified, that a grain of wheat must fall and die to bear fruit, that when he is lifted up he will draw all men, and a voice from heaven answers his prayer.
evidence: Say what Jesus says about the grain of wheat and about being lifted up.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the grain of wheat saying and what Jesus says about being lifted up?

topics.name: Unbelief and Jesus' Final Public Words
topics.description: Despite many signs the people do not believe, which John says fulfils Isaiah, and many rulers believe but fear confessing him; Jesus cries that believing in him is believing in the one who sent him and that he came as light, not to judge but to save.
evidence: Say why John says the people did not believe and what Jesus says about those who hear and reject his words.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what John says about unbelief and what Jesus says about his words and judgment?

topics.name: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
topics.description: Before the Passover, knowing his hour has come, Jesus rises from supper and washes his disciples' feet; he says Peter will know later and that those he washes are clean, then tells them to wash one another's feet as he did.
evidence: Say what Jesus did, what Peter said and what Jesus told the disciples to do.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the foot washing and what Jesus said it was for?

topics.name: Jesus Identifies the Betrayer
topics.description: Troubled in spirit, Jesus says one of the twelve will betray him; he gives a sop to Judas, Satan enters Judas, Jesus tells him to do quickly what he does, and Judas goes out into the night.
evidence: Say how Jesus pointed to the betrayer and what Judas did.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how Judas was identified and what he did?

topics.name: A New Commandment
topics.description: After Judas leaves, Jesus says the Son of man is now glorified and gives a new commandment to love one another as he loved them, by which all men will know they are his disciples; he tells Peter he will deny him thrice before the cock crows.
evidence: Say what the new commandment is and what Jesus told Peter.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus' new commandment is and what he foretold about Peter?

topics.name: I Am the Way, the Truth and the Life
topics.description: Jesus tells the disciples not to be troubled, that he goes to prepare a place in his Father's house and will come again; to Thomas he says 'I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me', and to Philip that seeing him is seeing the Father.
evidence: Say what Jesus promised about the Father's house and what he said about the way to the Father.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about the way to the Father and the place he prepares?

topics.name: The Promise of the Comforter
topics.description: Jesus promises to ask the Father to give another Comforter, the Spirit of truth, who will abide with them and teach and remind them of all he said; he leaves his peace and says that those who love him keep his word.
evidence: Say what Jesus promises about the Spirit and what he says about loving him.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus promises about the Comforter and the Holy Ghost in John 14?

topics.name: I Am the True Vine
topics.description: Jesus says he is the true vine, the Father the husbandman and the disciples the branches; they must abide in him to bear fruit, keep his commandments, love one another, and are called friends whom he chose.
evidence: Say what Jesus says branches must do and what he says about love and friends.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the vine and branches picture and what abiding means?

topics.name: The World's Hatred and the Witness of the Spirit
topics.description: Jesus warns the disciples that the world hated him first and will hate them and persecute them, that the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, will testify of him, and that they will also bear witness.
evidence: Say why Jesus says the world will hate his disciples and who will testify.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the world hates the disciples and who will bear witness according to Jesus?

topics.name: The Work of the Spirit
topics.description: Jesus says it is expedient that he goes away so the Comforter will come, who will reprove the world of sin, righteousness and judgment, guide the disciples into all truth and glorify Jesus.
evidence: Say what the Spirit will do when he comes.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus says the Spirit will do for the world and for the disciples?

topics.name: Sorrow Turned to Joy; I Have Overcome the World
topics.description: Jesus says the disciples will weep but their sorrow will become joy, like a woman after travail, promises that the Father will give what they ask in his name, and says that though they will be scattered he has overcome the world.
evidence: Say what Jesus says about their sorrow and his last words about peace and the world.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' words on sorrow turning to joy and 'I have overcome the world'?

topics.name: Jesus' Prayer for Glory and for His Disciples
topics.description: Jesus looks to heaven and prays for the Father to glorify the Son, says eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, and prays for the disciples he has kept, that the Father would keep them, sanctify them by truth, and not take them out of the world.
evidence: Say what Jesus asks for himself and for the disciples.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus prays for himself and his disciples in John 17?

topics.name: Jesus' Prayer for All Believers
topics.description: Jesus prays for those who will believe through the disciples' word, that they may all be one as the Father is in him and he in the Father so the world may believe, and that they be with him to see his glory.
evidence: Say who Jesus prays for here and what he asks.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say who Jesus prays for in John 17:20-26 and what he asks?

topics.name: Jesus Is Arrested in the Garden
topics.description: Jesus crosses the brook Cedron to a garden; Judas comes with soldiers and officers, Jesus says 'I am he' and they fall backward, he asks that his disciples go free, rebukes Peter's sword-cutting and says he must drink the cup the Father gave him.
evidence: Say what happened when Jesus said 'I am he' and what he told Peter.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the arrest of Jesus in John 18?

topics.name: Before Annas; Peter Denies
topics.description: Jesus is taken to Annas and Caiaphas and is questioned about his disciples and doctrine; meanwhile Peter at the fire three times denies being his disciple, and a cock crows.
evidence: Say what Jesus said to the high priest and what Peter did.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell Jesus before the high priest and Peter's denials?

topics.name: Jesus Before Pilate: My Kingdom Is Not of This World
topics.description: The Jews take Jesus to Pilate; Pilate asks if he is King of the Jews, Jesus says his kingdom is not of this world and that he came to bear witness to the truth, Pilate finds no fault, and the crowd asks for Barabbas.
evidence: Say what Jesus told Pilate about his kingdom and who the crowd chose.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told Pilate about his kingdom?

topics.name: Scourged, Mocked and Sentenced
topics.description: Pilate has Jesus scourged and mocked with a crown of thorns; the Jews say he made himself the Son of God and, when Pilate seeks to release him, cry 'Crucify him' and say 'We have no king but Caesar'; Pilate delivers Jesus to be crucified.
evidence: Say what the soldiers did, what the Jews cried and what Pilate finally did.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified?

topics.name: The Crucifixion
topics.description: Jesus carries his cross to Golgotha and is crucified between two others under a title 'Jesus of Nazareth the King of the Jews'; soldiers cast lots for his coat, he commits his mother to the beloved disciple, says 'I thirst' and 'It is finished', bows his head and gives up the ghost.
evidence: Say what Jesus said from the cross and what the soldiers did with his clothes.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the crucifixion in John and name Jesus' last words?

topics.name: His Side Pierced and the Burial
topics.description: The soldiers do not break Jesus' legs but pierce his side, and John says these things fulfil Scripture; Joseph of Arimathaea and Nicodemus wrap his body with spices and lay it in a new tomb in a garden.
evidence: Say what the soldiers did and who buried Jesus.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what happened to Jesus' body after his death and who buried him?

topics.name: The Empty Tomb
topics.description: Mary Magdalene finds the stone taken away and tells Peter and the beloved disciple; they run to the tomb, find the linen clothes lying, and the other disciple sees and believes.
evidence: Say what the disciples found in the tomb.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what Peter and the other disciple found at the tomb?

topics.name: Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene
topics.description: Mary weeps at the tomb, sees two angels, turns and takes Jesus for the gardener until he says her name; she tells the disciples she has seen the Lord.
evidence: Say how Mary recognised Jesus and what she told the disciples.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how Mary Magdalene met the risen Jesus?

topics.name: Jesus Appears to the Disciples
topics.description: On the evening of the first day Jesus stands among the disciples behind shut doors, shows his hands and side, says 'Peace be unto you', sends them as the Father sent him, breathes on them and says 'Receive ye the Holy Ghost'.
evidence: Say what Jesus showed them and what he told them.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Jesus showed and told the disciples on the evening of the resurrection?

topics.name: Thomas and the Purpose of John's Book
topics.description: Thomas, absent the first time, says he will not believe unless he sees and touches; eight days later Jesus appears and Thomas says 'My Lord and my God'; John says the signs are written that readers may believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life.
evidence: Say what Thomas said and why John says the book was written.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of Thomas and say why John says he wrote?

topics.name: The Great Catch and Breakfast by the Sea
topics.description: Seven disciples fish all night without a catch; Jesus on the shore tells them to cast on the right side and the net is full, the beloved disciple says 'It is the Lord', Peter swims ashore, and Jesus gives them bread and fish by a fire of coals.
evidence: Retell the catch and how the disciples recognised Jesus.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' appearance by the sea of Tiberias?

topics.name: Peter Restored and the Last Words
topics.description: Jesus asks Peter three times if he loves him and tells him to feed his sheep, foretells how Peter will die, tells him to follow him and not worry about the beloved disciple; John says this disciple wrote these things and that the world could not hold all that Jesus did.
evidence: Say what Jesus asked Peter and told him to do.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what Jesus asked Peter and told him after breakfast?

topics.name: 1 Kings: overview
topics.description: 1 Kings opens with David old and Solomon made king (1:1-53), moves through Solomon's wisdom, temple and decline, then the division of the kingdom and the prophets Elijah and Micaiah under Israel's kings, ending with Ahab's death and Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah (22:53).
evidence: Name the main phases: Solomon's accession, the temple, the divided kingdom, Elijah and Ahab
Say how the book begins (David's old age) and ends (Ahaziah of Israel)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline 1 Kings in order, from Solomon's accession to Ahab's death?

topics.name: Adonijah exalts himself and Solomon is anointed
topics.description: Adonijah declares he will be king, but Nathan and Bathsheba remind David of his oath, and David has Zadok and Nathan anoint Solomon at Gihon. Adonijah flees to the altar and Solomon spares him on condition of good conduct.
evidence: Retell how Adonijah's attempt failed and Solomon was anointed
Name the people who stood with Adonijah and the people who did not
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Solomon became king instead of Adonijah?

topics.name: David's charge to Solomon and his death
topics.description: David, nearing death, tells Solomon to keep the LORD's commandments so the LORD will continue his word about David's house, and gives instructions about Joab, Barzillai's sons and Shimei. David dies after reigning forty years and Solomon sits on his throne.
evidence: Say what David told Solomon to do in order to walk with the LORD (2:3-4)
State how long David reigned and where he was buried
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what David charged Solomon with before he died?

topics.name: Solomon establishes his kingdom
topics.description: Solomon has Adonijah put to death after Adonijah asks for Abishag, removes Abiathar from the priesthood, has Joab killed at the altar, and puts Shimei to death when he leaves Jerusalem against his oath. The text concludes that the kingdom was established in Solomon's hand.
evidence: List the four men dealt with in chapter 2 and why each was judged
Find the verse that says the kingdom was established (2:46)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon dealt with Adonijah, Abiathar, Joab and Shimei?

topics.name: Solomon asks for wisdom at Gibeon
topics.description: At Gibeon the LORD appears to Solomon in a dream and says "Ask what I shall give thee"; Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people, and God also gives him riches and honour with a call to walk in his ways.
evidence: Say what Solomon asked for and what God added
Explain why the LORD was pleased with the request (3:10-11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon asked God for at Gibeon, and what God gave him?

topics.name: Solomon judges between two mothers
topics.description: Two women claim the same living child; Solomon orders the child divided, and the mother whose heart yearns for her son is revealed. All Israel sees the wisdom of God in him.
evidence: Retell how Solomon found the real mother
Say what Israel concluded about Solomon (3:28)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of the two mothers and say what it shows about Solomon's wisdom?

topics.name: Solomon's officials, provisions and fame
topics.description: Chapter 4 lists Solomon's officials and twelve district officers, describes Israel dwelling safely and his wide dominion, and records his wisdom, proverbs and songs and the visitors who came to hear him.
evidence: Name the picture of peace in 4:25
Give two ways the chapter shows Solomon's wisdom or fame (4:29-34)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how 1 Kings 4 shows God keeping his word to give Solomon wisdom?

topics.name: Solomon and Hiram prepare to build the temple
topics.description: Solomon tells Hiram of Tyre that David could not build the house because of his wars, but that the LORD has given rest; Hiram supplies cedar and fir for wheat and oil, and Solomon raises a levy of workers.
evidence: Say why David had not built the house (5:3)
Describe the agreement between Solomon and Hiram
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Solomon, not David, built the house of the LORD?

topics.name: Solomon builds the temple
topics.description: The house of the LORD is built in seven and a half years of work with stone, cedar and gold, with an inner oracle holding two cherubim. In the middle of the building the LORD tells Solomon that if he keeps the statutes, God will dwell among Israel.
evidence: Say what was in the inner room (the oracle) and what covered the house
State the condition and promise in 6:12-13
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the temple Solomon built and what the LORD said to him about it?

topics.name: Solomon's palace and the temple furnishings
topics.description: Solomon builds his own house over thirteen years, and Hiram of Tyre casts the two bronze pillars, the molten sea, bases, lavers and other vessels for the temple.
evidence: Name some of the bronze items Hiram made
Say how long Solomon took to build his own house (7:1)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name some furnishings made for the temple and who made them?

topics.name: The ark is brought into the temple and the glory fills it
topics.description: At the feast Solomon and the elders bring the ark of the covenant into the oracle; there is nothing in it but the two tables of stone, and a cloud fills the house so the priests cannot minister.
evidence: Say what the ark contained (8:9)
Describe what happened when the priests came out (8:10-11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the ark was brought into the new temple?

topics.name: Solomon blesses Israel and recalls the LORD's word to David
topics.description: Solomon blesses the LORD for keeping what he spoke to David his father, that David's son would build the house, and says the place is set for the ark with the covenant the LORD made with Israel's fathers.
evidence: Say what the LORD promised David about the house (8:18-19)
Explain how Solomon says the promise was kept (8:20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon says the LORD had spoken to David about building the house?

topics.name: Solomon's prayer of dedication
topics.description: Standing before the altar, Solomon praises the LORD who keeps covenant and mercy, asks that the promise to David be confirmed, and prays that God will hear and forgive in specific situations of sin, defeat, famine, a stranger's prayer and exile.
evidence: Say what Solomon asks God to do when his people sin and then repent (8:33-34, 46-50)
Find where Solomon asks God to keep his word to David (8:25-26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} summarise Solomon's dedication prayer and what he asks for?

topics.name: Solomon blesses the people and the feast ends
topics.description: Solomon blesses the congregation, urges their hearts to be perfect with the LORD, and the king and all Israel offer great sacrifices and keep a feast before sending the people home joyful.
evidence: Say what Solomon urged the people to do (8:61)
Describe how the people went home (8:66)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the dedication of the temple ended?

topics.name: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time
topics.description: The LORD says he has hallowed the house and promises to establish Solomon's throne for ever as he promised David if Solomon walks in integrity, but warns that if Israel and their children turn away he will cut Israel off and cast out the house.
evidence: State the promise and the warning (9:4-7)
Say what the nations would conclude if Israel forsook the LORD (9:8-9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the conditions the LORD set before Solomon after the temple was finished?

topics.name: Solomon's cities, labour and ships
topics.description: Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities, raises a levy to build the temple, his house and cities, puts the remaining Canaanite peoples to forced labour, offers sacrifices three times a year, and builds a fleet that brings gold from Ophir.
evidence: Name some things built with the levy (9:15-19)
Say where the fleet gold came from (9:26-28)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon used his labour force and wealth after the temple was built?

topics.name: The queen of Sheba visits Solomon
topics.description: The queen of Sheba comes to test Solomon with hard questions, sees his wisdom and house, and blesses the LORD who set him on the throne. The chapter also records Solomon's great gold, ivory throne, chariots and horses.
evidence: Say what the queen concluded after seeing Solomon (10:6-9)
Name some signs of Solomon's wealth in the chapter
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why the queen of Sheba came and what she said about the LORD?

topics.name: Solomon's heart turns away
topics.description: Solomon loves many foreign wives from nations the LORD had forbidden, his wives turn his heart to other gods, and he builds high places. The LORD tells him he will tear the kingdom away, though not in his days and not all of it, for David's sake.
evidence: Say what turned Solomon's heart (11:3-4)
State what the LORD said would happen and what he would hold back (11:11-13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD was angry with Solomon and what he said would follow?

topics.name: Adversaries and Jeroboam's promise
topics.description: The LORD raises up Hadad the Edomite and Rezon of Damascus against Solomon, and the prophet Ahijah tears his garment in twelve pieces and tells Jeroboam he will rule ten tribes if he walks in the LORD's ways. Solomon seeks to kill Jeroboam, who flees to Egypt, and Solomon dies after forty years.
evidence: Name the adversaries raised up against Solomon
Explain what the torn garment pictured (11:29-31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe Ahijah's sign to Jeroboam and what it meant?

topics.name: The kingdom divides at Shechem
topics.description: Rehoboam rejects the old men's counsel and answers Israel harshly; ten tribes break away and make Jeroboam king while Judah stays with Rehoboam. The text says the cause was from the LORD, and Shemaiah forbids war against their brethren.
evidence: Compare the counsel of the old men and the young men (12:7, 10-11)
Say which tribes followed Rehoboam and which followed Jeroboam
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the kingdom of Israel was divided after Solomon?

topics.name: Jeroboam makes golden calves at Bethel and Dan
topics.description: Fearing his people will return to Rehoboam if they go to Jerusalem, Jeroboam makes two golden calves, sets them in Bethel and Dan, appoints priests who were not Levites and ordains a feast. The text says this thing became a sin.
evidence: Say why Jeroboam made the calves (12:26-27)
List the changes he made to Israel's worship
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jeroboam did at Bethel and Dan and why it was sin?

topics.name: The man of God from Judah and the old prophet
topics.description: A man of God from Judah cries against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, naming a child Josiah, and the altar is rent. He is told not to eat or drink there, but is deceived by an old prophet and killed by a lion on the way home.
evidence: Retell how the man of God disobeyed and what happened
Say what the sign at the altar was (13:3-5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of the man of God who came from Judah to Bethel?

topics.name: Ahijah announces judgment on Jeroboam's house
topics.description: Jeroboam's wife, disguised, goes to Ahijah about her sick son; Ahijah tells her the LORD will cut off Jeroboam's house and root up Israel from the land because of his sins. The chapter then reports Jeroboam's death and Rehoboam's evil reign in Judah, including Shishak's raid on Jerusalem.
evidence: Say what Ahijah announced about Jeroboam's house (14:10-16)
Name what Shishak of Egypt took from Jerusalem (14:25-26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD said through Ahijah about Jeroboam and about Israel?

topics.name: Abijam and Asa reign in Judah
topics.description: Abijam walks in his father's sins, yet for David's sake the LORD gives him a lamp in Jerusalem. Asa does right as David did, removes idols and his mother Maachah from being queen, but the high places stay; he pays Benhadad of Syria to break with Baasha of Israel.
evidence: Say what Asa removed and what he left (15:12-14)
Explain how Asa dealt with Baasha's building of Ramah (15:17-22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Asa served the LORD and where he fell short?

topics.name: Nadab and Baasha, kings of Israel
topics.description: Nadab of Israel walks in Jeroboam's sin and Baasha kills him and all of Jeroboam's house. The LORD then speaks through Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha for walking in Jeroboam's way.
evidence: Say how Jeroboam's house ended (15:29-30)
State the word of the LORD against Baasha (16:2-4)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the house of Jeroboam ended, and why Baasha was judged too?

topics.name: Elah, Zimri and Omri
topics.description: Zimri kills Elah and Baasha's house, reigns seven days and burns the palace when Omri besieges Tirzah; Israel divides between Tibni and Omri, and Omri prevails, buys the hill of Samaria and does worse than all before him.
evidence: Say how Zimri's reign ended (16:15-19)
Name the city Omri built and what he did in the LORD's sight (16:24-26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} follow the quick succession of Elah, Zimri and Omri in Israel?

topics.name: Ahab begins to reign
topics.description: Ahab son of Omri does evil above all before him, marries Jezebel daughter of the king of the Zidonians, serves Baal and builds an altar for Baal in Samaria. The chapter ends with Hiel building Jericho at the cost of his sons.
evidence: Name three things that made Ahab worse than earlier kings (16:30-33)
Say who Ahab married
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what kind of king Ahab was and who his wife was?

topics.name: Elijah announces drought and is fed by ravens
topics.description: Elijah the Tishbite tells Ahab there will be neither dew nor rain except by his word, and the LORD sends him to hide by the brook Cherith, where ravens bring him bread and flesh until the brook dries up.
evidence: Say what Elijah told Ahab (17:1)
Explain how the LORD fed Elijah at Cherith
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how God provided for Elijah by the brook Cherith?

topics.name: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath
topics.description: The LORD sends Elijah to a widow at Zarephath with only a handful of meal and a little oil; at his word she feeds him first, and the barrel and cruse do not run out.
evidence: Retell what the widow had and what happened to it
Say whose word the meal and oil followed (17:14, 16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the widow's meal and oil, and why?

topics.name: The widow's son is raised
topics.description: The widow's son falls sick and dies; Elijah prays and stretches himself on the child, the LORD hears and the child revives. The woman says she now knows Elijah is a man of God and the LORD's word in his mouth is truth.
evidence: Retell what Elijah did and prayed
Say what the widow confessed at the end (17:24)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the widow's son was brought back to life and what she said?

topics.name: Elijah meets Obadiah and Ahab
topics.description: In the third year of the famine the LORD sends Elijah to show himself to Ahab; Obadiah, who feared the LORD and hid a hundred prophets from Jezebel, brings word. Elijah tells Ahab that he and his father's house have troubled Israel by forsaking the LORD, and calls for a gathering on Carmel.
evidence: Say what Obadiah did for the LORD's prophets (18:4)
State who Elijah said had troubled Israel (18:17-18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Elijah told Ahab when they met?

topics.name: The LORD answers by fire on Mount Carmel
topics.description: Elijah challenges the people to choose between the LORD and Baal and sets a test: the God who answers by fire is God. Baal's prophets cry out all day without answer; Elijah's drenched sacrifice is consumed by the fire of the LORD, and the people declare that the LORD is God.
evidence: Retell the contest and its result
Say what the people cried when the fire fell (18:39)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the contest on Carmel and what it proved?

topics.name: The rain returns
topics.description: Elijah tells Ahab to eat, because there is the sound of abundance of rain; after he prays and his servant looks seven times, a small cloud rises and heavy rain falls.
evidence: Say what Elijah's servant saw on the seventh look (18:44)
Explain what this ended (compare 17:1)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the drought ended in Elijah's day?

topics.name: Elijah flees from Jezebel
topics.description: Jezebel vows to kill Elijah, and he flees to the wilderness and asks to die under a juniper tree; an angel touches him and feeds him, and he walks forty days and nights to Horeb.
evidence: Say what led Elijah to flee (19:1-3)
Describe how the LORD cared for him (19:5-8)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why Elijah ran away, and how God cared for him?

topics.name: The LORD speaks to Elijah at Horeb
topics.description: At Horeb Elijah complains that he alone is left; the LORD is not in the wind, earthquake or fire but in a still small voice, and sends him to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha, saying he has left seven thousand who have not bowed to Baal.
evidence: Describe the wind, earthquake, fire and voice
State the three people Elijah was told to anoint and the number left in Israel
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD told Elijah at Horeb and how he spoke?

topics.name: Elijah calls Elisha
topics.description: Elijah finds Elisha son of Shaphat ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen and casts his mantle on him; Elisha slaughters a yoke of oxen, boils the flesh, takes leave of his parents and follows Elijah.
evidence: Say what Elijah did to call Elisha (19:19)
Say what Elisha did before following
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Elisha was called to follow Elijah?

topics.name: Israel defeats Benhadad at Samaria
topics.description: Benhadad of Syria and thirty-two kings demand Ahab's silver, gold and family; a prophet tells Ahab the LORD will deliver the host into his hand by the young men of the provincial princes, and Israel wins.
evidence: Say what the prophet promised and why (20:13)
Describe how the battle went (20:15-21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Israel beat the Syrian army at Samaria?

topics.name: Aphek and Ahab spares Benhadad
topics.description: The Syrians say the LORD is a god of the hills, so the LORD gives Israel victory on the plain at Aphek; Ahab then makes a covenant with Benhadad and lets him go. A prophet, disguised, tells Ahab that for letting go the man the LORD appointed to destruction, his life will go for Benhadad's life.
evidence: Say what the Syrians said about the LORD and what the LORD answered (20:23, 28)
Explain the prophet's message to Ahab (20:42)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD was displeased when Ahab let Benhadad go?

topics.name: Naboth's vineyard
topics.description: Ahab wants Naboth's vineyard, but Naboth will not give his fathers' inheritance; Jezebel arranges false witnesses so Naboth is stoned and Ahab takes the vineyard.
evidence: Say why Naboth refused (21:3)
Describe what Jezebel did to get the vineyard
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how Ahab and Jezebel took Naboth's vineyard, and what was wrong with it?

topics.name: Elijah pronounces judgment on Ahab
topics.description: The LORD sends Elijah to Ahab in Naboth's vineyard: Ahab's house will be cut off like Jeroboam's and Baasha's and the dogs will eat Jezebel. Ahab tears his clothes and humbles himself, and the LORD says the evil will not come in his days but in his son's.
evidence: State the judgment on Ahab and on Jezebel (21:21-24)
Say how the LORD responded when Ahab humbled himself (21:27-29)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Elijah told Ahab about Naboth's vineyard and what happened when Ahab humbled himself?

topics.name: Micaiah prophesies against Ahab
topics.description: Ahab asks Jehoshaphat to join him at Ramoth-gilead; four hundred prophets say go, but Micaiah, after saying the LORD's word, describes Israel scattered as sheep without a shepherd and a lying spirit in the prophets' mouths. Ahab puts Micaiah in prison.
evidence: Compare the four hundred prophets and Micaiah
Say what Ahab did with Micaiah (22:26-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Jehoshaphat wanted to hear a prophet of the LORD and what Micaiah said?

topics.name: Ahab dies at Ramoth-gilead
topics.description: Ahab disguises himself in battle but a man draws a bow at random and strikes him; he dies, and the dogs lick his blood as the LORD had said.
evidence: Say how Ahab tried to avoid Micaiah's word and what happened
Find the verse that says his death was according to the LORD's word (22:38)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Ahab died and how it matched what the LORD said?

topics.name: Jehoshaphat of Judah and Ahaziah of Israel
topics.description: Jehoshaphat walks in the ways of Asa and does right, though the high places remain; his ships to Ophir are broken. Ahaziah son of Ahab reigns in Israel, serving Baal as his father did.
evidence: Say how Jehoshaphat is described (22:43)
Say how Ahaziah is described (22:52-53)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} compare Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah as the book of 1 Kings ends?

topics.name: 2 Kings: overview
topics.description: 2 Kings continues the divided kingdom from Ahaziah of Israel through Elijah and Elisha, the end of the house of Ahab, the fall of Samaria and the exile of Israel (ch. 17), the kings of Judah including Hezekiah and Josiah, and the exile of Judah to Babylon (ch. 25).
evidence: Name the two kingdoms and say how each ends (ch. 17 and ch. 25)
Name Elijah, Elisha, Hezekiah and Josiah and where they appear
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline 2 Kings in order, from Elijah's last days to the exile in Babylon?

topics.name: Ahaziah consults Baal-zebub and fire falls
topics.description: Ahaziah, hurt in a fall, sends to ask Baal-zebub god of Ekron whether he will recover; Elijah meets the messengers and says he will die because there is a God in Israel. Fire from heaven consumes two captains of fifty, and Elijah goes with the third.
evidence: Say why Ahaziah was told he would die (1:3-4, 16)
Retell what happened to the captains of fifty
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why Elijah sent Ahaziah this message and what happened to the soldiers?

topics.name: Elijah is taken up and Elisha receives his mantle
topics.description: Elijah and Elisha cross Jordan, Elisha asks for a double portion of Elijah's spirit, and Elijah is taken up by a whirlwind with a chariot of fire. Elisha takes up the fallen mantle, strikes the Jordan and crosses, and the sons of the prophets say the spirit of Elijah rests on him.
evidence: Describe how Elijah left and what Elisha picked up
Say what the sons of the prophets recognised (2:15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Elijah left the earth and who took up his work?

topics.name: Elisha heals the spring and the boys mock him
topics.description: At Jericho Elisha casts salt into the spring and the waters are healed, according to his word; going up to Bethel, small boys mock him and two she bears tear forty-two of them after he curses them in the LORD's name.
evidence: Say what Elisha did to the waters at Jericho and by whose word
Describe what happened at Bethel (2:23-24)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did at Jericho and what happened on the road to Bethel?

topics.name: Three kings and Moab: water in the valley
topics.description: Jehoram of Israel, Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom march against rebel Moab and run out of water; Elisha, for Jehoshaphat's sake, says the LORD will fill the valley and give Moab into their hand. Water comes by morning and Moab is defeated, though the king of Moab offers his eldest son on the wall.
evidence: Say why Elisha agreed to inquire of the LORD (3:13-14)
Describe how the water came (3:16-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD provided for the three kings, and why Elisha helped?

topics.name: Elisha and the widow's oil
topics.description: A prophet's widow cries to Elisha because a creditor will take her two sons; Elisha tells her to borrow empty vessels and pour from her small pot of oil, and the oil flows until all the vessels are full, so she sells it and pays her debt.
evidence: Say what the widow had in the house and what happened to it
Say what she did with the oil afterwards (4:7)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how Elisha helped the widow pay her debt?

topics.name: The Shunammite woman's son
topics.description: A woman of Shunem builds a room for Elisha and, as he promised, bears a son; when the boy later dies, she goes to Elisha at Carmel, and Elisha prays, stretches himself on the child, and the boy sneezes and opens his eyes.
evidence: Say what the woman did for Elisha and what he promised her
Describe how Elisha restored the child
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how the Shunammite's son was brought back to life?

topics.name: Death in the pot and the loaves
topics.description: In a famine at Gilgal, wild gourds make the stew deadly and Elisha casts in meal so it is harmless; he then has a hundred men fed from twenty loaves, with some left, according to the LORD's word.
evidence: Say how Elisha made the pottage safe
Say what the LORD said about the twenty loaves (4:43)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did for the sons of the prophets during the famine?

topics.name: Naaman is healed of leprosy
topics.description: Naaman, the Syrian commander, hears from an Israelite servant girl of the prophet in Samaria, goes to Elisha and is told to wash seven times in Jordan; he is angry but obeys and is healed, and confesses there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. Gehazi takes a reward by deceit and Naaman's leprosy comes on him.
evidence: Retell why Naaman was angry and what changed his mind
Say what happened to Gehazi and why (5:20-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell the story of Naaman, the servant girl and Gehazi?

topics.name: The iron axe head floats
topics.description: While the sons of the prophets cut beams at Jordan, a borrowed axe head falls into the water; Elisha casts in a stick and the iron swims, and the man takes it up.
evidence: Say what Elisha threw into the water and what happened
Say why the man was distressed (6:5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what happened to the borrowed axe head?

topics.name: Elisha and the Syrian army at Dothan
topics.description: The king of Syria sends an army to take Elisha at Dothan; Elisha's servant sees them, Elisha prays and the servant sees chariots of fire around the mountain. The Syrians are struck blind, led to Samaria, given food and sent home, and the bands of Syria stop coming into Israel.
evidence: Say what the servant saw when his eyes were opened (6:17)
Explain how Elisha told the king of Israel to treat the Syrians (6:21-23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha's servant saw at Dothan and how the story ended?

topics.name: Famine in besieged Samaria
topics.description: Benhadad besieges Samaria, a great famine follows and the king of Israel, hearing a woman's terrible plea, tears his clothes and swears to take Elisha's head; Elisha tells the elders the king's messenger is coming.
evidence: Describe the state of the city (6:25)
Say what the king blamed and decided (6:31, 33)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the famine in Samaria and how the king reacted?

topics.name: The LORD lifts the siege of Samaria
topics.description: Elisha says that by tomorrow fine flour will sell for a shekel at the gate; four lepers find the Syrian camp empty because the LORD made the Syrians hear the noise of a great host, and the city is plundered. The lord who doubted sees it but dies in the gate trampled by the crowd.
evidence: Say what Elisha prophesied (7:1) and how it happened
Say what happened to the doubting lord (7:17-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the siege of Samaria ended and how Elisha's word came true?

topics.name: The Shunammite's land and Elisha at Damascus
topics.description: Elisha warns the Shunammite of a seven-year famine; on her return the king hears about Elisha's deeds from Gehazi and restores her land. Elisha later tells Hazael he will be king of Syria and do great evil to Israel, and Hazael kills Benhadad.
evidence: Say what the king restored to the woman and why (8:4-6)
Say what Elisha told Hazael and how Elisha reacted (8:12)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the Shunammite woman after the famine, and what Elisha said to Hazael?

topics.name: Jehoram and Ahaziah of Judah
topics.description: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat marries a daughter of Ahab and does evil, yet the LORD will not destroy Judah for David's sake, as he promised David a light for his children. Edom revolts; his son Ahaziah walks in the way of Ahab's house and goes with Joram of Israel to fight Hazael at Ramoth-gilead.
evidence: Say why the LORD did not destroy Judah (8:19)
Say how Jehoram and Ahaziah are compared to the house of Ahab (8:18, 27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why God spared Judah despite Jehoram's evil?

topics.name: Jehu is anointed king over Israel
topics.description: Elisha sends a young prophet to Ramoth-gilead to pour oil on Jehu's head and announce that he will strike the house of Ahab, and that dogs will eat Jezebel; the captains acclaim Jehu king.
evidence: Say what Jehu was told to do (9:6-10)
Describe how the other captains responded (9:13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jehu was anointed and what he was told to do?

topics.name: Jehu strikes Joram and Ahaziah
topics.description: Jehu drives to Jezreel and shoots Joram, throwing him into Naboth's field according to the LORD's word; Ahaziah of Judah flees and is killed too.
evidence: Say where Joram died and why Jehu cited Naboth (9:25-26)
Say what happened to Ahaziah of Judah
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Joram and Ahaziah were killed?

topics.name: The death of Jezebel
topics.description: Jehu enters Jezreel; Jezebel is thrown from the window, trampled, and the dogs eat her, so that Jehu says it is the word of the LORD spoken by Elijah.
evidence: Say how Jezebel died and what remained
Find the verse that links her death to Elijah's word (9:36)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Elijah's word about Jezebel came true?

topics.name: Jehu destroys the house of Ahab and the worship of Baal
topics.description: Jehu has Ahab's seventy sons killed in Samaria, kills Ahaziah's brethren and the remainder of Ahab's house, then gathers the worshippers of Baal in the house of Baal and has them slain, destroying the house and image of Baal.
evidence: Say how Jehu summoned the worshippers of Baal and what he did
Say whose word Jehu says is fulfilled (10:10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jehu did to Ahab's house and to Baal worship in Israel?

topics.name: Jehu's reign and its limits
topics.description: The LORD tells Jehu that his sons to the fourth generation will sit on Israel's throne, but Jehu does not depart from Jeroboam's calves or walk in the law with all his heart, and the LORD begins to cut Israel short by Hazael.
evidence: Say what the LORD promised Jehu and what Jehu failed to do (10:30-31)
Say who began to cut Israel short (10:32)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain both the promise to Jehu and where he fell short?

topics.name: Athaliah and the hidden king Joash
topics.description: After Ahaziah's death Athaliah destroys the royal seed and reigns six years; Jehosheba hides the baby Joash in the house of the LORD, and in the seventh year Jehoiada anoints him, Athaliah is put to death, and Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD, the king and the people.
evidence: Say how Joash was saved and for how long he was hidden
Say what the covenant of Jehoiada was (11:17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how young Joash became king of Judah?

topics.name: Joash repairs the temple
topics.description: Joash does right while Jehoiada instructs him, though the high places stay; when the priests have not repaired the house by his twenty-third year, a chest is placed at the altar and the money repairs it. Hazael threatens Jerusalem and Joash is killed by his servants.
evidence: Say how the temple money was collected and used (12:9-15)
Say how Joash's reign ended (12:17-21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Joash arranged the repair of the temple?

topics.name: Jehoahaz and Joash of Israel
topics.description: Jehoahaz of Israel follows Jeroboam's sins, so the LORD delivers Israel into Hazael's hand; when Jehoahaz seeks the LORD, he gives Israel a saviour, yet they do not depart from Jeroboam's sins. His son Joash reigns in the same way.
evidence: Say what happened when Jehoahaz sought the LORD (13:4-5)
Say whether Israel turned from Jeroboam's sins (13:6)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD treated Israel under Jehoahaz?

topics.name: Elisha's last word and death
topics.description: The dying Elisha has King Joash shoot an arrow of the LORD's deliverance from Syria and strike the ground; Joash strikes only three times, so Elisha says he will defeat Syria only three times. After Elisha's death a dead man touches his bones and revives; the LORD is gracious to Israel because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
evidence: Describe the arrows and why Elisha was angry (13:17-19)
Find the verse that names the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (13:23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did on his deathbed and why the LORD still showed Israel compassion?

topics.name: Amaziah of Judah
topics.description: Amaziah does right, though not like David, kills the servants who killed his father but spares their children as the law of Moses says, defeats Edom, then challenges Joash of Israel and is beaten at Beth-shemesh, with Jerusalem's wall broken and the temple treasures taken. He is later killed in a conspiracy.
evidence: Say what Amaziah did and did not do with the children of the murderers (14:5-6)
Describe the result of his challenge to Israel (14:11-14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe Amaziah's reign, including his pride in challenging Israel?

topics.name: Jeroboam II of Israel
topics.description: Jeroboam son of Joash does evil like the earlier kings, yet restores Israel's border according to the word spoken by Jonah the prophet, because the LORD saw Israel's bitter affliction and had not said he would blot out Israel's name.
evidence: Name the prophet mentioned in 14:25
Say why the LORD saved Israel by Jeroboam (14:26-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD helped Israel by Jeroboam II even though he did evil?

topics.name: Azariah and Jotham of Judah
topics.description: Azariah (Uzziah) does right, but the high places remain and the LORD smites him with leprosy until his death; his son Jotham does right in the same way. In Jotham's days the LORD begins to send Rezin of Syria and Pekah against Judah.
evidence: Say what happened to Azariah and where he lived (15:5)
Say what remained in Judah despite the kings doing right (15:4, 35)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the reigns of Azariah and Jotham?

topics.name: Israel's last kings: Zachariah to Pekah
topics.description: Zachariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah and Pekah rule Israel in quick succession, mostly by conspiracy, all doing evil; Pul of Assyria is paid off by Menahem and Tiglath-pileser takes cities and carries people captive in Pekah's days. Hoshea then kills Pekah.
evidence: Say how Zachariah's end fulfilled the word to Jehu (15:12)
Say how Assyria begins to affect Israel (15:19, 29)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Assyria began to take Israel's land and people?

topics.name: Ahaz of Judah turns to Assyria
topics.description: Ahaz walks in the way of Israel's kings, burns his son in the fire and sacrifices at the high places. Rezin and Pekah besiege Jerusalem, and Ahaz sends the temple silver and gold to Tiglath-pileser; he then copies a Damascus altar and moves the LORD's bronze altar aside.
evidence: Say who Ahaz asked for help and what he paid (16:7-8)
Describe what he did with the altar at the temple (16:10-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Ahaz did instead of trusting the LORD when Syria and Israel attacked?

topics.name: Samaria falls to Assyria
topics.description: Hoshea becomes Assyria's servant, then conspires with Egypt; Shalmaneser besieges Samaria, takes it in Hoshea's ninth year and carries Israel into Assyria.
evidence: Say what Hoshea did that led to the siege (17:4)
Say where Israel was carried (17:6)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how and when the northern kingdom of Israel was taken captive?

topics.name: Why the LORD removed Israel
topics.description: The writer explains that Israel sinned against the LORD who brought them from Egypt, walked in the nations' ways, ignored the prophets, rejected his covenant and statutes, and followed Jeroboam's sin, so the LORD removed them. Judah also did not keep his commandments.
evidence: List several sins named in 17:7-17
Say how the LORD had warned them (17:13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} give the reasons 2 Kings 17 gives for Israel's exile?

topics.name: Foreign peoples settled in Samaria
topics.description: The king of Assyria brings peoples from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath and Sepharvaim to Samaria; lions come among them until a priest taught the manner of the God of the land, but each nation keeps its own gods while also fearing the LORD.
evidence: Say how the settlers came to fear the LORD (17:25-28)
Say why the writer says they did not truly fear the LORD (17:34-41)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened in the land after Israel was taken away?

topics.name: Hezekiah trusts the LORD
topics.description: Hezekiah does right as David did, removes the high places and breaks the bronze serpent Moses made, which Israel had been burning incense to, and trusts the LORD like no king before or after him. He rebels against Assyria.
evidence: Say what Hezekiah removed and what he did to the bronze serpent (18:4)
Say what the writer says about his trust in the LORD (18:5-7)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what made Hezekiah a good king?

topics.name: Sennacherib's officer taunts Jerusalem
topics.description: Sennacherib takes Judah's fortified cities and Hezekiah pays him; the king of Assyria still sends Rabshakeh, who mocks Hezekiah's trust in the LORD and Egypt and tells the people not to listen to him, asking which gods have delivered their land.
evidence: Say what Rabshakeh told the people on the wall (18:28-35)
Say how the people responded (18:36)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Rabshakeh said to shake Judah's trust in the LORD?

topics.name: The LORD delivers Jerusalem
topics.description: Hezekiah spreads Sennacherib's letter before the LORD and prays; Isaiah says the LORD will defend the city for his own sake and David's sake, and that night the angel of the LORD strikes 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib returns to Nineveh and is killed by his sons.
evidence: Retell Hezekiah's prayer and what he asked (19:15-19)
Say what happened to the Assyrian army (19:35)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how God answered Hezekiah's prayer against Sennacherib?

topics.name: Hezekiah's illness and the Babylonian envoys
topics.description: Hezekiah is told by Isaiah he will die, prays, and the LORD adds fifteen years, giving the shadow going back ten degrees as a sign. Afterward he shows Babylon's envoys all his treasures, and Isaiah tells him all will be carried to Babylon; Hezekiah says the word is good.
evidence: Say what sign the LORD gave and what he promised (20:5-11)
Say what Isaiah foretold about Babylon (20:16-18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD did when Hezekiah was sick, and what Isaiah said about Babylon?

topics.name: Manasseh and Amon
