topics.description: Manasseh rebuilds the high places, sets altars for the host of heaven in the LORD's house, passes his son through the fire and sheds much innocent blood; the LORD announces evil on Jerusalem like Samaria's. His son Amon does the same and is killed by his servants.
evidence: List some of Manasseh's sins (21:3-6, 16)
Say what the LORD announced would happen to Jerusalem (21:12-15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Manasseh led Judah further into sin, and what the LORD announced?

topics.name: Josiah and the book of the law
topics.description: In Josiah's eighteenth year, repairs to the temple turn up the book of the law; the king tears his clothes at its words, and Huldah the prophetess says the evil will come on Jerusalem but not in Josiah's days because his heart was tender.
evidence: Say what Hilkiah found and how Josiah reacted (22:8-11)
Say what Huldah told Josiah (22:16-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened when the book of the law was found in the temple?

topics.name: Josiah renews the covenant and cleanses the land
topics.description: Josiah reads the book of the covenant to all the people and makes a covenant before the LORD to walk after him; he removes idols and high places in Judah, defiles Topheth, and at Bethel breaks Jeroboam's altar and burns bones on it according to the word of the man of God.
evidence: Say what Josiah covenanted (23:3)
Describe what he did at Bethel and which earlier prophecy it matched (23:15-18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Josiah renewed the covenant and what he removed?

topics.name: Josiah's Passover and the verdict on Judah
topics.description: Josiah commands the people to keep the Passover as written; no such Passover had been held since the judges. No king before or after turned to the LORD as he did, yet the LORD did not turn from his wrath because of Manasseh, and says he will remove Judah as he removed Israel.
evidence: Say how the Passover was different (23:22)
Say why the LORD did not turn from his wrath (23:26-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD still would not turn from his anger after Josiah's reforms?

topics.name: Josiah's death and Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim
topics.description: Josiah dies at Megiddo when Pharaoh-nechoh goes up to Assyria; Jehoahaz reigns three months and is taken to Egypt, and Pharaoh makes Eliakim king as Jehoiakim, who taxes the land to pay him.
evidence: Say how Josiah died (23:29-30)
Say who appointed Jehoiakim (23:34)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Judah's kings right after Josiah?

topics.name: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin
topics.description: Jehoiakim serves Nebuchadnezzar, then rebels, and the LORD sends bands against Judah as he said by the prophets because of Manasseh's sin; his son Jehoiachin surrenders to Babylon and Nebuchadnezzar carries off the temple treasures and about ten thousand captives. He appoints Zedekiah king.
evidence: Say why the LORD sent the invaders (24:2-4)
Say what Nebuchadnezzar took and who he made king (24:13-17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Babylon took the first captives from Judah?

topics.name: The fall of Jerusalem
topics.description: Zedekiah rebels and Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem; the city is broken up, Zedekiah is blinded after his sons are killed, and the Chaldeans burn the temple, palace and houses, break the walls and carry off the temple's bronze and the people.
evidence: Describe what happened to Zedekiah and to the temple
Say how Judah's exile is summed up (25:21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how and why Jerusalem was destroyed?

topics.name: Gedaliah and Jehoiachin's release
topics.description: Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah over the people left in Judah, but Ishmael kills him and the people flee to Egypt. The book ends with Evil-merodach lifting Jehoiachin out of prison in Babylon and giving him a daily allowance.
evidence: Say what happened to Gedaliah (25:25)
Say how the book of 2 Kings ends (25:27-30)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how 2 Kings ends and who was released from prison?

topics.name: 1 Chronicles: overview
topics.description: 1 Chronicles opens with genealogies from Adam to the returned exiles (chs. 1-9), tells of Saul's death and David's reign (chs. 10-21), and then David's preparations for the temple, the organising of Levites and officers, and the accession of Solomon (chs. 22-29).
evidence: Name the three parts: genealogies, David's reign, preparations for the temple
Say how the book begins (Adam) and ends (David's death and Solomon reigning)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline 1 Chronicles in order, from the genealogies to David's death?

topics.name: Genealogies from Adam to Israel
topics.description: 1 Chronicles 1 lists the line from Adam to Noah's sons, the nations from Japheth, Ham and Shem, the line to Abraham, Abraham's sons through Ishmael, Keturah and Isaac, and Esau's descendants and the kings of Edom.
evidence: Say whose name begins the list (1:1) and whose sons are named in 1:34
Say which sons of Isaac are traced (1:34)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say where 1 Chronicles begins its list of names and why a book of history might start there?

topics.name: The twelve sons of Israel and the line of Judah
topics.description: Chapter 2 names the twelve sons of Israel and then follows Judah in detail through Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon and Jesse to David, with other branches of Judah's families.
evidence: List the twelve sons of Israel as named in 2:1-2
Say whose name ends the main line in 2:13-15
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} follow the line from Judah to David in 1 Chronicles 2?

topics.name: David's sons and the line of the kings of Judah
topics.description: Chapter 3 lists David's sons born in Hebron and Jerusalem, then follows Solomon's line through the kings of Judah to the exile and the descendants of Jehoiachin.
evidence: Say where David's sons were born and how long he reigned in each place (3:4)
Name some of the kings in the line from Solomon (3:10-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Chronicles 3 traces from David to the exile?

topics.name: Other families of Judah and Simeon, and Jabez
topics.description: Chapter 4 lists further families of Judah and Simeon. In the middle the text singles out Jabez, honoured above his brothers, who called on the God of Israel for blessing and was granted what he asked.
evidence: Say what Jabez asked of God and the result (4:10)
Name the two tribes whose families are listed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what is said about Jabez in 1 Chronicles 4?

topics.name: Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh
topics.description: Chapter 5 explains that Reuben lost the birthright to Joseph, lists Reuben, Gad and half Manasseh east of Jordan, notes that they cried to God and were helped in battle, and says they sinned by following other gods and were carried away by Assyria.
evidence: Say what happened to Reuben's birthright (5:1-2)
Say why the eastern tribes were carried away (5:25-26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 1 Chronicles 5 says the eastern tribes were taken captive?

topics.name: The tribe of Levi: priests and singers
topics.description: Chapter 6 traces Levi through Gershon, Kohath and Merari, the line of the high priests, the Levitical towns, and the singers David set over the service of song, Heman, Asaph and Ethan.
evidence: Name the three sons of Levi (6:1)
Say what David set the singers over (6:31-32)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say who the priests and singers were according to 1 Chronicles 6?

topics.name: Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim and Asher
topics.description: Chapter 7 lists families of several tribes, noting their numbers of mighty men of valour, and ends with Asher.
evidence: Name some tribes in the chapter
Say what the writer counts for several tribes
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name some of the tribes covered in 1 Chronicles 7?

topics.name: Benjamin and the house of Saul
topics.description: Chapter 8 lists Benjamin's families, and 8:33-40 traces Saul and his sons; the same line is repeated in 9:35-44, where Saul's descendants are listed again.
evidence: Say who is named as Saul's father and sons (8:33)
Say where else the line of Saul is listed (9:35-44)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find where 1 Chronicles lists Saul's family?

topics.name: Those who lived in Jerusalem after the captivity
topics.description: Chapter 9:1-34 says all Israel was reckoned by genealogies, the people carried away to Babylon for their transgression, and lists those who first dwelt in their cities: Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants, with the porters and singers and their duties.
evidence: Say why Judah was carried to Babylon (9:1)
Name the groups who lived in Jerusalem (9:2-3)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Chronicles 9 says about the people who lived in Jerusalem?

topics.name: Saul dies at Gilboa
topics.description: The Philistines fight Israel, Saul and his sons die, and the Philistines strip Saul and fasten his head in the temple of Dagon; the men of Jabesh-gilead bury him. The text says Saul died for his transgression and for not enquiring of the LORD, and the kingdom was turned to David.
evidence: Say why the writer says Saul died (10:13-14)
Say what happened to Saul's body and who buried it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 1 Chronicles says Saul died and what happened to the kingdom?

topics.name: David is made king and takes Jerusalem
topics.description: All Israel gathers to David at Hebron and he makes a covenant with the elders before the LORD; David and Israel take Jebus (Jerusalem) from the Jebusites, Joab leading, and David dwells there; he grows greater because the LORD of hosts was with him.
evidence: Say who came to Hebron and what they said (11:1-3)
Say who went up first against the Jebusites (11:6)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how David became king over all Israel and took Jerusalem?

topics.name: David's mighty men
topics.description: The chief of David's mighty men are named with their deeds: Jashobeam, Eleazar, Abishai and Benaiah, three men who brought David water from the well of Bethlehem (which he poured out to the LORD), and a list of other valiant men.
evidence: Say what David did with the water from Bethlehem and why (11:17-19)
Name two of the mighty men
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell about David's mighty men and the water from Bethlehem?

topics.name: Those who came to David at Ziklag and Hebron
topics.description: Chapter 12 lists warriors from Benjamin, Gad, Judah, Manasseh and other tribes who joined David at Ziklag and in the wilderness, and then the tribal armies that came to Hebron with a perfect heart to make him king over all Israel.
evidence: Say what Amasai told David (12:18)
Say why the tribes came to Hebron (12:38)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how all Israel came to support David as king?

topics.name: The ark moved on a cart and Uzza dies
topics.description: David consults the leaders and all Israel to bring the ark of God from Kirjath-jearim; on the way Uzza puts out his hand to steady the ark and the LORD strikes him. David is afraid and leaves the ark with Obed-edom, whose house is blessed.
evidence: Retell what happened to Uzza
Say where the ark was left and how the LORD treated that house (13:13-14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what went wrong when David first tried to bring the ark to Jerusalem?

topics.name: David established at Jerusalem and the Philistines defeated
topics.description: Hiram of Tyre sends cedar and craftsmen to David, who perceives that the LORD has confirmed him king; the Philistines come twice, David enquires of God each time, and God tells him the second time to wait for the sound in the mulberry trees, and the Philistines are beaten.
evidence: Say what David did before each battle (14:10, 14)
Say what sign God gave David (14:15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how David knew when to attack the Philistines?

topics.name: The ark is brought up to Jerusalem
topics.description: David prepares a place for the ark and says only Levites should carry it; the Levites sanctify themselves and bear it on their shoulders with the staves, singers and instruments appointed, and the ark comes to the city of David with shouting, though Michal despises David.
evidence: Say why David said only the Levites should carry the ark (15:2, 13)
Say how the ark was carried this time (15:15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how David brought the ark up properly the second time?

topics.name: The ark in its tent and the worship appointed
topics.description: The ark is set in the tent David pitched; burnt and peace offerings are made, bread is given to all Israel, and Levites are appointed to minister before the ark and praise the LORD, with Asaph and others, while Zadok and priests serve at Gibeon.
evidence: Say what David gave to the people (16:3)
Name the Levite chief appointed to sound the cymbals (16:5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the worship David appointed once the ark was in Jerusalem?

topics.name: David's psalm of thanksgiving
topics.description: David delivers to Asaph a psalm: give thanks to the LORD, seek his face, remember his marvellous works and his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, declare his glory to the nations, for the LORD is great and above all gods, and his mercy endures for ever.
evidence: Find the lines about the covenant with Abraham and the land of Canaan (16:15-18)
Say what the psalm says about the LORD and the gods of the peoples (16:25-26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell some reasons David's psalm gives for thanking the LORD?

topics.name: The LORD's promise to David's house
topics.description: David wants to build a house for the ark but the LORD tells Nathan he will build David a house: he will raise up David's seed, who will build the LORD's house, whose throne will be established for ever and to whom the LORD will be a father. David sits before the LORD, praises him and asks that the word be established.
evidence: State what the LORD promises about David's seed and throne (17:11-14)
Say how David responds in prayer (17:16-27)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD promised David in 1 Chronicles 17 and how David responded?

topics.name: David's victories and officers
topics.description: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, Hadarezer of Zobah, the Syrians and Edom, and dedicates the spoil to the LORD; the text says the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went, and lists his officers.
evidence: Say who preserved David in battle (18:6, 13)
Say what David did with the silver and gold (18:11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} summarise David's victories in 1 Chronicles 18?

topics.name: David and Ammon
topics.description: David sends messengers to console Hanun king of Ammon, who shames them; Ammon hires Syrians and Joab and Abishai defeat them, and David then defeats Syria. In the next year Joab besieges Rabbah, and giants of the Philistines are killed.
evidence: Say how Hanun treated David's servants (19:4)
Say what Joab said to Abishai before the battle (19:13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why David went to war with Ammon?

topics.name: David numbers Israel and the plague
topics.description: Satan provokes David to number Israel, Joab objects, and David confesses his sin; God sends a plague and 70,000 fall. When the angel stands over Jerusalem, David pleads to bear the punishment, buys Ornan's threshing floor, builds an altar and the LORD answers by fire.
evidence: Say what David chose among the three punishments and why (21:13)
Say what David bought and what he did there (21:24-26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why David's census was sin and how the plague ended?

topics.name: David prepares for the temple and charges Solomon
topics.description: David declares the threshing floor the site of the LORD's house, gathers materials, and tells Solomon that though he himself shed much blood, a son of rest will build the house for the LORD's name and the LORD will establish his throne for ever; David commands the princes to help.
evidence: Say why David himself could not build the house (22:8)
State what the LORD promised about Solomon (22:9-10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Solomon, not David, was to build the house, and what David prepared?

topics.name: The Levites' duties
topics.description: Old David makes Solomon king, numbers the Levites from age twenty and above, and divides them into courses to assist the sons of Aaron, as porters, singers and in the temple service, now that the LORD has given his people rest.
evidence: Name the Levite families (23:6) and some of their duties (23:28-31)
Say why they no longer carry the tabernacle (23:25-26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the Levites were appointed to do under David?

topics.name: The divisions of the priests
topics.description: Chapter 24 lists the sons of Aaron, notes that Nadab and Abihu died childless, and divides the descendants of Eleazar and Ithamar into twenty-four courses by lot, with Zadok and Ahimelech, and lists remaining Levite heads.
evidence: Say how the courses were assigned (24:5, 31)
Name the sons of Aaron who had no children (24:2)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how David organised the priests?

topics.name: The singers of the temple
topics.description: David and the captains set apart the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun for the service of prophesying with harps, psalteries and cymbals, in twenty-four courses by lot.
evidence: Name the three families of singers (25:1)
Say how their duties were assigned (25:8)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain who the temple singers were and how they served?

topics.name: Gatekeepers and treasurers
topics.description: Chapter 26 lists the courses of the porters at the gates of the house of the LORD, the Levites over its treasuries and dedicated things, and officers and judges for outward business.
evidence: Say what the porters did (26:12-19)
Say what the treasurers kept (26:20-28)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the gatekeepers and treasurers David appointed?

topics.name: The monthly army and tribal leaders
topics.description: Chapter 27 lists the twelve divisions of 24,000 men that served the king by month, the tribal princes, David's stewards and counsellors, and notes that David did not number those under twenty because the LORD had said he would multiply Israel.
evidence: Say how the army was organised through the year (27:1)
Name the people who counselled David (27:32-34)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how David's army and officers were organised?

topics.name: David's charge to Solomon and the assembly
topics.description: David assembles Israel's leaders, says God did not let him build because he was a man of war, chose him as king for ever and Solomon as successor; he charges Solomon to know and serve God, and gives him the plans for the temple, telling him to be strong.
evidence: State what David says God chose (28:4-6) and the condition he gives (28:7-9)
Say what David gave to Solomon (28:11-19)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what David told Solomon and the leaders about the house of God?

topics.name: The offerings, David's prayer and Solomon enthroned
topics.description: David gives his own treasure for the house, the leaders give willingly, and David blesses the LORD before the assembly, saying all things come of him, and prays for Solomon. Solomon is made king a second time and sits on the LORD's throne; David dies full of days, riches and honour after reigning forty years.
evidence: Say what David says about giving (29:14-16)
Say how long David reigned (29:27) and who succeeded him
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how David and the people gave to the house of the LORD, and how the book ends?

topics.name: 2 Chronicles: overview
topics.description: 2 Chronicles tells of Solomon's wisdom and the temple (chs. 1-9), then the kings of Judah from Rehoboam to Zedekiah, with attention to temple worship, reform and returning to the LORD, ending with the exile and Cyrus's decree to rebuild the house (ch. 36).
evidence: Say that the book follows Solomon's temple and then the kings of Judah
Say how it ends (36:22-23, Cyrus of Persia)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline 2 Chronicles in order, from Solomon's temple to Cyrus's decree?

topics.name: Solomon's wisdom and wealth
topics.description: Solomon and the congregation go to the high place at Gibeon, where the LORD appears and tells him to ask; he asks for wisdom and knowledge to judge God's people and, because he did not ask for riches, God gives him wisdom, knowledge, riches, wealth and honour.
evidence: Say what Solomon asked and what God added (1:10-12)
Describe Solomon's wealth in 1:14-17
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon asked for at Gibeon and what God gave him?

topics.name: Solomon prepares to build the temple
topics.description: Solomon determines to build a house for the LORD's name, numbers workmen, and asks Huram king of Tyre for timber and a skilled craftsman; Huram answers, blessing the LORD, and sends a cunning man and the timber.
evidence: Say what Solomon asked from Huram (2:7-9)
Say how Huram responded (2:11-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon arranged workers and timber for the temple?

topics.name: Solomon builds the temple
topics.description: Solomon begins to build on Mount Moriah, where the LORD appeared to David and on the threshing floor of Ornan, in his fourth year; the house is overlaid with gold, with two cherubim in the most holy place, a veil, and two pillars named Jachin and Boaz.
evidence: Say where the temple was built (3:1)
Say what stood in the most holy house (3:10-13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe where Solomon built the temple and what was inside?

topics.name: The temple furnishings
topics.description: Solomon makes the bronze altar, the molten sea on twelve oxen, ten lavers, golden lampstands and tables, and the courts; Huram makes the bronze pieces, and everything inside is of gold.
evidence: Name some of the furnishings and what the sea was used for (4:2-6)
Say what the vessels in the temple were made of (4:7-22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name some of the temple furnishings Solomon made?

topics.name: The ark is brought in and the glory fills the house
topics.description: At the feast the priests bring the ark of the covenant into the most holy place; when the singers and trumpeters praise the LORD, saying he is good and his mercy endures for ever, a cloud fills the house and the priests cannot minister because the glory of the LORD had filled it.
evidence: Say what was in the ark (5:10)
Describe what happened when the Levites praised the LORD (5:13-14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the ark was placed in the new temple?

topics.name: Solomon blesses Israel and recalls the promise to David
topics.description: Solomon says the LORD dwells in thick darkness, blesses the congregation, and says the LORD has performed his word to David: David's son has been set on the throne and built the house, in which the ark with the LORD's covenant is placed.
evidence: Say what Solomon says the LORD promised David (6:5-9)
Say what Solomon says he has done (6:10-11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Solomon says the LORD had promised David?

topics.name: Solomon's dedication prayer
topics.description: Kneeling before the whole congregation, Solomon praises the LORD who keeps covenant and mercy, asks that the promise to David be kept, and prays for the LORD to hear and forgive when Israel sins, is defeated, is in drought, or in captivity, and when a stranger prays toward the house.
evidence: Say what Solomon asks for if Israel repents (6:24-25, 36-39)
Find the request about the throne and David (6:16-17, 42)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} summarise Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple?

topics.name: Fire from heaven and the feast of dedication
topics.description: When Solomon finishes praying, fire comes down from heaven and consumes the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD fills the house; the people bow and praise, great sacrifices are offered, and they keep the dedication for seven days.
evidence: Describe what fell from heaven and how the people responded (7:1-3)
Say how many days they kept the feast (7:8-9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened after Solomon prayed at the dedication?

topics.name: The LORD answers Solomon
topics.description: The LORD appears to Solomon by night and says that if his people humble themselves, pray, seek his face and turn from their wicked ways he will hear, forgive and heal their land; he will establish Solomon's throne as he covenanted with David, but if they forsake him he will pluck them out of the land and cast out the house.
evidence: State the condition and promise of 7:14
Say what the LORD warns will happen if they serve other gods (7:19-22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD told Solomon about humbling themselves and about forsaking him?

topics.name: Solomon's cities, worship and ships
topics.description: Solomon builds cities, sets forced labour on the remaining peoples, keeps the burnt offerings and feasts as appointed, and orders the priests and Levites as David commanded; ships brought gold from Ophir.
evidence: Say how Solomon followed David's order for the priests and Levites (8:14-15)
Say what the ships brought (8:17-18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon kept worship in order after the temple was built?

topics.name: The queen of Sheba and the end of Solomon's reign
topics.description: The queen of Sheba tests Solomon with hard questions and blesses the LORD for setting him on the throne; the chapter describes his gold, throne, ships and wisdom, and ends with his forty-year reign and burial in the city of David.
evidence: Say what the queen said about the LORD (9:8)
State how long Solomon reigned (9:30)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why the queen of Sheba came and how Solomon's reign ended?

topics.name: Israel rebels against Rehoboam
topics.description: At Shechem Israel asks Rehoboam to lighten Solomon's yoke; he rejects the old men's counsel and answers roughly, and Israel rebels against the house of David, while Rehoboam reigns over the cities of Judah. The text says the cause was of God.
evidence: Compare what the old men and the young men advised (10:7-11)
Say what Israel said when the king answered roughly (10:16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the northern tribes broke from Rehoboam?

topics.name: Rehoboam strengthens Judah
topics.description: Rehoboam gathers an army to fight Israel but obeys the word of Shemaiah and returns; he fortifies cities, and priests and Levites and those who set their hearts to seek the LORD come to Judah from Jeroboam's kingdom.
evidence: Say why Rehoboam did not fight Israel (11:2-4)
Say why the Levites came to Judah (11:13-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why Rehoboam did not go to war and why the priests and Levites came to Judah?

topics.name: Shishak and Rehoboam humbles himself
topics.description: When Rehoboam is strong he forsakes the law of the LORD, and in his fifth year Shishak of Egypt comes against Jerusalem; Shemaiah tells them the LORD has left them, and when they humble themselves the LORD grants some deliverance, though they become Shishak's servants.
evidence: Say what turned Judah to humility (12:5-7)
Say what Shishak took (12:9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Shishak came and how the LORD responded when Rehoboam humbled himself?

topics.name: Abijah defeats Jeroboam
topics.description: Abijah of Judah, standing on Mount Zemaraim, tells Jeroboam that the LORD gave the kingdom to David and his sons by a covenant of salt, that Judah has not forsaken the LORD while Israel has made golden calves; Judah cries to the LORD and Israel is defeated.
evidence: Find the phrase about the covenant of salt (13:5)
Say why Judah prevailed (13:18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Abijah said about David and why Judah won?

topics.name: Asa removes idols and defeats Zerah
topics.description: Asa does good and right in the LORD's eyes, removes altars and high places, builds fenced cities during ten years of quiet, and when Zerah the Ethiopian comes with a huge host he cries to the LORD, saying it is nothing with him to help, and the LORD smites the Ethiopians.
evidence: Say what Asa prayed before the battle (14:11)
Say what Asa removed from Judah (14:3-5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Asa prayed and what happened to Zerah's army?

topics.name: Azariah's warning and Asa's covenant
topics.description: The Spirit of God comes on Azariah, who tells Asa that the LORD is with them while they are with him; Asa removes the idols, renews the altar, and Judah enters a covenant to seek the LORD with all their heart and soul, and he removes his mother Maachah from being queen.
evidence: State Azariah's message (15:2)
Say what the covenant was and what it required (15:12-13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Azariah told Asa and what covenant Judah made?

topics.name: Asa relies on Syria and not the LORD
topics.description: In Asa's thirty-sixth year Baasha of Israel builds Ramah, and Asa takes treasures from the temple to hire Benhadad of Syria; Hanani the seer rebukes him for not relying on the LORD, and Asa imprisons him. In his illness he seeks physicians and not the LORD.
evidence: Say what Hanani told Asa (16:7-9)
Say how Asa responded to Hanani and in his disease (16:10, 12)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Asa's trust changed late in his reign?

topics.name: Jehoshaphat strengthens Judah
topics.description: Jehoshaphat walks in the first ways of David and seeks the LORD, not Baalim; the LORD establishes his kingdom, and in the third year of his reign he sends princes, Levites and priests with the book of the law to teach through Judah's cities, so that fear of the LORD falls on the nations.
evidence: Say what Jehoshaphat sent teachers to do (17:7-9)
Say what the LORD did for Jehoshaphat (17:5, 10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Jehoshaphat taught Judah the law of the LORD?

topics.name: Jehoshaphat joins Ahab and Micaiah warns
topics.description: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab and goes to Ramoth-gilead; four hundred prophets say go, but Micaiah, after saying he will speak what God says, shows a lying spirit sent into the prophets' mouths. Ahab disguises himself but is struck by a random arrow and dies, while Jehoshaphat cries out and God helps him.
evidence: Compare Micaiah with the four hundred prophets
Say how Ahab died and how Jehoshaphat was saved (18:30-34, 31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Jehoshaphat went with Ahab and what Micaiah said?

topics.name: Jehu's rebuke and Jehoshaphat's reforms
topics.description: Jehu the seer rebukes Jehoshaphat for helping the ungodly yet notes the good in him; Jehoshaphat goes among the people turning them back to the LORD and sets judges in the fenced cities and in Jerusalem, telling them to judge for the LORD and fear him.
evidence: Say what Jehoshaphat told the judges (19:6-7)
Say what Jehu the seer said was good in him (19:3)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Jehoshaphat set up judges and what he told them?

topics.name: The LORD fights for Judah against Moab and Ammon
topics.description: A great multitude of Moab, Ammon and Mount Seir comes against Jehoshaphat, who proclaims a fast and prays that they have no might and their eyes are on God; Jahaziel says the battle is not theirs but God's, singers go before the army, and the LORD sets the enemy against each other.
evidence: Quote the way Jahaziel describes the battle (20:15)
Describe how Judah went out to battle (20:20-22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Judah won the battle against Moab and Ammon without fighting?

topics.name: The end of Jehoshaphat's reign
topics.description: Jehoshaphat walks in Asa's way, though the high places remain; he joins Ahaziah of Israel to build ships at Ezion-geber and Eliezer prophesies that the LORD has broken his works, and the ships do not sail.
evidence: Say what remained despite his good reign (20:33)
Say why the ships were broken (20:37)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why Jehoshaphat's ships were broken?

topics.name: Jehoram of Judah
topics.description: Jehoram kills his brothers, walks as the house of Ahab did (for Ahab's daughter is his wife), yet the LORD does not destroy David's house because of his covenant with David. Elijah writes warning of plague and a disease of his bowels, and Jehoram dies of it.
evidence: Say why the LORD did not destroy David's house (21:7)
Say what Elijah's writing announced (21:12-15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why God spared the house of David despite Jehoram?

topics.name: Ahaziah, Athaliah and the hidden Joash
topics.description: Ahaziah of Judah follows the counsel of Ahab's house and is killed with Joram of Israel by Jehu; Athaliah destroys the royal seed but Jehoshabeath hides the baby Joash in the house of God for six years.
evidence: Say who walked with Ahaziah and what happened to him (22:3-9)
Say who saved Joash and where he was hidden (22:11-12)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Joash escaped Athaliah?

topics.name: Jehoiada crowns Joash and Athaliah is slain
topics.description: In the seventh year Jehoiada makes a covenant with the captains, brings out the king's son in the temple with guards and Levites, anoints him, and Athaliah is put to death; Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD, the people and the king, and the house of Baal is destroyed.
evidence: Say how Joash was crowned and who protected him (23:1-11)
State what the king's son reigning is said to fulfil (23:3)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell how Joash became king and how the people renewed their covenant?

topics.name: Joash repairs the temple, then turns away
topics.description: Joash repairs the house of the LORD with money collected in a chest, but after Jehoiada dies the princes lead him to serve idols; when Zechariah the priest warns them, Joash has him stoned in the temple court, and Joash is later struck down by Syrians and conspirators.
evidence: Say how the temple was repaired (24:8-14)
Say what Joash did after Jehoiada's death (24:17-22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Joash did well while Jehoiada lived and what changed after he died?

topics.name: Amaziah of Judah
topics.description: Amaziah obeys the law about not killing children for fathers' sins, sends away hired Israelite troops at a prophet's word and defeats Edom, but then brings home Edom's gods and worships them. He ignores the prophet, challenges Joash of Israel and loses at Beth-shemesh, and is later killed in a conspiracy.
evidence: Say what Amaziah did after defeating Edom (25:14)
Say why God was angry and what resulted (25:15-24)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Amaziah went from obeying the LORD to worshipping idols?

topics.name: Uzziah's strength and pride
topics.description: Uzziah seeks God while Zechariah teaches him, and God makes him prosper with victories, buildings and an army; when he is strong his heart is lifted up, he enters the temple to burn incense, and the LORD strikes him with leprosy until his death.
evidence: Say what led to Uzziah's success (26:5)
Say what he did to bring leprosy on himself (26:16-21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Uzziah when he became strong?

topics.name: Jotham of Judah
topics.description: Jotham does right as Uzziah did, but does not enter the temple; he builds in Jerusalem and Judah, conquers Ammon, and becomes mighty because he prepared his ways before the LORD.
evidence: Say why Jotham became mighty (27:6)
Name something he built or won
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what made Jotham a strong king?

topics.name: Ahaz and Judah's defeat
topics.description: Ahaz walks in the ways of Israel's kings, makes images for Baalim and burns his children; the LORD delivers him to Syria and Israel, where Pekah kills many in Judah in one day. In his distress he sends to Assyria, who does not help, and he closes the temple and sets up altars everywhere.
evidence: List what Ahaz did instead of seeking the LORD (28:2-4, 22-25)
Say what happened when he turned to Assyria (28:20-21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Ahaz responded to his troubles and what happened?

topics.name: Oded and the captives sent home
topics.description: When Israel brings home 200,000 captives from Judah, the prophet Oded meets the army and says they also have sins and must send them back; some Ephraimite leaders agree, and clothe, feed and carry the captives to Jericho.
evidence: Say what Oded told the army (28:9-11)
Describe how the leaders cared for the captives (28:15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Israelites showed kindness to the captives from Judah?

topics.name: Hezekiah cleanses and reopens the temple
topics.description: Hezekiah reopens the doors of the LORD's house in his first year, calls the priests and Levites to sanctify it and carry out the filth, and says he intends to make a covenant with the LORD; sin offerings are made for the kingdom and the sanctuary, and worship with singing and instruments resumes.
evidence: Say what Hezekiah told the Levites (29:5-11)
Describe how worship was restored (29:25-30)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Hezekiah restored worship in the temple?

topics.name: Hezekiah's Passover
topics.description: Hezekiah sends letters to all Israel and Judah, including Ephraim and Manasseh, to come to Jerusalem and keep the Passover to the LORD, in the second month; some mock but many humble themselves and come, and the people keep the feast with great joy for fourteen days. Hezekiah prays for those who were not cleansed and the LORD heals the people.
evidence: Say whom Hezekiah invited (30:1-9)
Say what Hezekiah prayed for the uncleansed (30:18-20)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Hezekiah invited all Israel to the Passover and how the people responded?

topics.name: Hezekiah organises the offerings and priests
topics.description: After the Passover Israel breaks down the idols, Hezekiah appoints the priests and Levites to their courses, and the people bring tithes and firstfruits in abundance; storerooms are prepared and men are appointed to distribute. The text says Hezekiah did this with all his heart and prospered.
evidence: Say what the people brought (31:5-6)
Say how Hezekiah served God according to 31:20-21
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Hezekiah arranged for the support of the priests and Levites?

topics.name: Sennacherib threatens and the LORD delivers Jerusalem
topics.description: Sennacherib invades Judah; Hezekiah strengthens Jerusalem and tells the people there is more with them than with the king of Assyria. Sennacherib's servants mock the LORD, Hezekiah and Isaiah pray, and the LORD sends an angel to cut off the Assyrian leaders; Sennacherib goes home and his sons kill him.
evidence: Say what Hezekiah told the people (32:7-8)
Say what the LORD did after Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed (32:20-22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed when Sennacherib threatened Jerusalem, and what God did?

topics.name: Hezekiah's illness, pride and death
topics.description: Hezekiah is sick to death and prays and is given a sign, but his heart is lifted up and wrath falls on Judah until he and Jerusalem humble themselves. He prospers, stops the upper watercourse of Gihon, and when envoys come from Babylon God leaves him to test what was in his heart; he dies and is honoured in burial.
evidence: Say what happened because of Hezekiah's pride and how it was turned aside (32:25-26)
Name something Hezekiah built for Jerusalem (32:30)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Hezekiah's heart was tested and what the LORD did?

topics.name: Manasseh's repentance and Amon
topics.description: Manasseh rebuilds the high places and sets idols in the house of God; the LORD brings Assyria's captains, who take him in fetters to Babylon, and there he humbles himself, prays and is restored to Jerusalem, where he removes the idols and repairs the altar. His son Amon does evil and does not humble himself, and is killed by his servants.
evidence: Say what happened to Manasseh in affliction and what he did after returning (33:11-16)
Say how Amon differed from his father (33:23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Manasseh turned back to the LORD and how Amon was different?

topics.name: Josiah seeks God and purges the land
topics.description: Josiah begins to seek the God of David in his eighth year, and in his twelfth year purges Judah and Jerusalem of high places, groves and images, and also in Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon and Naphtali; in his eighteenth year he sends Shaphan and others to repair the house of the LORD.
evidence: Say when Josiah began to seek God and when he began to purge (34:3)
Say who oversaw the temple repair (34:8-13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Josiah did in the early years of his reign?

topics.name: The book of the law found and the covenant renewed
topics.description: Hilkiah finds the book of the law in the temple; Josiah tears his clothes, sends to Huldah the prophetess, who says the evil will come but not in his days because he humbled himself. Josiah reads the book to all the people and makes a covenant before the LORD to keep his commandments.
evidence: Say what Josiah did when the book was read (34:19)
Say what Huldah told him and what covenant he made (34:23-31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the book of the law was found and what Josiah did next?

topics.name: Josiah's Passover
topics.description: Josiah keeps the Passover in Jerusalem on the fourteenth of the first month, appointing priests and Levites to their duties, giving offerings to the people, with the singers in their places as David commanded; no Passover like it had been kept in Israel since Samuel.
evidence: Say how Josiah organised the Levites and priests (35:2-6)
Say how this Passover compared to earlier ones (35:18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe Josiah's Passover and what made it special?

topics.name: Josiah dies at Megiddo
topics.description: Pharaoh Necho goes up to fight at Carchemish and warns Josiah not to meddle, saying God commanded him; Josiah does not heed and goes out to fight at Megiddo, where archers wound him, and he dies; all Judah mourns, and Jeremiah laments for him.
evidence: Say what Necho told Josiah (35:21)
Say what Josiah did and what happened (35:22-24)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Josiah died and who mourned for him?

topics.name: Judah's last kings
topics.description: Jehoahaz is deposed by the king of Egypt, Jehoiakim is bound by Nebuchadnezzar and temple vessels are taken to Babylon; Jehoiachin is taken to Babylon, and Zedekiah rebels, hardens his heart, and with the priests and people pollutes the house of the LORD.
evidence: Say what Nebuchadnezzar took to Babylon (36:7, 10)
Say how Zedekiah and the people sinned (36:12-14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name Judah's last kings in order and say what happened to each?

topics.name: The LORD sends Judah into exile
topics.description: The LORD sent messengers to his people because of his compassion, but they mocked the prophets until there was no remedy; the Chaldeans burn the house of God, break down Jerusalem's wall, and carry the survivors to Babylon until the land enjoyed its sabbaths, seventy years, as Jeremiah spoke.
evidence: Say why the LORD sent the messengers and how they were treated (36:15-16)
Say what the seventy years were to fulfil (36:21)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Judah went into exile according to 2 Chronicles 36?

topics.name: Cyrus's decree
topics.description: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia the LORD stirs up his spirit to proclaim that the LORD God of heaven has charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and invites any of his people to go up.
evidence: Say whose spirit the LORD stirred up and what he proclaimed
Say how 2 Chronicles ends
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how 2 Chronicles closes and what Cyrus announced?

topics.name: Ezra: overview
topics.description: Ezra reports the return from Babylon under Cyrus and Zerubbabel and the rebuilding of the temple despite opposition (chs. 1-6), then Ezra's own journey to Jerusalem, his prayer over intermarriage, and the people's covenant to put away foreign wives (chs. 7-10).
evidence: Name the two parts: the return and temple under Zerubbabel, and Ezra's mission
Say how the book begins (Cyrus) and ends (the list of those with foreign wives)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline Ezra, from Cyrus's decree to the people's confession?

topics.name: Cyrus's decree and the first return
topics.description: In the first year of Cyrus the LORD stirs his spirit, and he proclaims that the LORD God of heaven charged him to build a house in Jerusalem and invites any of God's people to go up. Those whose spirit God raised go, neighbours help them, and Cyrus brings out the temple vessels to Sheshbazzar.
evidence: Say whose word was being fulfilled (1:1)
Say what Cyrus returned to Sheshbazzar (1:7-11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Cyrus decreed and who went up to Jerusalem?

topics.name: The list of those who returned
topics.description: Chapter 2 lists those who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua by family and town, then priests, Levites, singers, porters and temple servants, notes some who could not prove their ancestry, and gives the total and the freewill gifts for the house.
evidence: Say who led the group (2:2)
Say what some of the chief fathers gave (2:68-69)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Ezra records the names and numbers of the returnees?

topics.name: The altar is rebuilt and worship begins
topics.description: In the seventh month the people gather at Jerusalem; Jeshua and Zerubbabel build the altar of the God of Israel, offer burnt offerings morning and evening as written in the law of Moses, and keep the feast of tabernacles, although fear was on them because of the people of the lands.
evidence: Say what they built first and why (3:2-3)
Name the feast they kept (3:4)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the returned exiles began by building the altar?

topics.name: The foundation of the temple is laid
topics.description: In the second year the builders lay the foundation, with priests and Levites praising the LORD according to David's order; the people shout for joy, while many old men who had seen the first house weep, so that joy and weeping cannot be told apart.
evidence: Describe what the people sang (3:11)
Say why some of the old men wept (3:12)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why some people shouted for joy and some wept when the foundation was laid?

topics.name: The adversaries offer to help and then oppose
topics.description: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin ask to build with Zerubbabel, claiming they seek his God; Zerubbabel and Jeshua refuse, saying they must build alone as Cyrus commanded, and the people of the land weaken their hands and hire counsellors against them.
evidence: Say what the adversaries asked and what the leaders answered (4:2-3)
Say how they opposed the work (4:4-5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Zerubbabel refused the offer to help build the temple?

topics.name: Letters to the king and the work stops
topics.description: Later accusations are written against Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes; Rehum and Shimshai write to Artaxerxes that Jerusalem is a rebellious city, and the king orders the work stopped. The work on the house of God ceases until the second year of Darius.
evidence: Say what the letter claimed about Jerusalem (4:12-16)
Say how long the work ceased (4:24)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the rebuilding was stopped and for how long?

topics.name: Haggai and Zechariah and the resumed work
topics.description: Haggai and Zechariah prophesy to the Jews in the name of the God of Israel, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua rise and begin to build again; when Tatnai the governor asks who commanded it, the text says the eye of their God was on the elders.
evidence: Name the prophets and the leaders who began again (5:1-2)
Say what kept the work going when Tatnai questioned them (5:5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain who encouraged the Jews to start building again?

topics.name: Tatnai writes to Darius
topics.description: Tatnai and his companions write to Darius reporting that the Jews are building the house of the great God, say they build as servants of the God of heaven and earth by Cyrus's decree, and ask the king to search the records.
evidence: Say what the elders said about who commanded the building (5:11-16)
Say what Tatnai asked Darius to do (5:17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the Jewish elders told Tatnai about Cyrus's decree?

topics.name: Darius finds Cyrus's decree
topics.description: A search in the house of the rolls finds Cyrus's decree about the house of God in Jerusalem; Darius orders Tatnai to let the work alone, give costs from the royal revenue, supply offerings, and punish anyone who changes the decree.
evidence: Say where the decree of Cyrus was found (6:1-2)
State what Darius commanded (6:6-12)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the opposition to building the temple was ended?

topics.name: The temple is finished and dedicated
topics.description: Tatnai carries out the decree, and the elders of the Jews build and prosper through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah; the house is finished on the third of Adar in Darius's sixth year, dedicated with joy, and the Passover is kept.
evidence: Say when the house was finished (6:15)
Say what they kept after the dedication (6:19-22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the second temple was completed and celebrated?

topics.name: Ezra the scribe goes up to Jerusalem
topics.description: In the reign of Artaxerxes, Ezra, a priest of the line of Aaron and a ready scribe in the law of Moses, goes up from Babylon with a company because the good hand of God was on him; the text says he prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, to do it, and to teach in Israel.
evidence: Say what Ezra had prepared his heart to do (7:10)
Say what is said about the hand of God on him (7:6, 9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain who Ezra was and why he went to Jerusalem?

topics.name: Artaxerxes' letter and Ezra's blessing
topics.description: Artaxerxes' letter lets Ezra take volunteers, silver and gold and vessels to Jerusalem, orders treasurers to supply him, and tells Ezra to appoint judges to teach and enforce the law of God. Ezra blesses the LORD who put this in the king's heart.
evidence: Say what the king authorised Ezra to do (7:13-26)
Say how Ezra responded (7:27-28)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what the king's letter gave Ezra and how Ezra responded?

topics.name: The family heads who went up with Ezra
topics.description: Ezra 8:1-14 lists the chief fathers and the number of men who went up with Ezra in the reign of Artaxerxes, by family.
evidence: Say what the list records
Name at least one family that went up
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Ezra 8:1-14 records?

topics.name: Fasting at the river Ahava
topics.description: At the river Ahava Ezra finds no Levites and sends for some; he proclaims a fast to seek a right way, being ashamed to ask the king for soldiers after saying God's hand is for good on those who seek him. They entrust the silver, gold and vessels to twelve priests, travel safely, and deliver the treasure in Jerusalem.
evidence: Say why Ezra did not ask for soldiers (8:22)
Say how God answered the fast (8:23, 31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Ezra fasted instead of asking for an escort?

topics.name: Intermarriage reported to Ezra
topics.description: The princes tell Ezra that the people, priests and Levites have not separated from the peoples of the lands and have taken their daughters as wives, the princes and rulers being chief in this trespass; Ezra tears his garment and hair and sits appalled.
evidence: Say what the princes reported (9:1-2)
Say how Ezra reacted (9:3)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the people had done that grieved Ezra?

topics.name: Ezra's confession
topics.description: At the evening sacrifice Ezra falls on his knees and confesses the people's guilt from their fathers' days, remembers the mercy shown in giving a remnant and a little reviving, and says they have again broken God's commandments, and that the LORD is righteous.
evidence: Say what mercy Ezra recalls (9:8-9)
Say how Ezra ends the prayer (9:15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} summarise how Ezra prayed over the people's sin?

topics.name: The people covenant to put away foreign wives
topics.description: As Ezra weeps before the house of God a great congregation weeps with him; Shechaniah says there is hope in Israel and proposes making a covenant to put away the foreign wives according to the law. Ezra has the leaders swear and a gathering is held in Jerusalem, where the people confess and agree to separate.
evidence: Say what Shechaniah proposed (10:2-4)
Say how the matter was carried out (10:7-17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what the people agreed to do after Ezra's prayer?

topics.name: The names of those with foreign wives
topics.description: Ezra 10:18-44 lists priests, Levites, singers, porters and other Israelites who had taken foreign wives, with a ram of the flock as guilt offering from the priests, and ends by noting that some had children by these wives.
evidence: Say what the priests offered (10:19)
Say how the book of Ezra ends (10:44)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Ezra 10:18-44 records and how the book closes?

topics.name: Nehemiah: overview
topics.description: Nehemiah, cupbearer to Artaxerxes, prays and returns to Jerusalem to rebuild its wall in fifty-two days despite opposition (chs. 1-7), then the law is read, the feast of booths is kept, the people confess and covenant (chs. 8-10), and the city is repopulated, the wall dedicated and abuses corrected (chs. 11-13).
evidence: Name the main parts: building the wall, reading the law and covenant, dedication and reforms
Say who Nehemiah was and what he did for Jerusalem
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline Nehemiah, from the prayer in Susa to the reforms at the end?

topics.name: Nehemiah hears about Jerusalem and prays
topics.description: Nehemiah, in Shushan in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes, hears from Hanani that the remnant in Judah is in affliction and Jerusalem's wall is broken down; he weeps, fasts and prays, confessing sin, recalling the LORD's word to Moses about scattering and gathering, and asks for mercy before the king.
evidence: Say what Nehemiah learned and how he responded (1:3-4)
Say what promise to Moses he recalls (1:8-9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Nehemiah responded when he heard about Jerusalem and what he prayed?

topics.name: The king grants Nehemiah's request
topics.description: Months later Nehemiah, as cupbearer, is asked by Artaxerxes why he is sad; after a quick prayer he asks to be sent to rebuild Jerusalem, and the king grants letters and timber, the good hand of God being on him.
evidence: Say what Nehemiah did before answering the king (2:4)
Say what the king gave him (2:7-9)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Nehemiah got permission to go to Jerusalem?

topics.name: Nehemiah inspects the wall and rallies the people
topics.description: After three days in Jerusalem Nehemiah rides out by night to view the broken wall, then tells the officials of God's good hand and the king's words, and the people say, Let us rise up and build; Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem mock them.
evidence: Say what Nehemiah did first and why he did it by night (2:12-15)
Say how the people and the enemies responded (2:18-19)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Nehemiah got the people ready to build the wall?

topics.name: Who built the wall
topics.description: Chapter 3 names the priests, families, officials and guilds who repaired each section and gate of Jerusalem's wall, from the Sheep Gate around to the Sheep Gate again.
evidence: Name the first gate mentioned and the people who built it (3:1)
Say how the work was shared
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Nehemiah 3 lists so many builders?

topics.name: Opposition and a weapon in every builder's hand
topics.description: Sanballat and Tobiah mock the builders; Nehemiah prays and sets a guard when they plot to attack, tells the people to remember the LORD and fight for their families, and from then half the men work and half hold spears, each builder with a sword, trusting that God will fight for them.
evidence: Say how Nehemiah responded to mockery and threat (4:4, 9, 14)
Describe how the work went on under threat (4:16-18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the builders kept working while their enemies threatened them?

topics.name: Nehemiah stops oppression among the Jews
topics.description: The poor cry out that they have mortgaged lands and sold children into bondage to their own brethren during a famine; Nehemiah rebukes the nobles for exacting usury and they promise to restore what was taken, while he reports that he and his brethren did not take the governor's food allowance because of the fear of God.
evidence: Say what the poor complained of (5:2-5)
Say why Nehemiah did not take the governor's bread (5:14-15)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what was wrong when the nobles took usury and what Nehemiah did?

topics.name: Plots against Nehemiah and the wall is finished
topics.description: Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem try to lure Nehemiah away, send an open letter accusing him of rebellion, and hire Shemaiah to frighten him into the temple; Nehemiah refuses, prays, and the wall is finished on the twenty-fifth of Elul in fifty-two days, so that the nations' confidence fails because the work was of God.
evidence: Say what Nehemiah answered when invited to meet (6:3)
Say how long the wall took and what the enemies concluded (6:15-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Nehemiah resisted his enemies' schemes and how the wall was finished?

topics.name: Guarding Jerusalem and the register of the first returnees
topics.description: With the wall built and doors set up, Nehemiah puts Hanani and Hananiah in charge of Jerusalem and sets watches at the gates; the city is large but its people few, so God puts it in Nehemiah's heart to gather the people by genealogy, and he finds the register of those who came up first, which is read out.
evidence: Say who was put in charge and how the gates were guarded (7:1-3)
Say what record Nehemiah found (7:5)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Nehemiah looked for the register of the first returnees?

topics.name: Ezra reads the law and the people weep
topics.description: On the first day of the seventh month all the people gather at the water gate; Ezra reads the law from morning until midday, the Levites explain it so the people understand, and when they weep Nehemiah, Ezra and the Levites tell them to rejoice because the joy of the LORD is their strength.
evidence: Describe how the law was read and explained (8:3-8)
Say what the leaders told the people when they wept (8:9-10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened when Ezra read the book of the law to the people?

topics.name: The feast of booths is kept
topics.description: On the second day the leaders study the law and find that Israel should dwell in booths in the seventh month; the people make booths of branches and keep the feast with very great gladness, as had not been done since the days of Joshua, with daily reading from the law.
evidence: Say what the law said about the feast (8:14-15)
Say how long they kept the feast and what they heard (8:17-18)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how the people kept the feast of booths in Nehemiah's day?

topics.name: The people fast and confess
topics.description: On the twenty-fourth day Israel assembles with fasting, sackcloth and earth, separates from foreigners, stands and confesses their sins and their fathers' iniquities, reads the law a quarter of the day and worships; the Levites call on them to bless the LORD.
evidence: Say how the people showed their repentance (9:1-2)
Say how the time was spent (9:3)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Israel gathered to confess their sins in Nehemiah 9?

topics.name: The Levites' prayer retelling Israel's story
topics.description: The prayer blesses the LORD as creator, recalls his choice of Abram and his covenant to give the land to his seed, the exodus, Sinai, manna and water, the golden calf, the conquest, the cycle of rebellion and rescue under judges, the prophets' warnings, and ends by asking for mercy in their present distress; the people write a sure covenant.
evidence: Find the lines about the covenant with Abraham (9:7-8)
Say how the prayer describes God's patience and the people's repeated rebellion (9:16-31)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline Israel's history as told in the Levites' prayer and say what it asks for?

topics.name: The sure covenant is sealed
topics.description: The leaders, priests and Levites seal the covenant, and the rest of the people swear to walk in God's law, to avoid intermarriage with the peoples of the land, to keep the sabbath and seventh year, and to support the temple with a yearly charge, wood, firstfruits and tithes, saying "we will not forsake the house of our God".
evidence: List some commitments the people made (10:28-39)
Say what they promised about the house of God (10:39)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list what the people promised in the covenant in Nehemiah 10?

topics.name: Who lived in Jerusalem
topics.description: The rulers dwell in Jerusalem and the people cast lots so that one in ten will live there, and the people bless those who volunteer; the chapter lists the Judah and Benjamin families, priests, Levites and others in Jerusalem and the towns elsewhere.
evidence: Say how people were chosen to live in Jerusalem (11:1-2)
Say who was among the residents
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Jerusalem was filled with people after the wall was built?

topics.name: Priests and Levites from Zerubbabel's time
topics.description: Chapter 12:1-26 lists the priests and Levites who went up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua and their successors, noting Jeshua, Joiakim, Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and Jaddua as the line of high priests, and the Levites chief of the fathers.
evidence: Name some priests who went up with Zerubbabel (12:1-7)
Say what the list records about later priests (12:10-11, 22-23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Nehemiah 12:1-26 records?

topics.name: The dedication of the wall
topics.description: The Levites are sought out to keep the dedication with gladness and singing; Nehemiah brings the princes up on the wall and appoints two great thanksgiving companies that go in procession and meet at the house of God, where great sacrifices are offered and the joy of Jerusalem is heard afar off, and the services and storehouses are organised.
evidence: Describe the two companies on the wall (12:31-40)
Say what was heard afar off (12:43)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated?

topics.name: Separation from foreigners and Tobiah's chamber
topics.description: When the book of Moses is read, the people separate the mixed multitude after finding that Ammonites and Moabites were not to enter the congregation; on a later return from the king Nehemiah finds that Eliashib gave Tobiah a chamber in the temple and he throws Tobiah's goods out, cleanses the chamber, and restores the Levites' portions.
evidence: Say what the law said that led to the separation (13:1-3)
Say what Nehemiah did about Tobiah and the Levites (13:7-13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Nehemiah did about Tobiah's room in the temple?

topics.name: Sabbath breaking and mixed marriages
topics.description: Nehemiah rebukes the nobles for trading on the sabbath, orders the gates shut at sunset, and warns the merchants; he also contends with Jews who married women of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, citing Solomon's sin, and drives away a son of the high priest who was son-in-law to Sanballat. He ends by asking God to remember him for good.
evidence: Say what Nehemiah did to guard the sabbath (13:19-22)
Say what example he used against mixed marriages (13:26)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Nehemiah dealt with the sabbath and with mixed marriages?

topics.name: Esther: overview
topics.description: Esther tells how a Jewish orphan becomes queen of Persia, Haman plots to destroy the Jews, Esther and Mordecai act, the plot is reversed, and the feast of Purim is established. The name of God does not appear in the book.
evidence: Say who the main people are: Ahasuerus, Esther, Mordecai and Haman
Say what the feast of Purim remembers
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline the book of Esther from Vashti's removal to the feast of Purim?

topics.name: Queen Vashti refuses the king
topics.description: Ahasuerus holds a great feast in Shushan; when he commands Queen Vashti to appear before the guests she refuses, and on the advice of Memucan she is removed and a decree goes out in the king's name that every man should rule in his own house.
evidence: Say what Vashti refused to do and what followed (1:10-19)
Say how the king proclaimed the decree (1:20-22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell why Vashti lost her place as queen?

topics.name: Esther becomes queen
topics.description: The king's servants gather beautiful young women to Shushan; Mordecai, a Benjamite carried away with Jeconiah, has raised his cousin Hadassah (Esther), who finds favour, is made queen in Vashti's place, and keeps her people secret at Mordecai's charge.
evidence: Say who Mordecai was and how he was related to Esther (2:5-7)
Say what Mordecai told her not to reveal (2:10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Esther came to be queen and what she kept secret?

topics.name: Mordecai exposes a plot
topics.description: Mordecai sits in the king's gate and learns that two chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, plan to kill the king; he tells Esther, who tells the king in Mordecai's name, and the matter is written in the book of the chronicles.
evidence: Say who was plotting and how the king learned of it (2:21-22)
Say where it was recorded (2:23)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Mordecai saved the king's life?

topics.name: Haman plots to destroy the Jews
topics.description: King Ahasuerus promotes Haman the Agagite, and when Mordecai will not bow to him Haman seeks to destroy all the Jews in the kingdom; lots are cast, he offers the king silver, and the king gives him his ring so a decree is sent to all the provinces that the Jews be destroyed on a set day.
evidence: Say why Haman wanted to destroy the Jews (3:5-6)
Say what the king did and what the decree ordered (3:10-13)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Haman wanted to destroy the Jews and what he persuaded the king to do?

topics.name: Mordecai's plea and Esther's decision
topics.description: The Jews mourn the decree; Mordecai tells Esther through Hatach to go to the king, saying deliverance will arise from another place and asking who knows whether she came to the kingdom for such a time as this. Esther asks the Jews to fast three days and says she will go in to the king, and if she perishes, she perishes.
evidence: Say what Mordecai asked Esther to do (4:8, 13-14)
Say what Esther decided (4:15-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what Mordecai asked Esther to do and how she answered?

topics.name: Esther's banquets and Haman's gallows
topics.description: Esther stands in the inner court and the king holds out his sceptre to her; at her banquet she asks that the king and Haman come again the next day. Haman, angered by Mordecai, accepts his wife's advice and has a high gallows made for him.
evidence: Say what the king did when Esther came uninvited (5:2)
Say what Haman prepared for Mordecai (5:14)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened when Esther went to the king and what Haman planned?

topics.name: The king honours Mordecai
topics.description: The king cannot sleep and has the records read; he learns Mordecai was never rewarded and asks Haman what to do for the man the king delights to honour, and Haman, thinking it is himself, describes royal robes and a horse; he is made to lead Mordecai through the city.
evidence: Say what the king learned from the records (6:1-3)
Describe what Haman had to do for Mordecai (6:10-11)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Haman ended up honouring Mordecai?

topics.name: Esther reveals Haman
topics.description: At the second banquet Esther asks the king for her life and her people, who have been sold to be destroyed, and names Haman as the enemy; the king in his wrath has Haman hanged on the gallows Haman prepared for Mordecai.
evidence: Say what Esther asked and whom she named (7:3-6)
Say how Haman died (7:9-10)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell how Esther revealed Haman's plot to the king?

topics.name: The king's second decree
topics.description: The king gives Haman's house to Esther and Mordecai his ring; Esther begs him to reverse Haman's letters, and since a decree cannot be revoked he permits Mordecai to write a new decree allowing the Jews to gather and defend their lives on the appointed day. Mordecai goes out in royal apparel and there is joy among the Jews.
evidence: Say what the new decree allowed (8:11)
Say how the Jews responded (8:15-17)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the king made a way for the Jews to defend themselves?

topics.name: The Jews are delivered
topics.description: On the thirteenth of Adar the Jews gather and overcome those who hated them; the rulers help them for fear of Mordecai, Haman's ten sons are killed, and in Shushan they have a second day, but the text repeats that they did not take the spoil. They rest and feast on the fourteenth.
evidence: Say what happened on the thirteenth of Adar (9:1-5)
Say what the text notes about the spoil (9:10, 15-16)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened on the day the Jews' enemies expected to destroy them?

topics.name: The feast of Purim is established
topics.description: Mordecai writes to the Jews in all the provinces to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar yearly as days of feasting, gladness, sending portions and gifts to the poor; they are called Purim after Pur, the lot Haman cast, and Esther and Mordecai confirm it.
evidence: Say why the feast is called Purim (9:24-26)
List what the Jews were to do on these days (9:22)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Purim remembers and how it is kept?

topics.name: Mordecai's greatness
topics.description: King Ahasuerus lays a tribute on the land and the sea; the book ends by saying Mordecai the Jew was next to the king, great among the Jews, seeking the wealth of his people and speaking peace to all his seed.
evidence: Say how Mordecai is described (10:3)
Say whose welfare he sought
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how the book of Esther ends and how it describes Mordecai?

topics.name: Job: overview
topics.description: Job opens with a righteous man losing everything (1-2), moves through his lament and long exchanges with three friends (3-31), Elihu (32-37) and the LORD answering from the whirlwind (38-41), and ends with Job’s repentance and restoration (42).
evidence: Outline the book of Job in its main parts: prologue, speeches, the LORD’s answer, epilogue.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} outline the book of Job in four or five parts and name who speaks in each?

topics.name: Job’s integrity and the loss of everything
topics.description: Job is described as blameless and God-fearing and is very rich; the LORD allows Satan to take his possessions and children, and Job worships, saying the LORD gave and the LORD has taken away.
evidence: Retell what Job lost in chapter 1 and how he responded (1:20-22).
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} retell what happened to Job in chapter 1 and what he said when he heard the news?

topics.name: Job’s sores and his friends’ silence
topics.description: Satan is allowed to strike Job’s body with sore boils, his wife tells him to curse God and die, Job refuses, and three friends come and sit with him seven days without speaking.
evidence: Explain how Job answers his wife in 2:9-10 and what the three friends do in 2:11-13.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Job says to his wife and what his three friends do when they arrive?

topics.name: Job laments the day of his birth
topics.description: Job breaks the silence by cursing the day he was born and asking why light is given to those in misery who long for death.
evidence: Summarize Job’s complaint in chapter 3 and name what he wishes had happened (3:11-13).
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Job speaks in chapter 3 and how it differs from his words in chapters 1-2?

topics.name: Eliphaz’s first speech
topics.description: Eliphaz says the innocent do not perish and those who sow wickedness reap it, tells of a night vision asking whether mortal man can be more just than God, and urges Job to seek God and not despise his correction.
evidence: Identify Eliphaz’s argument in 4:7-8 and his advice in 5:8 and 5:17.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} state Eliphaz’s main argument to Job in chapters 4-5?

topics.name: Job answers: my grief is heavy, my friends fail me
topics.description: Job says his grief outweighs the sand of the sea, compares his friends to a stream that fails in summer, and cries that his days are hopeless and short, asking God why he is watched so closely.
evidence: Find the image Job uses for his friends in 6:15-20.
Describe how Job speaks to God in 7:11-21.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Job answers Eliphaz in chapters 6-7 and what he asks of God?

topics.name: Bildad’s first speech
topics.description: Bildad asks whether God perverts justice, suggests Job’s children sinned, and says that if Job is pure God will restore him while the hope of the godless perishes.
evidence: Note Bildad’s questions in 8:3 and the promise in 8:20-21.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Bildad says about God’s justice and what he thinks it means for Job?

topics.name: How can a man be right with God? Job longs for a mediator
topics.description: Job agrees that a man cannot contend with a God of great power, laments that there is no daysman between them to lay a hand on both, and in chapter 10 pleads with God to show why he contends with him, recalling that God made him.
evidence: Find Job’s question in 9:2 and his wish in 9:33.
List what Job says about being made by God in 10:8-12.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Job means by wanting a daysman in 9:33?

topics.name: Zophar’s first speech
topics.description: Zophar accuses Job of empty talk, says God’s wisdom cannot be searched out, and promises that if Job puts away iniquity and prepares his heart he will be secure, while the eyes of the wicked fail.
evidence: What does Zophar say about searching out God (11:7-9) and about repentance (11:13-19)?
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} summarize Zophar’s first speech and compare it with Bildad’s?

topics.name: Job replies: God’s power, and whether a man will live again
topics.description: Job tells the friends he is not inferior to them, says wisdom and strength belong to God, who overturns counsellors and kings, declares he will trust God though he slay him, and in chapter 14 asks whether a man who dies shall live again.
evidence: Locate 13:15 and 14:14 and say what each expresses.
List things God does to rulers in 12:17-21.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how Job speaks of God’s power in chapter 12 and what he asks about death in 14:14?

topics.name: Eliphaz’s second speech: the wicked man’s torment
topics.description: Eliphaz rebukes Job for vain words and describes at length how the wicked man suffers pain and fear all his days.
evidence: Describe the picture of the wicked man in 15:20-35.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Eliphaz accuses Job of in chapter 15 and how he describes the wicked?

topics.name: Job: miserable comforters, and a witness on high
topics.description: Job calls his friends miserable comforters, says God has broken and worn him down, yet declares that his prayer is pure and that his witness is in heaven; his spirit is broken and the grave is ready for him.
evidence: Find the phrase Job uses for his friends in 16:2 and what he claims in 16:17-19.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Job describes his friends and what he says about a witness in chapters 16-17?

topics.name: Bildad’s second speech: the light of the wicked is put out
topics.description: Bildad describes the wicked man snared, terrified and rooted out of his tent so that his remembrance perishes from the earth.
evidence: List the images of the wicked man’s end in chapter 18.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list two of the pictures Bildad uses for the end of the wicked?

topics.name: I know that my redeemer lives
topics.description: Job says God has fenced his way and his family and friends have forsaken him, and he longs for his words to be written, declaring that he knows his redeemer lives and that in his flesh he shall see God.
evidence: Read 19:23-27 and state what Job says he knows and expects to see.
List the losses Job names in 19:13-20.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} read Job 19:25-27 and say what Job expects in spite of his condition?

topics.name: Zophar’s second speech: the triumph of the wicked is short
topics.description: Zophar says the triumphing of the wicked is short, that ill-gotten riches will be vomited up, and that God casts the fury of his wrath on him.
evidence: State Zophar’s claim in 20:5 and the portion he assigns the wicked in 20:29.
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Zophar’s claim about the wicked in chapter 20?

topics.name: Job: the wicked often prosper
topics.description: Job answers that the wicked live, grow old, see their children established and die at ease, and asks how often the lamp of the wicked is put out, rejecting his friends’ consolations as falsehood.
